If no such instructions are received, the depositary shall vote the Class&#160;D shares represented by ADSs in accordance with the recommendations YPF S.A.&#8217;s Board of Directors made to all holders of shares, unless the depositary is prohibited from doing so by any applicable provision of Argentine law. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;text-align:justify"><span style="font-style:italic">Shareholders and ADS holders outside of Argentina may face additional investment risks from currency exchange rate fluctuations in connection with their holding of our Class&#160;D shares or ADSs </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">We are organized under the laws of Argentina and future dividends on our Class&#160;D shares will be determined in the legal tender in Argentina, which is the Argentine peso. The Argentine peso has historically and recently fluctuated significantly against many major world currencies, including the U.S. dollar. A devaluation of the Argentine peso would likely adversely affect the U.S. dollar or other currency equivalent of any dividends paid on our Class&#160;D shares and could result in a decline in the value of our Class&#160;D shares and ADSs as measured in U.S. dollars. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;text-align:justify"><span style="font-style:italic">It may be difficult to effect service of process within the United States for civil liabilities against us or our directors, officers and controlling persons, and the enforcement in Argentina of any foreign judgment that results therein would be conditioned on compliance with the requirements of Argentine procedural law </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">We are organized under the laws of Argentina and our principal place of business (&#8220;domicilio social&#8221;) is in the City of Buenos Aires, Argentina. Our directors, officers and controlling persons reside outside the United States. In addition, a substantial portion of our assets and their assets is located outside the United States. As a result, it may be difficult for holders of our securities to effect service of process within the United States on such persons or to enforce judgments against us or them, including in any action based on civil liabilities under the U.S. federal securities laws. Under Argentine law, enforcement of foreign judgments would be recognized, provided that the requirements of Articles 517 through 519 of the Federal Code of Civil and Commercial Procedure are complied with, including the requirement that the judgment does not violate principles of public policy of Argentine law, as determined by an Argentine court, and provided that an Argentine court will not order the attachment of any property located in Argentina and determined by such court to be essential for the provision of public services. </p>

Our address is Macacha G&#252;emes 515, C1106BKK, Autonomous City of Buenos Aires, Argentina and our telephone number is <span style="white-space:nowrap">(54-11)</span> 5441-0000. Our legal name is YPF Sociedad An&#243;nima and we conduct our business under the commercial name &#8220;YPF&#8221;. YPF S.A. operates under the laws of Argentina, with <span style="white-space:nowrap">by-laws</span> registered on the Public Registry of Commerce of the Autonomous City of Buenos Aires. It is in force for a limited term of 100 years from June&#160;15, 1993, with the date of termination of its Memorandum of Incorporation being June&#160;15, 2093. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The SEC maintains an internet site that contains reports, proxy and information statements, and other information regarding issuers that file electronically with the SEC. All of the SEC filings made electronically by YPF S.A. are available to the public on the SEC website at www.sec.gov (commission file number <span style="white-space:nowrap">1-12102).</span> YPF S.A.&#8217;s website is www.ypf.com. The information contained on, or that can be accessed through, YPF S.A.&#8217;s website is not part of, and is not incorporated into, this annual report. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">We are Argentina&#8217;s leading energy company, operating a fully integrated oil and gas chain with leading market positions across the domestic upstream, downstream and gas and power segments. See &#8220;&#8212;Business organization&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">We have a <span style="white-space:nowrap">100-year</span> history. Beginning in the 1920s and until 1990, both the upstream and downstream segments of the Argentine oil and gas industry were effectively monopolies of the Argentine government. During this period, we and our predecessors were owned by the state, which controlled the exploration and production of oil and natural gas, as well as the refining of crude oil and marketing of refined petroleum products. In August 1989, Argentina enacted laws aimed at the deregulation of the economy and the privatization of Argentina&#8217;s state-owned companies, including us. Following the enactment of these laws, a series of presidential decrees were promulgated, which required us, among other things, to sell majority interests in our exploitation concessions in certain major productive areas and to undertake an internal management and operational restructuring program. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">In November 1992, the Argentine Congress enacted Law No.&#160;24,145 (&#8220;Privatization Law&#8221;), which established the procedures for our privatization. In accordance with the Privatization Law, in July 1993, we completed a worldwide offering of 160&#160;million Class&#160;D shares, representing approximately 45% of our outstanding capital stock, that had previously been owned by the Argentine government. Concurrently with the completion of such offering, the Argentine government transferred approximately 40&#160;million Class&#160;B shares to the Argentine provinces, which represented approximately 11% of our outstanding capital stock and made an offer to holders of pension bonds and certain other claims to exchange such bonds and other claims for approximately 46.1&#160;million Class&#160;B shares, representing approximately 13% of our outstanding capital stock. As a result of that offering and other transactions, the Argentine government&#8217;s ownership interest in our capital stock was reduced from 100% to approximately 20% by the end of 1993. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">In January 1999, Repsol YPF acquired 52,914,700 Class&#160;A shares (14.99% of our shares) which were converted to Class&#160;D shares. Additionally, on April&#160;30, 1999, Repsol YPF announced a tender offer to purchase all outstanding Class&#160;A, B, C and D shares (&#8220;Offer&#8221;). Pursuant to the Offer, in June 1999, Repsol YPF acquired an additional 82.47% of our outstanding capital stock. Repsol YPF acquired additional stakes in us from minority shareholders and other transactions in 1999 and 2000. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Repsol YPF owned approximately 99% of our capital stock from 2000 until 2008, when Petersen Energ&#237;a Inversora, S.A.U. and Petersen Energ&#237;a, S.A.U. (&#8220;Petersen&#8221;) acquired ADRs evidencing ADSs representing 15.46% of our capital stock. On May&#160;3, 2011, Petersen exercised an option to acquire, from Repsol YPF, ADRs evidencing ADSs representing 10.0% of our capital stock, and on May&#160;4, 2011, Repsol YPF acknowledged and accepted such exercise. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">On May&#160;3, 2012, the Argentine Congress passed Law No.&#160;26,741 (&#8220;Expropriation Law&#8221;), enacted on May&#160;4, 2012. On May&#160;7, 2012, the Expropriation Law was published in the Official Gazette, declaring a national public interest and a priority for Argentina in the achievement of self-sufficiency in the supply of hydrocarbons, as well as in the exploitation, industrialization, transportation and sale of hydrocarbons. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Article 3 of the Expropriation Law provides that the principles of the hydrocarbon policy of Argentina are the following: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Expropriation of shares held by Repsol YPF </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">For the purpose of ensuring the fulfillment of its objectives, the Expropriation Law provided for the expropriation of 51% of the share capital of YPF S.A. represented by an identical stake of Class&#160;D shares owned, directly or indirectly, by Repsol YPF and its controlled or controlling entities. According to the Expropriation Law, the shares subject to expropriation, which have been declared of public interest and were subsequently transferred to the Republic of Argentina, will be assigned as follows: 51% to the Argentine Republic and 49% to the Argentine provinces that compose the National Organization of Hydrocarbon Producing States. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">In addition, the Expropriation Law provided for the expropriation of 51% of the share capital of Repsol YPF GAS S.A. (&#8220;Repsol YPF GAS&#8221;) represented by 60% of the Class&#160;A shares of such company owned, directly or indirectly, by Repsol Butano S.A. and its controlled or controlling entities. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">As of the date of this annual report, the transfer of the shares subject to expropriation between the Argentine Executive Branch and the Argentine provinces that compose the National Organization of Hydrocarbon Producing States is still pending. According to Article 8 of the Expropriation Law, the distribution of the shares among the provinces that accept their transfer must be conducted in an equitable manner, considering their respective levels of hydrocarbon production and proved reserves. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">To ensure compliance with its objectives, the Expropriation Law provides that the Argentine Executive Branch, by itself or through an appointed public entity, shall exercise all the political rights associated with the shares subject to expropriation until the transfer of political and economic rights to the Argentine provinces that compose the National Organization of Hydrocarbon Producing States is completed. In addition, in accordance with Article 9 of the Expropriation Law, each of the Argentine provinces to which shares subject to expropriation are allocated must enter into a shareholder&#8217;s agreement with the federal government that will provide for the unified exercise of its rights as a shareholder. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Any future transfer of the shares subject to expropriation is prohibited without the permission of the Argentine Congress by a vote of <span style="white-space:nowrap">two-thirds</span> of its members. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">In accordance with Article 9 of the Expropriation Law, the appointment of YPF S.A. Directors representing the expropriated shares shall be made proportionately considering the holdings of the Argentine Republic and Argentine provinces, and one Director shall represent the employees of YPF S.A. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">In accordance with Article 16 of the Expropriation Law, the federal government and the provinces must exercise their rights pursuant to the following principles: (a)&#160;the strategic contribution of YPF S.A. to the achievement of the objectives set forth in the Expropriation Law; (b)&#160;the administration of YPF S.A. pursuant to the industry&#8217;s best practices and corporate governance, safeguarding shareholders&#8217; interests and generating value on their behalf; and (c)&#160;the professional management of YPF S.A. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">In accordance with Article 17 of the Expropriation Law, YPF S.A. will resort to internal and external sources of funding, strategic alliances, joint ventures, temporary business partnerships, and cooperation partnerships, whether public, private or mixed companies, domestic and foreign. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">You can find a copy of an English translation of the Expropriation Law in the report on Form <span style="white-space:nowrap">6-K</span> furnished by YPF S.A. to the SEC on May&#160;9, 2012. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">In addition, on February&#160;25, 2014, the Republic of Argentina and Repsol reached an agreement (&#8220;Repsol Agreement&#8221;) in relation to compensation for the expropriation of 200,589,525 of YPF S.A.&#8217;s Class&#160;D shares pursuant to the Expropriation Law Under the Repsol Agreement, Repsol accepted US$ 5.0&#160;billion in sovereign bonds from the Republic of Argentina and withdrew judicial and arbitral claims it had filed, including claims against YPF S.A., and waived additional claims. YPF S.A. and Repsol also executed a separate agreement (&#8220;Repsol Arrangement&#8221;) on February&#160;27, 2014, pursuant to which YPF S.A. and Repsol each withdrew, subject to certain exclusions, all present and future actions and/or claims based on causes occurring prior to the date of execution of the Repsol Arrangement arising from the expropriation of the YPF S.A. shares owned by Repsol pursuant to the Expropriation Law, including the intervention of YPF S.A. and the temporary occupation for public purposes of 51% of Repsol&#180;s capital stock in YPF S.A. Repsol and YPF S.A. agreed to withdraw reciprocal actions and claims with respect to third parties and/or pursued by them and to grant a series of mutual indemnities, which at the time were subject to certain conditions precedent. The Repsol Arrangement entered into force the day after Repsol notified YPF S.A. that the Repsol Agreement had entered into force. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The Repsol Agreement was ratified on March&#160;28, 2014, at a Repsol general shareholders&#8217; meeting and approved by the Argentine Congress by Law No.&#160;26,932 enacted by Decree No.&#160;600/2014. On May&#160;8, 2014, YPF S.A. was notified of the entry into force of the Repsol Agreement, and as a result the Republic of Argentina is definitively the owner of 51% of the capital stock of each of YPF S.A. and YPF GAS S.A. (formerly, Repsol YPF GAS). </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">See &#8220;Item 7. Major shareholders and related party transactions&#8221; for details on our current major shareholders. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Legal nature of YPF S.A. </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">According to the Expropriation Law, YPF S.A. is and will continue to operate as a publicly traded corporation pursuant to Chapter II, Section V of the Argentine General Corporations Law and its corresponding regulations, and neither is nor will be subject to any legislation or regulation applicable to the management or control of companies or entities owned by the federal government or provincial governments. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">See &#8220;Item 7. <div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold" id="rom804823_14"><span style="font-style:italic">Overview </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Argentina is the largest producer of natural gas and the fourth largest producer of crude oil and condensate in Central and South America, according to the 2023 edition of the Energy Institute Statistical Review of World Energy, published in June 2023. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">YPF operates mainly in Argentina (see &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk factors&#8212;Risks relating to Argentina&#8212;Our business is largely dependent upon economic conditions in Argentina&#8221;) and our revenues are primarily derived from the sales of fuels (gasoline and diesel) and natural gas in the Argentine domestic market, which together represented 69.3% of total revenues in 2023. Additionally, in 2023, our main expenditures are related to investments and operating costs in conventional fields aiming to compensate or reduce their natural decline, in unconventional fields with the objective of growing production and reserves, and in the maintenance and/or investment in our downstream business, among others, as well as royalties and taxes related to our operations and the payment of interests related to our financial debt. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold" id="rom804823_15"><span style="font-style:italic">Business strategy </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Our strategy has evolved over the last few years to prioritize the monetization of our vast unconventional hydrocarbon resources. Over the last 10 years, we have invested significantly in the Vaca Muerta formation together with our international and local partners, gaining experience, incorporating technology and adapting processes to become competitive on a global scale. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Having achieved competitive efficiency levels on both capital and operating expenditures, we now have the opportunity to accelerate the development of our shale resources. This has become even more relevant in the current geopolitical context in which the world demands affordable, reliable and sustainable energy, increasing the attractiveness of becoming a net exporter of crude oil and, in the medium term, capitalizing the opportunity to become a relevant LNG exporter. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Therefore, we will continue to focus our efforts on our most profitable business, the Vaca Muerta formation, given its level of recoverable resources. Furthermore, we expect to actively manage our portfolio with a capital allocation discipline, reallocating resources from other less profitable businesses. In that sense, we are targeting a significant reduction of our exposure to conventional mature fields. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">While accelerating the growth potential of our shale resources, we also remain focused on maintaining high standards with regards to the health and safety of our people and the communities we work in, reducing our carbon footprint, and remaining focused on securing further efficiencies in all of our operations, including refining/processing of crude oil and natural gas and the distribution and marketing of hydrocarbon and derivative products, which position us as the leading integrated energy company in Argentina. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">We intend to strengthen our competitiveness and timely adaptation to the trends that are taking place in the global energy space and that would have a decisive impact in the coming decades, such as decarbonization and electrification, as well as those that aim to increase the efficiency of hydrocarbons production and processing. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Our strategic pillars are: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">

<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td align="left" style="vertical-align:top"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:9pt;text-align:justify">Discipline in the allocation of capital, focused on the development of our unconventional hydrocarbon acreage with competitive advantages, generating value in a sustainable way. </p></td></tr></table>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">

In this regard, ongoing improvement in well construction efficiency is a fundamental factor in the development of our unconventional assets. </p></td></tr></table>

(&#8220;YPF EE&#8221;), as part of our commitment to sustainability. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">During 2023, we continued to focus on implementing our corporate sustainability policy and our commitment to climate change-related actions. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The investment plan related to our strategy requires the reinvestment of our earnings, our association with strategic partners and the use of debt financing at levels we consider prudent for companies in our industry. The financial viability of these investments and hydrocarbon recovery efforts will depend on numerous factors that YPF does not control or influence, such as the prevailing economic and regulatory conditions in Argentina, the ability to obtain financing in satisfactory amounts at competitive costs, among others. See &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk factors&#8212;Risks relating to Argentina&#8221;, &#8220;Item 3. Furthermore, we continue to manage our portfolio actively, prioritizing the divestment of matured conventional assets and including the evaluation of new joint ventures to develop our unconventional acreage. </p>

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold" id="rom804823_16"><span style="font-style:italic">Business organization </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">For a chart illustrating our organizational structure, including our principal subsidiaries see Note 1 to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Our operations, properties and clients are mainly located in Argentina. However, we also hold participating interests in exploratory areas in Bolivia and sell jet fuel, natural gas, lubricants and derivatives in Chile and lubricants and derivatives in Brazil. As of December 31, 2023, we conducted our business according to the following organization: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:2%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top" align="left"><span style="font-weight:bold">(i)</span></td>
<td align="left" style="vertical-align:top"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;text-align:justify">Upstream business segment </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The Upstream business segment performs all activities related to the exploration and exploitation and production of crude oil, natural gas and frac sand for well drilling. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Its revenues are largely derived from: (i)&#160;the sale of the crude oil produced to the Downstream business segment; and (ii)&#160;the sale of the natural gas produced and the sale of the natural gas retained in plant to the Gas and Power business segment. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">This segment incurs all costs related to the activities mentioned above. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">On January&#160;1, 2023, certain assets related to the exploration, exploitation and production of frac sand for well drilling, which were formerly included in Central Administration and Others, were assigned to the Upstream business segment. </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:2%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top" align="left"><span style="font-weight:bold">(ii)</span></td>
<td align="left" style="vertical-align:top"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;text-align:justify">Downstream business segment </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The Downstream business segment performs activities relating to: (i)&#160;crude oil refining and petrochemical production; (ii)&#160;logistics related to the transportation of crude oil to refineries and the transportation and distribution of refined and petrochemical products to be marketed at the different sales channels; (iii)&#160;commercialization of crude oil and refined and petrochemical products obtained from such processes; and (iv)&#160;commercialization of specialties for the agribusiness industry and of grains and their <span style="white-space:nowrap">by-products.</span> </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Its revenues are derived primarily from the sale of crude oil, refined and petrochemical products, specialties for the agribusiness industry and grains and their <span style="white-space:nowrap">by-products.</span> These operations are performed through the businesses of B2C (Retail), B2B (Industries, Transportation, Aviation, Agri, Lubricants and Specialties), LPG, Chemicals, International Trade and Transportation and Sales to Companies. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">This segment incurs all costs related to the activities mentioned above, including the purchase of crude oil from the Upstream business segment and third parties and the purchase of gasoline, propane and butane and natural gas from the Gas and Power business segment to be consumed in the refineries and petrochemical industrial complexes. </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:2%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top" align="left"><span style="font-weight:bold">(iii)</span></td>
<td align="left" style="vertical-align:top"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;text-align:justify">Gas and Power business segment </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The Gas and Power business segment performs activities related to: (i)&#160;natural gas transportation to third parties and the Downstream business segment, and its commercialization; (ii)&#160;commercial and technical operation of the LNG regasification terminals in Escobar and Bah&#237;a Blanca, by hiring regasification vessels; (iii)&#160;transportation, conditioning and processing of natural gas retained in plant for the separation and fractionation of gasoline, propane and butane; (iv)&#160;distribution of natural gas through our subsidiary Metrogas S.A. (&#8220;Metrogas&#8221;); and (v)&#160;the storage of the natural gas produced. Also, through our investments in associates and joint ventures, it undertakes activities related to: (i)&#160;separation of NGLs and their fractionation, storage and transportation for the production of ethane, propane, butane and gasoline; (ii)&#160;generation of conventional thermal electric power and renewable energy; and (iii)&#160;production, storage, distribution and sale of fertilizers. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Its revenues are largely derived from the commercialization of natural gas as producers to third parties and the Downstream business segment, the distribution of natural gas through our subsidiary Metrogas, the sale of gasoline, propane and butane to the Downstream business segment and the provision of LNG regasification services. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">This segment incurs all costs related to the activities mentioned above, including the purchase of natural gas and natural gas retained in plant from the Upstream business segment. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">On January&#160;1, 2023, certain assets related to the production, storage, distribution and sale of fertilizers through the Profertil S.A. (&#8220;Profertil&#8221;) joint venture, which were formerly included in the Downstream business segment, were assigned to the Gas and Power business segment. </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

Operating and financial review and prospects&#8212;Liquidity and capital resources&#8212;Capital investments, expenditures and divestitures&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold" id="rom804823_17"><span style="font-style:italic">Upstream </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">YPF&#8217;s Upstream business segment seeks to add value to the Company by optimizing the use of deployed capital, achieving levels of operational excellence, thus generating new development opportunities, while delivering profitable growth driven by the increasing incorporation of unconventional projects to its activities where well construction efficiency is a fundamental factor. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The plan of promotion for natural gas production in Argentina, Plan GasAr 2020-2024, launched in November 2020, gave to the Company an opportunity to monetize natural gas reservoirs, ensuring to supply the demand for four years at a price that allows for the development of our natural gas projects in certain basins. In this sense, Plan GasAr 2023-2028, launched in November 2022, allowed the Company to extend this opportunity by ensuring to supply the natural gas demand over the next five years. For further information see &#8220;&#8212;Gas and Power&#8212;Natural gas operations&#8221; and Note 35.d.1) to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center">21 </p>

<h5><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></h5>


<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">During 2023, we continued actively managing our portfolio. As of December&#160;31, 2023, we held interests in 114 oil and gas fields in Argentina. According to the Secretariat of Energy (&#8220;SE&#8221;) in 2023, these assets accounted for 38.2% of the Argentina&#8217;s total production of crude oil, excluding NGLs, and 32.7% of its total natural gas production, including NGLs. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">During 2023, YPF hydrocarbon production increased by 2.0% compared to 2022. Crude oil daily production increased by 7.4%, NGLs daily production increased by 3.2%, offset by a 3.3% decrease in natural gas daily production comparing to 2022. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Our unconventional production continues to increase strongly during 2023. Crude oil daily production increased by 26.4%, NGLs daily production increased by 13.9% and natural gas daily production increased by 2.3% comparing to 2022. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">On February&#160;29, 2024 YPF&#8217;s Board of Directors resolved the disposal of certain groups of assets, mainly mature fields from Golfo San Jorge, Neuquina, Cuyana and Austral basins. This disposal of assets involves 55 blocks and is consistent with the Company&#8217;s new management plans which considers that the rationalization of the conventional upstream portfolio is one of the drivers on which the YPF&#8217;s strategy is based, with focus on activities and investments in unconventional fields. See &#8220;&#8212;Business strategy&#8221;, &#8220;&#8212;Oil and gas reserves&#8221;, &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk Factors&#8212;Risks relating to Argentina&#8212;Our business is largely dependent upon economic conditions in Argentina&#8221;, &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk Factors&#8212;Risks relating to our business&#8212;Our business depends on complex, long-term and capital-intensive projects&#8221; and &#8220;Item 5. Operating and financial review and prospects&#8212;Liquidity and capital resources&#8212;Capital investments, expenditures and divestitures&#8221;. The carrying amount of these assets as of December 31, 2023 may be adjusted in future periods depending on the results of the disposition process conducted by YPF and the financial consideration to be agreed with third parties for such assets and, in addition, the closing of such dispositions will be subject to the fulfillment of customary closing conditions, including applicable regulatory approvals. See Note 8 and 38 to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Acreage </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Our production is concentrated in the Neuquina, Golfo San Jorge, Cuyana, Noroeste and Austral basins in Argentina: </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The following table sets forth information regarding our developed and undeveloped acreage by geographic area: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

In Colombia, YPF notified the Colombian National Hydrocarbons Agency (Agencia Nacional de Hidrocarburos or &#8220;ANH&#8221;) of the decision to relinquish the COR 12 and COR 33 blocks; and in July 2022, the ANH began an administrative proceeding claiming the exploration commitments were not performed or paid, and as of the date of this annual report the Company has presented its defenses in the administrative process and the ANH is considering the evidence offered. In Bolivia, YPF&#8217;s net undeveloped surface acreage totaled 91,553 acres, and in Uruguay YPF&#180;s net undeveloped surface acreage totaled 4,160,266 acres. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The net exploratory undeveloped acreage in Argentina under the first or second exploration periods, which mature in 2024 and in the period 2025-2027, respectively, is 5,007 km<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">2</sup> (24.6%) and 15,339 km<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">2 </sup>(75.4%), respectively, of our 20,346 km<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">2</sup> net exploratory undeveloped acreage as of December&#160;31, 2023. The net exploratory undeveloped acreage in the Rest of South America is 11,172 km<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">2</sup>, which mature mainly in the period 2025-2027. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The extension of the expiring acreage that the Company would be required to surrender to the relevant Province will depend on our decision to extend our exploration permit in a given area, provided that the requirements of the Argentine Hydrocarbons Law have been met, including the satisfaction of our obligations under the exploration permit relating to those areas. Therefore, the areas to be relinquished usually consist of acreage where drilling has not been successful and are considered <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-core</span> lease acreage. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">As of December&#160;31, 2023, we do not have any material undeveloped acreage related to our exploitation concessions expiring in the near term. </p>

<hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%"/>
<h5><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></h5>


<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Exploration&#160;&amp; Development activity </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold">Argentina </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Exploration activities </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">YPF&#8217;s <span style="font-weight:bold">onshore exploration portfolio</span> is mainly focused on high-impact projects such as <span style="font-weight:bold">Palermo Aike</span>, believed to be the second shale formation located in the Austral basin behind the Vaca Muerta formation in terms of potential, and <span style="font-weight:bold">Vaca Muerta</span>. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Regarding the <span style="font-weight:bold">Palermo Aike</span> project, in May 2023 YPF signed an agreement with Compa&#241;&#237;a General de Combustibles S.A. (&#8220;CGC&#8221;) to drill the first horizontal well to evaluate the Palermo Aike formation in the El Cerrito block. As of December&#160;31, 2023, this well is being drilled while completion and testing are expected to occur during 2024. Also, in June 2023, the Santa Cruz Province granted exploration permits to YPF for strengthening exploration in the Palermo Aike formation in the La Azucena and El Campamento Este blocks. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">In the Vaca Muerta formation, 2 horizontal wells were drilled during 2023, one in the <span style="white-space:nowrap">CN-VII</span> block where we have an exploration permit and the other one in the Paso de las Bardas Norte exploitation concession. These wells were drilled as a result of the significant geochemical indexes (from cores and cuttings). As of December&#160;31, 2023, both wells are being on completion while the testing is expected to occur during 2024. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">YPF&#180;s<span style="font-weight:bold"> offshore exploration portfolio</span> is formed by the <span style="white-space:nowrap">CAN-100,</span> <span style="white-space:nowrap">CAN-102</span> and CAN-114 blocks located in the North Argentina basin, and the <span style="white-space:nowrap">MLO-123</span> block located in the West Malvinas basin, which are in their first exploration period and are being developed jointly with our partners Equinor, Shell and Total Austral. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">In March 2023, a deferral until November 2025 for the first exploratory period in the <span style="white-space:nowrap">CAN-102</span> block was granted by the Argentine National government. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">In the <span style="white-space:nowrap">CAN-100</span> block, an exploration permit located at 300 km from the Mar del Plata City in the Buenos Aires Province, the first deepwater well in Argentina <span style="white-space:nowrap">(Argerich.x-1)</span> is planned to be drilled during the second quarter of 2024. To this end, during 2023, after a public hearing, all environmental permits were approved. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Seismic activities </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">During 2023, a <span style="white-space:nowrap">3-D</span> seismic study took place in <span style="white-space:nowrap">CAN-114,</span> an offshore <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-operated</span> block located in the North basin in Argentina, covering 1,862 km, which represents 40% of the activity completed by December&#160;31, 2023. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Development activities </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Unconventional activities </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">During 2023 the production from our unconventional activities was 183.1 mboe/d (YPF net from operated areas), representing 36% of YPF&#180;s total production (YPF net from operated and <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-operated</span> areas). In 2023, YPF, jointly with its partners, continued with its growth plan with more than US$ 1,873&#160;million invested (YPF net from operated areas), 151 wells were put into production and more than 6,000 frac stages were carried out in blocks operated by YPF. Considering the above, YPF believes that it will continue to lead the unconventional activities development in Argentina. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">In 2023, YPF&#8217;s was highly active in its drilling operations at the <span style="font-weight:bold">Core Hub blocks</span> (<span style="font-weight:bold">Loma Campana</span>, <span style="font-weight:bold">La Amarga Chica</span>, <span style="font-weight:bold">Bandurria Sur</span> and <span style="font-weight:bold">Aguada del Cha&#241;ar</span>), with 11 operative rigs in these oil blocks. Operational efficiencies continued to break records, with a well reaching 2,518 meters (8,261 feet) of lateral length in 12 days (5,640 meters of total length). </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The average lateral length drilled in the Core Hub blocks was 2,781 meters (9,125 feet). The longest well drilled during 2023 reached 4,343 meters (14,249 feet) of lateral length. During 2023, 2 wells were put into production at a new landing level. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The activity is focused on the most profitable and proven intervals while approximately 6% of it is directed to appraisal wells. Promising results observed during 2023 in a well pad drilled westwards of the developed area in the <span style="font-weight:bold">Bandurria Sur</span> block in 2022 allowed us to extend the current development towards the center of the block. In the northern area of the <span style="font-weight:bold">Aguada del Cha&#241;ar</span> block, an appraisal well pad was drilled and was in process of being fractured as of December&#160;31, 2023. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">During 2023 production performance was according to expectations throughout the Core Hub blocks. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Even though drilling activity in the <span style="font-weight:bold">Hub Gas blocks</span> (<span style="font-weight:bold">Aguada de la Arena</span> and <span style="font-weight:bold">Rinc&#243;n del Mangrullo</span>, main natural gas blocks operated by YPF) during 2023 was similar compared to 2022, it was lower than the activity planned in order to adjust it to a lower domestic natural gas demand, 3 pads (12 wells) were drilled in the <span style="font-weight:bold">Aguada de la Arena</span> block and 3 pads (11 wells) were drilled in the <span style="font-weight:bold">Rinc&#243;n del Mangrullo</span> block, which is a delineation objective that will test productivity in the southern area of the block potentially increasing its resources. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">In the southern area of the Neuquina basin regarding the <span style="font-weight:bold">Delineation block</span>, <span style="font-weight:bold">Sur de los Lagos</span>, within the boundaries of the Loma La Lata - Sierra Barrosa conventional concession, 2 horizontal oil wells finished their evaluation test during 2023. In terms of productivity, 1 well is below expectations and 1 well is above expectations. </p>

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">During 2023, in order to fulfill the investment commitments with the Neuqu&#233;n Province in the southwest area of the Neuquina basin (which will allow us the extension of the exploration permit in the <span style="font-weight:bold">Las Tacanas</span> block) 2 wells were drilled and fractured, 1 vertical well to gather information in the area of interest and a horizontal side-track in the lower level of the Vaca Muerta formation, and 1 horizontal well in an upper level of the Vaca Muerta formation. </p> <p style="margin-top:5pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">With the objective of understanding the productivity of the Vaca Muerta formation in various positions of the <span style="font-weight:bold">Loma Amarilla Sur</span> block, 4 wells drilled as part of the delineation pilot phase, were put into production in August 2023 (1 vertical oil well to gather information in the sequences of interest and 4 horizontal oil wells targeting two landing zones). As of December&#160;31, 2023, evaluation tests were ongoing. </p> <p style="margin-top:5pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The activity in the <span style="font-weight:bold">Gas Window Delineation</span>, in the western area of the Neuquina basin, was resumed during 2023 with the drilling of 2 horizontal wells, with 1 well drilled in the <span style="font-weight:bold">Cerro Las Minas</span> block and 1 well being drilled in the <span style="font-weight:bold">Loma del Molle</span> block. This activity is part of an investment commitment with the Neuqu&#233;n Province to extend the exploration permits of both blocks, that will allow us to have a better understanding on the Vaca Muerta formation&#180;s potential productivity in these blocks. </p> <p style="margin-top:5pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Conventional activities </span></p> <p style="margin-top:5pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold">Sur Region </p> <p style="margin-top:5pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">During 2023, the <span style="font-weight:bold">Sur Region</span>&#180;s production was 93.4 mboe/d (YPF net from operated areas), representing 18% of YPF&#8217;s total production (YPF net from operated and <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-operated</span> areas). </p> <p style="margin-top:5pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">During 2023, activity in the Sur Region involved a total investment (YPF net from operated areas) of US$ 955&#160;million. </p> <p style="margin-top:5pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Milestones for the Sur Region, during 2023, were mainly driven by the development of polymer injection activities performed in the <span style="font-weight:bold">El Tr&#233;bol</span> and <span style="font-weight:bold">Escalante</span> blocks where oil response to the polymer injection pilot carried out in 2022 outperformed and exceeded the forecasts. In the <span style="font-weight:bold">Manantiales Behr</span> block, a secondary polymer injection pilot (without previous conventional waterflooding) continues to boost oil production, exceeding expectations by achieving new production highs in 2023 compared to the Grimbeek Norte block&#180;s results in 2022; based on these results, we are analyzing moving towards a polymer injection massification in this block. </p> <p style="margin-top:5pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Also, the implementation of horizontal tight wells drillings, contributed to the Sur Region productivity results. Based on the positive results accomplished with the first horizontal tight oil well drilled in 2022, targeting the <span style="white-space:nowrap">D-129</span> formation in the <span style="font-weight:bold">Ca&#241;ad&#243;n Le&#243;n</span> and <span style="font-weight:bold">Meseta Espinosa</span> blocks, 3 horizontal tight oil wells were drilled and completed during 2023 with results according to expectations. All of them with an extension of 1,500 meters of horizontal branch and 18 stages of hydraulic stimulation, which represents a significant milestone considering the increase of 500 meters and 6 stages of hydraulic stimulations compared to 2022, allowing a decrease in development costs. </p> <p style="margin-top:5pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold">Oeste Region </p> <p style="margin-top:5pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">During 2023, the <span style="font-weight:bold">Oeste Region</span>&#180;s production was 137.5 mboe/d (YPF net from operated areas), representing 27% of YPF&#180;s total production (YPF net from operated and <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-operated</span> areas). </p> <p style="margin-top:5pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">During 2023, the activity in the Oeste Region involved a total investment (YPF net from operated areas) of US$ 384&#160;million. </p> <p style="margin-top:5pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The activity in the Oeste Region during 2023 was focused in the <span style="font-weight:bold">Rio Neuqu&#233;n</span> block where the only Upstream conventional project related to natural gas production takes place. This project is part of the Plan GasAr 2020-2024 and Plan GasAr 2023-2028, aimed at boosting natural gas production in Argentina by granting competitive prices, with the drilling of 18 wells (16 tight gas wells and 2 service wells). During 2023, 11 wells were put into production with results according to expectations, reaching<span style="font-weight:bold"> </span>its plateau as a result of a sustain drilling campaign started back in 2021. In the <span style="font-weight:bold">Chachahuen Sur</span> block<span style="font-weight:bold">,</span> we are executing our main project of tertiary activity in the Neuquina basin, with the commissioning during 2023 of 3 polymer plants with results according to expectations. Also, a 50% royalty reduction was granted for this block through Administrative Decision No.&#160;01/2024 of the Mendoza Province as result of the fulfillment of the investment commitments in the project. </p> <p style="margin-top:5pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="text-decoration:underline"><span style="white-space:nowrap">Non-operated</span> activities </span></p> <p style="margin-top:5pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">During 2023, the production of the <span style="font-weight:bold"><span style="white-space:nowrap">non-operated</span> areas</span> was 99.6 mboe/d (YPF net from <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-operated</span> areas), representing 19% of YPF&#180;s total production (YPF net from operated and <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-operated</span> areas). </p> <p style="margin-top:5pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">During 2023, the <span style="font-weight:bold">conventional activities </span>in the <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-operated</span> areas involved a total investment (YPF net from <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-operated</span> areas) of US$ 13&#160;million in drilling and completion and US$ 38&#160;million in production facilities and other capital expenditures. During 2023, the Company signed an agreement with the Salta Province which extended 10 years from the expiration date of their original terms in the <span style="font-weight:bold">Aguarag&#252;e</span> block. This agreement granted a 2% royalty reduction. </p> <p style="margin-top:5pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">During 2023, the <span style="font-weight:bold">unconventional activities</span> in the <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-operated</span> areas in the Neuquina basin involved a total investment (YPF net from <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-operated</span> areas) of US$ 361&#160;million in drilling and completion and US$ 315&#160;million in production facilities and other capital expenditures. The main investments were concentrated in shale oil developments in the <span style="font-weight:bold">Lindero Atravesado</span> and <span style="font-weight:bold">Bajada de A&#241;elo</span> blocks and in shale gas in the <span style="font-weight:bold">La Calera</span> and <span style="font-weight:bold">Aguada Pichana Oeste</span> blocks. During 2023, in the <span style="font-weight:bold">La Calera</span> block we finished the construction of an oil pipeline, which connects this block with the Loma Campana block, and we started the construction of the Central Production Facility project that is expected to be finished in the second quarter of 2024 and will allow a gas treatment capacity of 10 mmcm/d and 4,800 cm/d of condensate. </p> <p style="margin-top:5pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The Aguarag&#252;e, La Calera and Aguada Pichana Oeste blocks are part of the Plan GasAr 2020-2024 and Plan GasAr 2023-2028 that aims to boost natural gas production in Argentina by granting competitive prices. </p>

<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold">Rest of South America </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold"><span style="font-style:italic">Exploration activities </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">In December 2023, the Company successfully bid on an offshore area in <span style="font-weight:bold">Uruguay</span>, obtaining an exploration permit for the <span style="white-space:nowrap">OFF-5</span> block, which increased the Company&#8217;s international offshore acreage in 16,836 km<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">2</sup>. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The Charagua block, an onshore area in <span style="font-weight:bold">Bolivia</span>, entered into its third exploratory phase in November 2023 after obtaining the drilling environmental permit in July 2023. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The COR 12 and COR 33 blocks are located in the Cordillera Oriental basin in <span style="font-weight:bold">Colombia</span>, which we operate pursuant to the authorization by the ANH. Our working interest is 60% in the COR 12 block and 55% in the COR 33 block. The combined net area of these blocks is 700 km<sup style="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">2</sup>. In 2016, together with our partners, we informed to the ANH of our decision to relinquish both blocks. In July 2022, the ANH began an administrative proceeding claiming the exploration commitments were not performed or paid. As of the date of this annual report, the Company presented its defenses in the administrative process and the ANH is considering the evidence offered. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Oil and gas reserves </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Proved oil and gas reserves are those quantities of oil and gas which, by analysis of geoscience and engineering data, can be estimated with reasonable certainty to be economically producible (from a given date forward, from known reservoirs, and under existing economic conditions, operating methods and government regulations) prior to the time at which contracts providing the right to operate expire, unless evidence indicates that renewal is reasonably certain, regardless of whether deterministic or probabilistic methods are used for the estimation. The project to extract the hydrocarbons must have commenced or the operator must be reasonably certain that it will commence the project within reasonable time. In some cases, substantial investments in new wells and related facilities may be required to recover proved reserves. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Information on net proved reserves as of December&#160;31, 2023, 2022 and 2021 was calculated in accordance with the SEC rules and FASB ASC 932 rules. Accordingly, crude oil prices used to determine reserves were calculated for crude oils of different quality produced by the Company. Consequently, to calculate our net proved reserves as of December&#160;31, 2023, the Company considered, according to the SEC rules and FASB ASC 932 rules, the unweighted average realized price of crude oils for each month within the <span style="white-space:nowrap">12-month</span> period ended December&#160;31, 2023, which refers to the domestic crude oil prices adjusted by each different quality produced by the Company. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The reported reserves contained in this annual report include only our proved reserves and do not include probable reserves or possible reserves. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Additionally, since there are no benchmark market natural gas prices available in Argentina, the Company considered the <span style="white-space:nowrap">12-month</span> period average ended December&#160;31, 2023 of domestic market realized prices according to the SEC rules and FASB ASC 932 rules, and the prices of contracts awarded to YPF under the Plan GasAr 2020-2024 and the Plan GasAr 2023-2028 for certain areas in certain basins, which will be in effect until their corresponding termination dates. See Note 35.d.1) to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Notwithstanding the foregoing, commodity prices have fluctuated significantly in recent years. See &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk factors&#8212;Risks relating to our business&#8212;Our reserves and production may decline&#8221; and &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk factors&#8212;Risks relating to our business&#8212;Our oil and natural gas reserves are estimates&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Net reserves are defined as that portion of the gross reserves attributable to the interest of the Company after deducting interests owned by third parties. In determining net reserves, the Company excludes from its reported reserves royalties due to others, whether payable in cash or in kind, where the royalty owner has a direct interest in the underlying production and is able to make lifting and sales arrangements independently. By contrast, to the extent that royalty payments required to be made to a third-party, whether payable in cash or in kind, are a financial obligation, or are substantially equivalent to a production or severance tax, the related reserves are not excluded from the reported reserves despite the fact that such payments are referred to as royalties under local regulations. The same methodology is followed in reporting our production amounts. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Natural gas reserves exclude the gaseous equivalent of liquids expected to be removed from the natural gas on concessions and leases, at field facilities and at natural gas processing plants. These liquids are included in net proved reserves of NGLs. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Technology used in establishing proved reserves additions </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">YPF&#8217;s estimated proved reserves as of December&#160;31, 2023 are based on estimates generated through the integration of available and appropriate data, utilizing well-established technologies that have been demonstrated in the field to yield repeatable and consistent results. Data used in these integrated assessments include information obtained directly from the subsurface via wellbore, such as well logs, reservoir core samples, fluid samples, static and dynamic pressure information, production test data, and surveillance and performance information. The data utilized also include subsurface information obtained through indirect measurements, including high quality <span style="white-space:nowrap">2-D</span> and <span style="white-space:nowrap">3-D</span> seismic data, calibrated with available well control. Where applicable, geological outcrops information was also utilized. The tools used to interpret and integrate all this data included both proprietary and commercial software for reservoir modeling, simulation and data analysis. In some circumstances, where appropriate analog reservoir models are available, reservoir parameters from these analog models were used to increase the reliability of our reserves estimates. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">For further information on the estimation process of our proved reserves, see &#8220;&#8212;Internal controls on reserves and reserves audits&#8221;. </p>

<td align="left" style="vertical-align:top"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:8pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Proved crude oil and NGLs reserves include an estimated 72 mmbbl of crude oil and 10 mmbbl of NGLs with respect to royalty payments which, as described above, are a financial obligation or are substantially equivalent to a production or similar tax. Proved natural gas reserves include an estimated 292 bcf with respect to such payments. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">On February&#160;29, 2024 YPF&#8217;s Board of Directors resolved the disposal of certain groups of mature assets. This optimization and divestment plan involves 55 blocks from Golfo San Jorge, Neuquina, Cuyana, and Austral basins. The total proved reserves associated with these areas, which were included in the total proved reserves as of December&#160;31, 2023, account for approximately 85 mmboe mainly related to conventional crude oil assets. See Notes 8 and 38 to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements and &#8220; &#8212;Business strategy&#8221;, &#8220; &#8212;Upstream&#8221;, &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk Factors&#8212;Risks relating to Argentina&#8212;Our business is largely dependent upon economic conditions in Argentina&#8221;, &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk Factors&#8212;Risks relating to our business&#8212;Our business depends on complex, long-term and capital-intensive projects&#8221; and &#8220;Item 5. Operating and financial review and prospects&#8212;Liquidity and capital resources&#8212;Capital investments, expenditures and divestitures&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">For information regarding changes in our estimated net proved reserves for the year ended December&#160;31, 2023, 2022 and 2021 see &#8220;Supplemental information on oil and gas producing activities (unaudited)&#8221; beginning on page <span style="white-space:nowrap">S-1</span> of this annual report. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Reserves replacement ratio </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The reserves replacement ratio is the net amount of added proved reserves divided by the volumes produced in any given period. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">As of December&#160;31, 2023, the reserves replacement ratio was 39% as a result of an addition of 72 mmboe of net proved reserves (41 mmboe of liquids, and 31 mmboe of natural gas), and considering 187 mmboe produced during the year and the amount of proved reserves at the beginning of 2023. There were no reserves volumes additions related to sales and acquisitions during 2023. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">For additional information regarding changes in proved reserves and the reliability of proved reserves estimates, see &#8220;Supplemental information on oil and gas producing activities (unaudited)&#8221;, &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk factors&#8212;Risks relating to our business&#8212;Our reserves and production may decline&#8221; and &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk factors&#8212;Risks relating to our business&#8212;Our oil and natural gas reserves are estimates&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The table below sets forth, for each of the periods indicated, information regarding reserves replacement ratio: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p><div>

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The following paragraphs explain in further detail the most significant changes in our net proved undeveloped reserves for the year ended December&#160;31, 2023. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Changes in our net proved undeveloped reserves during 2023 </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">YPF had an estimated volume of net proved undeveloped reserves of 473 mmboe as of December&#160;31, 2023, which represented 44% of the 1,072 mmboe total net proved reserves as of such date. As of December&#160;31, 2022, the estimated net proved undeveloped reserves were 597 mmboe (50% of the 1,187 mmboe total net proved reserves as of such date). </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The 21% decrease in net proved undeveloped reserves in 2023, is mainly attributable to: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:3%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top" align="left">&#9679;</td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td align="left" style="vertical-align:top"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:9pt;text-align:justify">Field development projects related to proved undeveloped reserves, which allowed to transfer 132 mmboe to proved developed reserves. The main contributions are related to development wells (129 mmboe) mainly in the Neuquina basin, and improved recovery projects and workovers (3 mmboe) mainly in the Golfo San Jorge and Neuquina basins. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">

<td align="left" style="vertical-align:top"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:9pt;text-align:justify">Extensions and discoveries, which added 105 mmboe (192 bcf of natural gas, 7 mmbbl of NGLs and 64 mmbbl of crude oil) of proved undeveloped reserves mainly from unconventional oil and gas projects of the Vaca Muerta formation at the Neuquina basin in the following areas: </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:6%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">- Crude oil: Loma La Lata Norte, Bandurria Sur and La Amarga Chica. </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:6%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">- Natural gas: La Calera and Aguada Pichana Oeste. </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<td align="left" style="vertical-align:top"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:9pt;text-align:justify">Changes in some reserves development projects strategy and drilling schedules, that resulted in a deduction of 68 mmboe (41 mmboe of liquids and 148 bcf of natural gas). </p></td></tr></table> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td align="left" style="vertical-align:top"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:9pt;text-align:justify">Changes in oil and gas prices and its impact in economics, that resulted in a reduction of 37 mmboe of proved undeveloped reserves. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">During 2023, YPF&#8217;s total capital expenditures to continue the development of reserves was US$ 2,473&#160;million, of which US$ 1,929&#160;million was allocated to projects related to proved undeveloped reserves. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">As of December&#160;31, 2023, we did not have material amounts of proved undeveloped reserves in individual fields or countries that have remained undeveloped for five years or more after being disclosed as proved undeveloped reserves. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Internal controls on reserves and reserves audits </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">All of our oil and gas reserves held in consolidated companies have been estimated by our petroleum engineers. In order to meet the high standard of &#8220;reasonable certainty&#8221;, reserves estimates are stated taking into consideration additional guidance as to reservoir economic producibility requirements, acceptable proved area extensions, drive mechanisms and improved recovery methods, marketability under existing economic and operating conditions and project maturity. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Where applicable, the volumetric method is used to determine the original quantities of petroleum in place. Estimates are made by using various types of logs, core analysis and other available data. Formation tops, gross thickness and representative values for net pay thickness, porosity and interstitial fluid saturations are used to prepare structural maps to delineate each reservoir and isopachous maps to determine reservoir volume. Where adequate data is available and where circumstances are justified, material-balance and other engineering methods are used to estimate the original hydrocarbon in place. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Estimates of ultimate recovery in conventional reservoirs are usually reviewed by applying recovery factors to the original quantities of petroleum in place. These factors are based on the drive mechanisms inherent in the reservoir, analysis of the fluid and rock properties, the structural position of the reservoir and its production history. In some instances, comparisons are made with similar production reservoirs in the areas where more complete data is available. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">For unconventional reservoir developments, reserves estimates are focused on performance-based methodologies, where stimulation technique and current technology information are also integrated in the analysis. When applicable, statistical evaluations are implemented considering <span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap"><span style="white-space:nowrap">state-of-the-art</span></span></span> methods. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Where adequate data is available and where circumstances are justified, material-balance and other engineering methods are used to estimate ultimate recovery. In these instances, reservoir performance parameters such as cumulative production, production rate, reservoir pressure, gas to oil ratio behavior and water production are considered in estimating ultimate recovery. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">In certain cases where the above methods could not be used, proved reserves are estimated by analogy to similar reservoirs where more complete data are available. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">To control the quality of reserves booking, a process has been established that is integrated into the internal control system of YPF. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center">29 </p>
