Within four months from the end of each fiscal year, an ordinary shareholders&#8217; meeting must be held to consider the annual financial statements of YPF S.A. and determine the allocation of its net income for such year. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Under applicable CNV regulations, cash dividends must be paid to shareholders within 30 calendar days from the shareholders&#8217; meeting approving such dividends. In cases where the shareholders meeting delegates the authority for the distribution of dividends to the Board of Directors, the payment of dividends has been usually resolved within 30 days from the relevant Board of Directors&#8217; resolution. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">In the case of payment of stock dividends, or payment of both stock and cash dividends, both shares and cash, as the case may be, are required to be available within 3 months of the receipt of notice of the authorization of the CNV for the public offering of the shares arising from such dividends. In accordance with the Argentine Civil and Commercial Code, the statute of limitations to the right of any shareholder to receive dividends determined by the shareholders&#8217; meeting is 5 years from the date on which it has been made available to the shareholder. </p>

<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Under the deposit agreement, subject to certain terms and conditions set out in the deposit agreement, (including, among others, the Depositary&#8217;s judgement on determining that currency it receives other than U.S. dollars can be converted on a reasonable basis into U.S. dollars in a manner consistent with legal restrictions on foreign exchange) the Depositary converts dividends it receives on deposited shares in currency other than the U.S. dollar into U.S. dollars and distributes the amount thus received to the holders of ADRs associated with those shares. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">For information about exchange regulation on dividends payments see &#8220;&#8212;Exchange regulations&#8212;Specific provisions on access to the foreign exchange market&#8212;Profit and dividend payment&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold" id="rom804823_74"><span style="font-style:italic">Material contracts </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">None. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold;text-align:justify" id="rom804823_75"><span style="font-style:italic">Exchange rates </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">From 1991 until the end of 2001, Law No.&#160;23,928 (the &#8220;Convertibility Law&#8221;) established a fixed exchange rate of 1 Argentine peso per 1 U.S. dollar. On January&#160;6, 2002, Law No.&#160;25,561 (the &#8220;Public Emergency Law&#8221;) formally put an end to that U.S. dollar-Argentine peso parity. Following a brief period during which the Argentine government established a temporary dual exchange rate system pursuant to the Public Emergency Law, the Argentine peso has been allowed to float freely against other currencies since February 2002, although the Argentine government has the power to intervene by buying and selling foreign currency on its own account, a practice in which it engages on a regular basis. On December&#160;23, 2019, Law No.&#160;27,541 (the &#8220;Solidarity Law&#8221;) declared again the public emergency until December&#160;31, 2020. See &#8220;Item 3. Key information&#8212;Risk factors&#8212;Risks relating to Argentina&#8212;We may be exposed to fluctuations in foreign exchange rates&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Currency controls that tightened restrictions on capital flows, exchange controls, and the official exchange rate between the Argentine Peso and the U.S. dollar and transfer restrictions that substantially limit the ability of companies to retain foreign currency or make payments abroad are currently in place in Argentina and have been for alternating periods during the past years. By means of Decree No.&#160;609/2019 dated September&#160;1, 2019, as amended, the Argentine Executive Branch reinstated foreign exchange controls and authorized the BCRA to: (a)&#160;regulate access to the Foreign Exchange Market for the purchase of foreign currency and outward remittances; and (b)&#160;set forth regulations to avoid practices and transactions aimed at eluding, through the use of securities and other instruments, the measures adopted through the Decree No.&#160;609/2019. As of the date of this annual report, foreign exchange regulations have been (i)&#160;extended indefinitely, and (ii)&#160;consolidated in a single set of regulations, Communication &#8220;A&#8221; 7,914, as subsequently amended and supplemented from time to time by the BCRA. See &#8220;&#8212;Exchange regulations&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The BCRA requested the CNV to implement aligned measures to avoid elusive practices and operations. In this regard, the CNV, in line with the provisions of Article 3 of the Decree No.&#160;609/2019, established various measures to avoid such elusive practices and operations. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The following table, for the periods indicated, sets forth the low, high, average and <span style="white-space:nowrap">period-end</span> exchange rates, expressed in nominal Argentine peso per U.S. dollar, based on the average between the buying and selling exchange rates quoted by the BNA. The Federal Reserve Bank of New York does not report a noon buying rate for the Argentine peso. </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold" id="rom804823_76"><span style="font-style:italic">Exchange regulations </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">For the purposes of this section, (i) &#8220;foreign currency&#8221; means any currency other than the Argentine peso; and (ii) &#8220;Foreign Exchange Regulations&#8221; means the foreign exchange regulations issued by the BCRA pursuant to Communication &#8220;A&#8221; 7,953 as amended and supplemented from time to time. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Specific provisions for income from the foreign exchange market </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Entry and settlement of the proceeds from the export of goods through the foreign exchange market </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The Argentine exchange regime establishes that proceeds from exports of goods must be entered and settled in Argentine pesos through the foreign exchange market within 5 business days following their collection. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center">102 </p>

<h5><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></h5>


<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Decree No.&#160;28/2023 published on December&#160;13, 2023, established that in connection with: (i)&#160;the export countervalue of the services included in subsection c) of paragraph 2 of Article 10 of Law No.&#160;22,415 (&#8220;Customs Code&#8221;) and its amendments (which refers to services rendered in the country, with effective use or exploitation carried out abroad); and (ii)&#160;the countervalue of the export of goods included in the Common Nomenclature of MERCOSUR (&#8220;NCM&#8221;), including <span style="white-space:nowrap">pre-financing</span> and/or post-financing of exports from abroad or a liquidation advance; 80% of such countervalue must be brought into the country in foreign currency and/or negotiated through the foreign exchange market, and for the remaining 20% must be carried out through purchase and sale transactions with negotiable securities acquired with liquidation in foreign currency and sold with liquidation in local currency. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">In the case of funds received or credited abroad, the deposit and liquidation for the amount equivalent to the usual expenses debited by the financial entities abroad for the transfer of funds to the country may be considered as completed. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">There are some exceptions to the obligation to settle through the foreign exchange market, including, but not limited to: (i)&#160;collections from exporters under the Regime for the Promotion of Knowledge Economy Exports (established by Decree No.&#160;679/2022); and (ii)&#160;certain collections from exports of services by physical persons, as established by Article 2.2.2.2.1. of the Ordered Text. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Amounts collected in foreign currency for claims related to exported goods must also be entered and settled in Argentine pesos in the foreign exchange market, up to the amount of the insured exported goods. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The exporter must designate a financial entity to follow up each export transaction. The obligation to enter and settle foreign currency through the foreign exchange market corresponding to a shipment permit will be considered satisfied when the financial entity designated to follow up certifies that the entry and settlement have taken place. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Local charges for exports under the regime of farms to foreign-flagged means of transport </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">With respect to local charges for exports under the regime of farms to foreign-flagged means of transport, it will be considered as fully or partially compliant with the <span style="white-space:nowrap">follow-up</span> of the shipping permit, for an amount equivalent to that paid locally in Argentine pesos and/or in foreign currency to the exporter by a local agent of the company owning the foreign-flagged means of transport, provided that the following conditions are met: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:4%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:4%;vertical-align:top" align="left">(i)</td>
<td align="left" style="vertical-align:top"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The documentation shows that the delivery of the exported goods has taken place in the country, that the local agent of the company owning the foreign-flagged means of transport has made the payment to the exporter locally and the currency in which such payment was made. </p></td></tr></table>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:4%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:4%;vertical-align:top" align="left">(ii)</td>
<td align="left" style="vertical-align:top"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The company has a certification issued by a financial entity stating that the referred local agent would have had access to the foreign exchange market for the equivalent amount in foreign currency that is intended to be imputed to the permit. The financial entity issuing such certification must previously verify compliance with all the requirements established by the exchange regulations for access to the foreign exchange market by Article 3.2.5.2. of Exchange Regime, with the exception of the provisions of Article 3.16.1 of such regulations and have a sworn statement from the referred local agent stating that it has not transferred and will not transfer funds abroad for the proportional part of the transactions included in the certification. </p></td></tr></table>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:4%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:4%;vertical-align:top" align="left">(iii)</td>
<td align="left" style="vertical-align:top"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">In the event that the amounts have been received in the country in foreign currency, the company has the certification of settlement of the funds in the foreign exchange market. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The local agent of the company owning the foreign-flagged means of transport must not have used this mechanism for an amount exceeding US$ 2,000,000 in the charged calendar month. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Obligation to settle foreign currency from exports of services </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Payments received for the provision of services by residents to <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-residents</span> must be entered and settled through the foreign exchange market within 5 business days from the date of its collection abroad or in the country or its crediting to foreign accounts. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">In the case of funds received or credited abroad, the collection and liquidation may be considered completed for the amount equivalent to the usual expenses debited by the financial entities abroad for the transfer of funds to the country. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The aforementioned provisions of Decree No.&#160;28/2023 are also applicable to the export of services (see &#8220;&#8212;Entry and settlement of the proceeds from the export of goods through the foreign exchange market&#8221;). </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Application of export revenues </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The Exchange Regime authorizes the application of export revenues to the repayment of: <span style="white-space:nowrap">(i)&#160;pre-financing</span> of exports and export financing granted or guaranteed by local financial entities; <span style="white-space:nowrap">(ii)&#160;pre-</span> financing of exports and export advances settled in the foreign exchange market, provided that the corresponding transactions have been executed through public deeds or public registries; (iii)&#160;financial indebtedness under contracts entered into prior to August&#160;31, 2019 that provide for the cancellation thereof through the application abroad of export funds; (iv)&#160;other foreign financial indebtedness subject to certain requirements as set forth in Articles 7. 9 and 7.10 of the Exchange Regime; and (v)&#160;advances, <span style="white-space:nowrap">pre-financing</span> and post-financing from abroad with partial liquidation under the provisions of Decrees No.&#160;492/2023, No.&#160;549/2023, No.&#160;597/2023 and No.&#160;28/2023. Likewise, it allows keeping export revenues abroad to guarantee the payment of new indebtedness, provided certain requirements are met. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Financial indebtedness with foreign countries </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">According to Article 2.4 of the Exchange Regime for resident debtors to be able to access the foreign exchange market to repay financial indebtedness with foreign countries disbursed as from September&#160;1, 2019, the loan proceeds must have been settled through the foreign exchange market and the transaction must have been declared in the External Assets and Liabilities Survey (&#8220;Relevamiento de Activos y Pasivos Externos&#8221;). Accordingly, although settlement of the loan proceeds is not mandatory, failure to settle will preclude future access to the foreign exchange market for repayment purposes. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Access to the foreign exchange market to make such payments more than three days in advance of the due date is, as a general rule, subject to the BCRA&#8217;s prior authorization. Prepayments made with funds from new foreign loans duly settled or in connection with debt refinancing or liability management processes may be exempt from such prior authorization from the BCRA to the extent they comply with several requirements as set forth in Article 3.5 of the Exchange Regime. </p>
 <p style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:center">103 </p>

</div></div>



<p style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"> </p>
<hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%"/>
<h5><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></h5>


<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Until December&#160;31, 2024, prior BCRA approval is required for local residents to access the foreign exchange market to make principal and interest payments under cross-border financial borrowings with related parties. Certain specific exceptions apply and are included in item 3.5.6. of the Ordered Text. (unless the loan proceeds were settled through the foreign exchange market after October&#160;1, 2020, and the loan has an average life of at least 2 years). </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Specific provisions on access to the foreign exchange market </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">General requirements </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">As a general rule, and in addition to the specific rules of each transaction for access, certain general requirements must be complied with by a local company or individual to access the foreign exchange market for the purchase of foreign currency or its transfer abroad (i.e., payments of imports and other purchases of goods abroad; payment of services rendered by <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-residents;</span> distribution of profits and dividends; payment of principal and interest on foreign indebtedness; interest payments on debts for the import of goods and services, among others) without requiring prior approval from the BCRA. In this regard, the local company or individual must file a sworn statement stating that: </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; text-indent:-2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">(a)&#160;(i) At the time of access to the foreign exchange market, all of its foreign currency holdings in the country are deposited in accounts in financial institutions, and (ii)&#160;at the beginning of the day on which it requests access to the foreign exchange market, it does not hold Argentine certificates of deposit (for its acronym in Spanish, &#8220;CEDEARs&#8221;) representing foreign shares and/or available liquid foreign assets that together have a value greater than US$ 100,000 (funds deposited abroad that constitute reserve or guarantee funds under debt contracts with foreign countries, or funds granted as guarantee for derivatives arranged abroad are excluded from this limit). If the customer is a local government, foreign currency holdings deposited with local financial institutions must also be accounted up to December&#160;31, 2024. For these purposes, &#8220;liquid foreign assets&#8221; are considered to be holdings of banknotes and coins in foreign currency, cash in gold coins or bars of good delivery, demand deposits in financial institutions abroad and other investments that allow immediate availability of foreign currency. On the other hand, funds deposited abroad that cannot be used by the client because they are reserve or guarantee funds created by virtue of the requirements set forth in foreign debt contracts or funds created as guarantee for derivative transactions arranged abroad should not be considered as liquid foreign assets available. In the event that the client is a local government and exceeds the established limit, the institution may also accept an affidavit from the client stating that the excess was used to make payments for the foreign exchange market through swap and/or arbitrage operations with the deposited funds. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; text-indent:-2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">(b) It undertakes the obligation to settle in the foreign exchange market, within five business days of its availability, the funds received abroad from the collection of loans granted to third parties, time deposits, or the sale of any type of asset, to the extent that the asset subject to the sale was acquired, the deposit constituted or the loan granted after May&#160;28, 2020. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; text-indent:-2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">(c) On the date of access to the foreign exchange market and in the previous 90 calendar days in the case of securities issued under Argentine Law and in the 180 calendar days prior in the case of transactions that are not carried out with securities issued under Argentine Law, it: (i)&#160;did not arrange sales in the country of securities with settlement in foreign currency; (ii)&#160;did not exchange securities issued by residents for foreign assets, (iii)&#160;did not transfer securities to depository entities abroad, (iv)&#160;did not acquire in the country securities issued by <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-residents</span> with settlement in Argentine pesos, (v)&#160;did not acquire CEDEARs representing foreign shares, (vi)&#160;did not acquire securities representing private debt issued in foreign jurisdiction, and (vii)&#160;did not deliver funds in local currency or other local assets (except funds in foreign currency deposited in local financial institutions) to any entity (whether physical or legal, resident or <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-resident,</span> related or not), receiving as prior or subsequent consideration, directly or indirectly, by itself or through a related, controlled or controlling entity, foreign assets, crypto-assets or securities deposited abroad. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; text-indent:-2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">(d) It undertakes the obligation not to enter into any of the transactions described in paragraph (c)&#160;above from the time it requests access to the foreign exchange market and for 90 calendar days thereafter in the case of securities issued under Argentine Law and for the following 180 calendar days in the case of transactions that are not carried out with securities issued under Argentine Law. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:3%; text-indent:-2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">(e) Article 3.16.3 of the Exchange Regime adds that, in the event that the customer requesting access to the exchange market is a legal entity, in order for the transaction not to be covered by the requirement of prior approval by the BCRA must be submitted to the corresponding financial institution: </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:6%; text-indent:-2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">(A) a sworn statement evidencing that within the term provided in section 3.16.3.4. (180 days prior to accessing the foreign exchange market) it has not delivered in the country any funds in local currency or other liquid local assets, except funds in foreign currency deposited in local financial institutions, to any person or legal entity, except those directly associated with regular transactions in the course of its business (this sworn statement shall be called &#8220;Sworn Statement - Section&#160;1&#8221;); or </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:6%; text-indent:-2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">(B)(i) as required by Article 3.16.3.3. of the Exchange Regime, an affidavit stating details of the physical or legal persons exercising a direct control relationship over the client and of other legal persons with which it is part of the same economic group. In determining the existence of a direct control relationship, the types of relationships described in item 1.2.2.1 of the Large Exposures rules should be considered. Companies sharing a control relationship of the type defined in items 1.2.1.1 and 1.2.2.1 of the Large Exposures rules should be considered as members of the same &#8220;economic group&#8221; (the &#8220;Economic Group Description Affidavit&#8221;); and (ii)&#160;that on the day on which it requests access to the market and in the 180 days prior to that date, it has not delivered in the country any funds in local currency or other liquid local assets, except funds in foreign currency deposited in local financial institutions, to any individual or legal entity that exercises a direct control relationship over it, or to other companies with which it is part of the same economic group, except those directly associated with regular transactions between residents for the acquisition of goods and/or services (the &#8220;Sworn Statement of <span style="white-space:nowrap">Non-Delivery</span> of Pesos to the Economic Group&#8221;). It also provides that in the case of individuals or legal entities exercising a direct control relationship, the term of 180 calendar days shall only be applicable for deliveries made as from April&#160;21, 2013, and the term of 90 calendar days shall be applicable for deliveries made prior to that date. While for legal entities that are part of the same economic group but did not exercise a direct control relationship over the customer as of May&#160;11, 2023, the provisions shall be applicable only for deliveries made as of May&#160;12, 2023. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:6%; text-indent:-2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">(C) The provisions of item 3.16.3.4. (as detailed in (B)(ii) above) may be deemed to have been complied with if the customer seeking access has submitted: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Payment for services rendered by <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-residents</span> </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Pursuant to Article 3.2 of the Exchange Regime, entities may access the foreign exchange market to make payments for services rendered by <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-residents</span> as long as they have documentation to support the existence of the service. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">In the case of commercial debts for services, access is granted as from the expiration date, provided that it is verified that the operation is declared, if applicable, in the last due presentation of the &#8220;External Assets and Liabilities Survey&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Communication &#8220;A&#8221; 7,953 issued on January&#160;26, 2024, substantially modified the regime of access to the foreign exchange market for the payment of imports of goods and services. The aforementioned Communication established the following regarding access to the foreign exchange market for the payment of imports of services, effective as of December&#160;13, 2023: </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:6%; text-indent:-2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">(a) Access to the foreign exchange market for the payment of services. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:6%; text-indent:-2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">(b) Entities may provide access to the foreign exchange market to make payments for <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-residents</span> services that were or will be rendered as of December&#160;31, 2023, when, in addition to the other applicable regulatory requirements, the transaction falls within one of the situations detailed below: </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:10%; text-indent:-2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">(i) The payment corresponds to a transaction that falls under the following concept codes: </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">S03.&#8195;&#8194;Passenger transportation services. </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">S06.&#8195;&#8194;Travel (excluding transactions associated with withdrawals and/or consumption with resident cards with <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-resident</span> suppliers or <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-resident</span> cards with Argentine suppliers). </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">S23.&#8195;&#8194;Audiovisual services. </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">S25.&#8194;&#8195;Government services. </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:13%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">S26.&#8194;&#8195;Health services by travel assistance companies. </p> <p style="margin-top:0pt; Likewise, the aforementioned conformity shall not be applicable when (1)&#160;the client has a &#8220;Certification of Increase of Exports of Goods&#8221; for the years 2021 to 2023, issued within the framework of the provisions of Article 3.18 of the Exchange Regime for the equivalent of the amount of capital to be paid, (2)&#160;in the case of a financial indebtedness abroad with an average life of not less than 2 years, settled between August&#160;21, 2021 and December&#160;12, 2023, and which was originally used to pay commercial debts for the import of goods and services that originated the issuance of a Certificate of Entry of New Financial Indebtedness Abroad within the framework of Article 3.19 of the Exchange Regime; (3)&#160;in the case of a financial indebtedness abroad with an average life of not less than 2 years originated between August&#160;27, 2021 and December&#160;12, 2023, originated in a refinancing with the creditor of commercial debts for the importation of goods and services within the framework of the provisions of Article 3. 20 of the Exchange Regime; the entity must have a certification for access to the foreign exchange market issued within the 5 previous business days, by the entity that registered with the BCRA within the concept code &#8220;P17. <h5><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></h5>


<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Access to the foreign exchange market for the payment of new issues of debt securities </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Entities may access to the foreign exchange market for the payment of principal and services of debt securities denominated and publicly registered abroad when the debtor has settled through the foreign exchange market an amount equivalent to the face value of the external indebtedness. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The aforementioned requirement will be deemed to be met for the portion of debt securities publicly registered abroad issued as from January&#160;7, 2021, intended to refinance <span style="white-space:nowrap">pre-existing</span> debt by extending their average life, for an amount equivalent to the refinanced principal, and provided that the new securities do not have a principal maturity schedule within two years, for interest accrued through the date of refinancing and, interest that would accrue during the first two years on the refinanced indebtedness and/or on the deferral of the refinanced principal and/or interest that would accrue on the refinanced amounts. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Duly registered securities that are denominated and payable in foreign currency in Argentina </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Pursuant to Article 2.5 of the Exchange Regime, resident debt issuers will have access to the foreign exchange market for the payment at maturity of principal and interest of duly registered debt security issues that are denominated and payable in foreign currency in Argentina, to the extent that (i)&#160;they are fully subscribed in foreign currency, and (ii)&#160;provided that the proceeds of the issue are previously settled through the foreign exchange market. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic"><span style="white-space:nowrap">Non-resident</span> access to the foreign exchange market </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Pursuant to Article 3.13 of the Exchange Regime, the prior approval of the BCRA will be required for access to the foreign exchange market by <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-residents</span> for the purchase of foreign currency, with the exception of the following situations: (a)&#160;international organizations and institutions that perform the functions of official export credit agencies; (b)&#160;diplomatic representations and consular and diplomatic personnel accredited in the country for transfers made in the exercise of their functions; (c)&#160;representatives of courts, authorities or offices, special missions, commissions or bilateral organizations established by treaties or international agreements, to which the Argentine Republic is a party, to the extent that the transfers are made in the exercise of their functions; (d)&#160;transfers abroad on behalf of persons who are beneficiaries of retirement and/or pensions paid by the National Administration of Social Security (&#8220;ANSES&#8221;), for up to the amount paid by such agency in the calendar month and to the extent that the transfer is made to a bank account owned by the beneficiary in his/her registered country of residence; (e)&#160;purchase of foreign currency in cash by <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-residents</span> for tourism and travel expenses, up to a maximum amount of US$ 100, to the extent that the financial institution can verify in the online system implemented by the BCRA that the customer has settled an amount equal to or greater than the amount to be purchased within the 90 days prior to the transaction; (f)&#160;transfers to offshore bank accounts of persons who are beneficiaries of pensions granted by the National State in accordance with Laws No.&#160;24,043, No.&#160;24,411, No.&#160;25,914 and complementary laws; and (g)&#160;repatriations of direct investments of <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-residents</span> in companies that are not controlling companies of local financial entities, to the extent that the capital contribution has been entered and settled through the foreign exchange market as from October&#160;2, 2020 and the repatriation takes place at least two years after its entry. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Access to the foreign exchange market for savings or investment purposes by individuals </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Pursuant to Article 3.8 of the Exchange Regime, Argentine residents may access the foreign exchange market for purposes of asset formation abroad, family assistance and derivative transactions (with some expressly stated exceptions) for up to US$ 200 (through debits to local bank accounts) or US$ 100 (in cash) per person per month through all authorized exchange entities. If the access involves a transfer of funds abroad, the destination account must be an account owned by the same person. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">In all cases, the general requirements detailed under &#8220;&#8212;Specific Provisions on Access to the Foreign Exchange Market - General Requirements&#8221; apply. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Purchases in Argentine pesos made abroad with debit cards and amounts in foreign currency acquired by physical persons in the foreign exchange market as from September&#160;1, 2020, for the payment of obligations between residents within the framework of Article 3.6 of the Exchange Regime, including payments for purchases with credit cards in foreign currency, will be deducted, as from the following calendar month, from the monthly quota of US$ 200. If the amount of such purchases exceeds the quota available for the following month or such quota has already been absorbed by other purchases made since September&#160;1, 2020, such deduction shall be made from the quotas of the following months until the amount of such purchases is completed. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The corresponding entity will verify in the online system implemented by the BCRA whether the person has not reached the limits set for the corresponding calendar month or has not exceeded them in the previous calendar month and, therefore, is entitled to perform the exchange transaction, and will request the customer to submit a sworn statement stating that such person is not a beneficiary of any &#8220;Zero Rate Credits&#8221; referred to in Article 9 of Decree No.&#160;332/2020, as amended, &#8220;Subsidized Rate Credits for Companies&#8221; and/or &#8220;Zero Rate Credits for Culture&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">In addition, by means of Communication &#8220;A&#8221; 7,606, the BCRA established that users of public utilities that requested and obtained the subsidy in the tariffs derived from the supply of natural gas and/or electric energy, as well as those that had obtained it automatically, and those that maintain the subsidy in the potable water tariffs, may not, while maintaining the mentioned benefit: (i)&#160;access the foreign exchange market to make purchases of foreign currency by physical persons for the formation of foreign assets of residents, remission of family aid and for operations with derivatives, under the terms of Article 3.8. of the rules on exterior and foreign exchange; nor (ii)&#160;to carry out the transactions set forth in Article 4.3.2. of the rules on exterior and foreign exchange. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Finally, through Communication &#8220;A&#8221; 7,609 the BCRA established, effective as from September&#160;20, 2022, that customers who are legal persons residing in the country engaged in agricultural activities who sell goods within the framework of Decree No.&#160;576/2022 to those who export them directly or as a result of a productive process carried out in the country may not: (i)&#160;access the foreign exchange market to make purchases of foreign currency by physical persons for the formation of foreign assets of residents, remission of family assistance and for transactions with derivatives, under the terms of Article 3.8. of the regulations on exterior and foreign exchange; nor (ii)&#160;to carry out the transactions set forth in Article 4.3.2. of the regulations on exterior and foreign exchange. These last provisions are not applicable to physical persons. </p>

<div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">
 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Access to the foreign exchange market by other residents -excluding entities- for the formation of foreign assets and for derivative transactions. </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Pursuant to Article 3.10 of the Exchange Regime, access to the foreign exchange market for the constitution of foreign assets and for derivative transactions by local governments, investment funds, other universalities established in Argentina, requires the prior authorization of the BCRA. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Access to the foreign exchange market by guarantee trusts for the payment of principal and interest </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Pursuant to Article 3.7 of the Exchange Regime, Argentine guarantee trusts created to guarantee principal and interest payments of resident debtors may access the foreign exchange market to make such payments at their scheduled maturity, to the extent that, in accordance with the applicable regulations in force, the debtor would have had access to the foreign exchange market to make such payments directly. Also, under certain conditions, a trustee may access the foreign exchange market to guarantee certain principal and interest payments on foreign financial debt and anticipate access to the foreign exchange market. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Derivative transactions </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Article 3.12 of the Exchange Regime requires that, as from September&#160;11, 2019, the settlement of futures transactions in regulated markets, &#8220;forwards&#8221;, options and any other type of derivatives entered into in the country, be made in Argentine pesos. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Likewise, access to the foreign exchange market will be allowed for the payment of premiums, constitution of guarantees and cancellations corresponding to interest rate hedging contract transactions for the obligations of residents abroad declared and validated, as applicable, in the Relevance of Foreign Assets and Liabilities, provided that such guarantees do not cover risks higher than the foreign liabilities incurred by the debtor at the interest rate of the risk being hedged through such transaction. The client that access the local market through this mechanism must designate an authorized institution to operate in the foreign exchange market that will do the follow up the operation and will submit a sworn statement committing to repatriate and settle the funds corresponding to it as a consequence of such operation or as a consequence of the release of the money from the guarantee, within 5 business days following the date on which such payment or release occurs. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Profit and dividend payment </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Pursuant to Article 3.4 of the Exchange Regime, access to the foreign exchange market for the transfer of foreign currency abroad for the payment of dividends and profits to <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-resident</span> shareholders is subject to the prior approval of the BCRA, unless the following requirements are met: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

When the financial institution charges a commission or fee for these transactions, it will be instrumented in a specifically designated item. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Securities transactions </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">According to CNV General Resolution No.&#160;988/2023, as amended, sales of marketable securities with settlement in foreign currency, in any jurisdiction and regardless of the law under which they are issued may be made, provided that a minimum holding period of 1 business day counted as of its accreditation at the Central Depository Agent of Negotiable Securities (&#8220;<span style="font-style:italic">Agente Depositario Central de Valores Negociables&#8221;</span>), to the extent that the purchases of the marketable securities in question have been made against Argentine pesos. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Likewise, transfers to foreign depository institutions of marketable securities purchased with Argentine pesos, regardless of the law under which they are issued, must comply with a minimum holding period of 1 business day as from the date of deposit of such marketable securities, unless such accreditation (i)&#160;results from a primary placement of marketable securities issued by the National Treasury or by the BCRA, in the framework of the Communication &#8220;A&#8221; 7.918, as amended, (ii)&#160;refers to transactions under Articles 3.16.3.6 point (v) and 4.7.2.2. of the Exchange Regime, and (iii) or refers to Argentine shares and/or certificates of deposit (CEDEAR) traded in markets regulated by the CNV. Intermediaries and trading agents must verify compliance with the aforementioned minimum holding period of marketable securities. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">In addition, (i)&#160;the beneficiaries of refinancings provided for in Article 1.1.1. of the rules on &#8220;Financial Services within the Framework of the Sanitary Emergency provided for by Decree No.&#160;260/2020 Coronavirus <span style="white-space:nowrap">(COVID-19)&#8221;,</span> until their total cancellation, (ii)&#160;the beneficiaries of &#8220;Zero Rate Credits&#8221;, &#8220;Zero Rate Credits 2021&#8221;, &#8220;Zero Rate Credits Culture&#8221; or &#8220;Subsidized Rate Credits for Companies&#8221;, provided for in Articles1. 1.2. and 1.1.3. of the rules on &#8220;Financial Services within the Framework of the Sanitary Emergency provided by Decree No.&#160;260/2020 Coronavirus <span style="white-space:nowrap">(COVID-19)&#8221;,</span> until their total cancellation, (iii)&#160;the beneficiaries of financing in Argentine pesos under section 2 of the Communication &#8220;A&#8221; 6,937, Articles2 and 3 of Communication &#8220;A&#8221; 7. 006, as supplemented; until its total cancellation, (iv)&#160;the beneficiaries of Article 2 of Decree No.&#160;319/2020 and complementary and regulatory rules, for the duration of the benefit with respect to the update of the value of the installment, and (v)&#160;the persons included in the Joint Resolution of the President of the Honorable Senate of the Nation and of the President of the Honorable Chamber of Deputies of the Nation No.&#160;12/2020; will be prevented from selling marketable securities issued by residents to be settled in foreign currency in Argentina or transferring such marketable securities to foreign depositories or exchanging marketable securities issued by residents for foreign assets or the acquisition in the country with settlement in Argentine pesos of marketable securities issued by <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-residents.</span> Customers included in the BCRA Communications &#8220;A&#8221; 7,606 and &#8220;A&#8221; 7,609 may not carry out these transactions either. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Special provisions for financing under the Plan GasAr </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Article 3.5.5 of the Exchange Regime states that to the extent that the BCRA&#8217;s prior conformity requirement is in effect for access to the foreign exchange market for the cancellation at maturity of principal and interest on foreign financial debt, this requirement shall not apply to the extent that all of the following conditions are met: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:4%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top" align="left">(i)</td>
<td align="left" style="vertical-align:top"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The funds were used to finance projects within the framework of the Plan GasAr. </p></td></tr></table>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:4%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top" align="left">(ii)</td>
<td align="left" style="vertical-align:top"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The funds have been deposited and settled by the foreign exchange market as of November&#160;16, 2020; and </p></td></tr></table>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:4%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top" align="left">(iii)</td>
<td align="left" style="vertical-align:top"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The indebtedness has an average life of not less than two years. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Special provisions for the Export Investment Promotion Regime established by Decree No.&#160;234/2021 </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The Decree No.&#160;234/2021 established a new Export Investment Promotion Regime (the &#8220;Promotion Regime&#8221;), with the objective, among others, of increasing exports of goods and promoting sustainable economic development. The Ministry of Economy and the Ministry of Productive Development will be the authorities for the application of the Promotion Regime. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The Promotion Regime covers investments for new productive projects in, among others, forestry, mining, hydrocarbon, manufacturing and agro-industrial activities, as well as the expansion of existing business units that require investments to increase their production. The benefits of the Promotion Regime do not apply to commodities such as wheat, corn, soybeans and biodiesel, among others. Although the regulatory entities may include and/or exclude activities from the Promotion Regime, the decree establishes that vested rights will not be affected. </p>

 <p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The requirements are as follows: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

<td align="left" style="vertical-align:top"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Both legal entities and individuals, resident or <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-resident,</span> may apply. </p></td></tr></table>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">

<td align="left" style="vertical-align:top"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Presentation of an &#8220;Export Investment Project&#8221; consisting of a minimum direct investment of US$ 100,000,000. </p></td></tr></table>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">

<td align="left" style="vertical-align:top"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Comply with the terms and conditions of the projects submitted and approved by the regulators. </p></td></tr></table>
<table style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0">

<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top" align="left">(iv)</td>
<td align="left" style="vertical-align:top"> <p style=" margin-top:0pt ; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The followings time are not eligible to apply for the Promotion Regime: (a)&#160;individuals and legal entities whose representatives or directors have been convicted of certain crimes with prison sentences and/or disqualification for a specific period of time; (b)&#160;individuals and legal entities with overdue and unpaid tax or social security debts; (c)&#160;individuals and legal entities with tax or social security debts; (d)&#160;individuals and legal entities that have unpaid taxes, fees, fines or surcharges imposed on them by a final judicial or administrative decision in customs, exchange, tax or social security matters; and (e)&#160;individuals that have unjustifiably failed to comply with their obligations in connection with other promotion schemes. </p></td></tr></table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Once the relevant requirements have been verified, the application authority will approve the project and will issue an &#8220;Export Investment Certificate&#8221; for the purpose of accessing the benefits established by the Promotion Regime, which will have a term of 15 years. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Beneficiaries participating in the Export Promotion Regime may apply up to 20% of the foreign currency income obtained from exports related to the project to (i)&#160;the payment of principal and interest of financial or commercial debts with foreign countries, (ii)&#160;the payment of dividends, and (iii)&#160;the repatriation of direct investments of <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-residents.</span> However, this benefit may not exceed an annual maximum of 25% of the gross amount of foreign currency liquidated by such beneficiary through the foreign exchange market to finance the development of the project. In estimating the gross amount of foreign currency settled by the beneficiary in the foreign exchange market to finance the project, foreign currency flows from exports will not be taken into account. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">In the case of projects involving investments in excess of US$ 500,000,000, the beneficiaries may opt to access an extended benefit for each year in which the benefit previously provided for has not been used. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">In the case of projects involving investments between US$ 500,000,000 and US$ 1,000,000,000, for each year in which the benefit has not been used, they may enjoy, for two consecutive years, an amount of free application equivalent to double the percentage previously foreseen. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The calculation of the benefit will be made on the foreign exchange earned from exports related to the project during the year in which the extended benefit is used. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The amount of the free application benefit may not exceed an annual maximum of 40% of the gross amount of the foreign currency effectively entered by the beneficiary in the foreign exchange market to finance the development of the project, at the time of making use of the same. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The benefits of the Promotion Regime will cease (i)&#160;upon expiration of the term of use, (ii)&#160;in certain cases, when the beneficiary ceases to have the capacity to carry out the activity that is the reason for the investment project, as established in the applicable regime, or (iii)&#160;if the beneficiary fails to comply with its obligations under the Promotion Regime without justification. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic">Regime for Access to Foreign Currency for Incremental Petroleum Production (&#8220;RADPIP&#8221;) </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The Decree No.&#160;277/2022 approved the Foreign Exchange Access Regime for the Incremental Production of Hydrocarbons with the purpose of promoting production in the hydrocarbons sector, generating incentives through the granting of foreign exchange access channels without prior authorization from the BCRA. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">In this way, two regimes of access to the foreign exchange market were created to increase investments related to the production of crude oil and natural gas, which will be subordinated to a third regime for the promotion of employment, work and the development of suppliers in the regional and national hydrocarbons industry: </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify"><span style="font-style:italic">Beneficiaries:</span> Those subjects registered in the Registry of Oil Companies of the National State that are holders of hydrocarbon exploitation concessions granted by the National State, the provinces or Autonomous City of Buenos Aires and that: </p> <p style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</p>

The volume effectively injected will be the average daily injection of the last 12 preceding months. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify"><span style="font-style:italic">Incentives</span>: The beneficiary will enjoy the benefits of the RADPIGN on a percentage of its incremental injection on a quarterly basis. The information contained in these websites is not part of this annual report and is not deemed to be incorporated herein. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;font-weight:bold" id="rom804823_77"><span style="font-style:italic">Taxation </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Argentine tax considerations </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The following discussion is a summary of the material Argentine tax considerations relating to the purchase, ownership and disposition of our Class&#160;D shares or ADSs, based upon tax laws of Argentina as in effect on the date of this annual report and subject to any change in Argentine law that may come into effect after such date. Any change could apply retroactively and could affect the continued validity of this summary. Holders are encouraged to consult their tax advisors regarding the tax treatment of our Class&#160;D shares or ADSs in each tax as it relates to their particular situation. Although the following description is based on a reasonable interpretation of the rules in force, there can be no assurance that the tax authorities or the courts will agree with each and every one of the comments made herein. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify"><span style="font-style:italic">Income tax (&#8220;IT&#8221;) </span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:4%; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><span style="font-style:italic"><span style="text-decoration:underline">Taxation on dividends </span></span></p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">No Argentine IT withholding would be levied on dividends paid on our Class&#160;D shares or ADSs derived from profits earned during tax periods beginning up to December 31, 2017, whether disbursed in cash, property or other equity securities, except for the application of the equalization tax (&#8220;Equalization tax&#8221;). The Equalization tax applies to dividends exceeding the &#8220;net accumulated taxable income&#8221; from th e immediate prior fiscal period at the time of distribution. To determine the &#8220;net accumulated taxable income&#8221; under Argentine Income Tax Law (&#8220;Income Tax Law&#8221;), the IT paid in the same fiscal period should be subtracted and the local dividends received in the previous fiscal period should be added to such income. The Equalization tax would be imposed at a 35% rate on the excess amount. It is considered a final tax and it is not applicable if dividends are paid in shares (&#8220;<span style="font-style:italic">acciones liberadas</span>&#8221;) instead of cash. If applicable, the Company is responsible for withholding the IT. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Dividends originated in profits obtained during fiscal years initiated on or after January 1, 2018 on Argentine shares paid to Argentine resident individuals and/or <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-Argentine</span> residents would be subject to a 7% IT withholding as a single and definitive payment on the amount of such dividends (&#8220;Dividend tax&#8221;). However, if dividends are distributed to Argentine entities (in general, entities organized or incorporated under Argentine law, certain traders and intermediaries, local branches of <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-Argentine</span> entities, sole proprietorships and individuals carrying on certain commercial activities in Argentina, among others), no Dividend tax would apply. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">In addition, Equalization tax is not applicable for dividends originated in profits obtained during fiscal years initiated on or after January 1, 2018. </p>

</table> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">The amounts stated in the chart above are subject to annual updates based on the CPI inflation index rate published by the INDEC. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Losses arising from the sale of shares and ADSs can only be offset against income derived from the same type and source of operations (understanding by &#8220;type&#8221; the different concepts of income included under each article of Chapter II, Title IV of the Income Tax Law), for a five-year carryover period. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Starting in 2018, Argentine resident individuals and undivided estates enjoy an exemption from capital gains tax on income derived from the sale of shares and other securities in specific scenarios. These scenarios encompass: (i)&#160;shares placed through a <span style="white-space:nowrap">CNV-authorized</span> public offering; (ii)&#160;shares traded on <span style="white-space:nowrap">CNV-authorized</span> stock markets with segments that ensuring priority of price-time and interference of offers; and/or (iii)&#160;the sale, exchange or other disposition of shares through <span style="white-space:nowrap">CNV-authorized</span> tender offer regimes and/or share exchanges. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Additionally, Article 34 of the Solidarity Law stipulates that Argentine resident individuals and undivided estates are exempt from capital gains tax on the sale, exchange or disposal of securities falling under the provisions of Article 98 of the Income Tax Law, not included in the first paragraph of Article 26 subsection u) of the Income Tax Law. This exemption applies as long as said securities are listed on <span style="white-space:nowrap">CNV-authorized</span> stock exchanges or securities markets, without the application of Article 109 of the Income Tax Law. In this sense, Article 109 of the Income Tax Law specifies that total or partial exemptions established or that will be established in the future by special laws for securities issued by national, provincial, or municipal states or the Autonomous City of Buenos Aires, do not affect IT for Argentine resident individuals and undivided estates. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Notably, ADSs would not qualify for the exemption applicable to Argentine resident individuals due to <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-compliance</span> with the referred conditions. In the absence of the exemption, income obtained by Argentine resident individuals and undivided estates located in Argentina from the sale, exchange, or other disposal of ADSs (and shares, if applicable) is subject to a 15% capital gains tax on net income (calculated in Argentine pesos). The acquisition cost may be adjusted based on the CPI inflation index rate published by the INDEC, provided the extent the equity participation was acquired after January 1, 2018. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">If Argentine resident individuals and undivided estates undertake a conversion process involving securities representing shares, that do not fall within the exemption scenarios outlined in points (i), (ii) and/or (iii)&#160;above, with the intention to hold the underlying shares eligible for the exemption, such conversion would be considered a taxable transfer of the securities representing shares. The taxable value is determined based on their fair market value at the time of conversion. The same tax treatment will apply if the conversion process involves shares not eligible for the exemption being transformed into securities representing shares that qualify for the exemption. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Upon completion of the conversion, the results obtained from any subsequent sale, exchange, swap or any other disposition of the underlying shares or securities representing shares would be exempt from IT, provided that the conditions specified in points (i), (ii) and/or (iii)&#160;of the paragraph above are satisfied. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">In light of amendments introduced by the Solidarity Law, it could also be construed that a capital gains exemption could also apply for Argentine resident individuals and undivided estates if the securities involved in the conversion process are listed on stock exchanges or securities markets authorized by the CNV (although the matter is not free from doubt and further clarifications should be issued). </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Due to the amendments introduced to the Income Tax Law, <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-Argentine</span> resident individuals or legal entities (&#8220;foreign beneficiaries&#8221;) are also exempt from IT derived from the sale of Argentine shares in the following situations: (i)&#160;when the shares are placed through a <span style="white-space:nowrap">CNV-authorized</span> public offering; (ii)&#160;when shares are traded on <span style="white-space:nowrap">CNV-authorized</span> stock markets, with segments that ensuring priority of price-time and interference of offers; and/or (iii)&#160;the sale, exchange or other disposition of shares through <span style="white-space:nowrap">CNV-authorized</span> tender offer regimes and/or share exchanges. The exemption applies to the extent the foreign beneficiaries reside in a &#8220;cooperative jurisdiction&#8221; and, in accordance with Article 90 of the Regulatory Decree of the Income Tax Law, if their funds come from &#8220;cooperative jurisdictions&#8221;. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">In addition, under Law No.&#160;27,430 income arising from the sale of ADSs is categorized as Argentine source income. However, capital gains resulting from the sale, exchange or other disposition of ADSs by foreign beneficiaries residing in a &#8220;cooperative jurisdiction&#8221; and, whose funds originate from &#8220;cooperative jurisdictions&#8221;, as per Article 90 of the Regulatory Decree of the Income Tax Law, are exempt from IT on capital gains. This exemption applies as long as the underlying shares are authorized for public offering by the CNV. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">In the event that foreign beneficiaries undergo a conversion process of shares not eligible for the exemption into securities representing shares that are exempt from IT, such conversion would be treated as a taxable transfer of shares. The taxable value is determined based on their fair market value at the time of the conversion. </p> <p style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:Times New Roman;text-align:justify">Nevertheless, it is essential to highlight that if <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-Argentine</span> residents are situated in a <span style="white-space:nowrap">&#8220;non-cooperating</span> jurisdiction&#8221; (as defined below) or if the invested funds are originated in a <span style="white-space:nowrap">non-cooperating</span> jurisdiction, the aforementioned exemptions do not apply. Consequently, any capital gains resulting from the disposal of Class&#160;D shares or ADSs will be subject to IT at an effective rate of 31.5% on the gross sale price. </p>
