<td colspan="5" style="vertical-align:top"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">NOTES TO THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</div></div><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 1pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">AS OF DECEMBER 31, 2023, 2022 AND 2021</div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_46" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_47"><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_47" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_48"><ix:exclude>

<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">BASIS OF PREPARATION OF THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (cont.) </div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_48" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_49"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993498_2"><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">At the closing date of each period, the Group reviews if there is any indication that these investments may have suffered an impairment in value or recovery of an impairment loss recognized in previous periods. If such an indication exists, the recoverable amount of the investment is estimated. If an impairment in value or recovery of an impairment loss is recognized in previous periods, it is recognized in the &#8220;Income from equity interests in associates and joint ventures&#8221; line item in the statement of comprehensive income. </div></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForFinancialInstrumentsExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" escape="true" continuedAt="TextSelection_111997092" id="ixv-30286"><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.b.7) Financial instruments </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Group&#8217;s classification of financial assets is determined by the business model for the management of such assets and the characteristics of contractual cash flows. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">A financial asset is measured at amortized cost if the following conditions are met: (i)&#160;the objective of the Group&#8217;s business model is to hold the asset to collect the contractual cash flows; and (2)&#160;the contractual terms establish payments, on specific dates, solely of principal and interest. These financial assets are initially recognized at fair value plus costs of the transaction incurred and are subsequently measured at amortized cost using the effective interest rate method less any impairment losses. Gain (loss) arising from derecognition, modifications, reclassifications at fair value through profit or loss, impairment in value, or from applying the effective interest rate are recognized in the &#8220;Net financial results&#8221; line item in the statement of comprehensive income. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">If a financial asset fails to meet any of the above conditions to be measured at amortized cost, it is measured at fair value through profit or loss. These financial assets are initially recognized at fair value and the costs of the transaction incurred are recognized as expenses in net income in the statement of comprehensive income. Changes in the fair value and results from the sale of these assets are recognized in the &#8220;Net financial results&#8221; line item in the statement of comprehensive income. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The purchase and sale of financial assets are recognized at the date in which the Group undertakes to purchase or sell those assets. The Group reclassifies financial assets only when the business model used to manage such assets changes. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Financial liabilities are initially recognized at fair value less costs of the transaction incurred and are subsequently measured at amortized cost using the effective interest rate method. Interest on debt instruments is recognized in the &#8220;Net financial results&#8221; line item in the statement of comprehensive income, except for interest that is capitalized. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In general, the Group uses the transaction price to determine the fair value of a financial instrument on initial recognition. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Impairment of financial assets </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Group evaluates the impairment of its financial assets measured at amortized cost using the expected credit loss model, recognizing in profit or loss for the period the amount of change in the expected credit losses during the lifetime of the financial asset, as an impairment gain or loss in the &#8220;Selling expenses&#8221; line item in the statement of comprehensive income, and applying the simplified approach allowed under IFRS 9 &#8220;Financial instruments&#8221; for trade receivables. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Under IFRS 9, expected credit losses are estimated by preparing a matrix based on maturity tranches, grouping the financial assets by type of customer: i) related parties; ii) public sector and iii) private sector. These groups are subsequently divided into sub-groups based on special characteristics indicative of the repayment capacity, such as i) payment defaults; ii) existence of guarantees; and iii) existence of a legal proceeding already initiated or in process of initiation for collection purposes, among others. Once each group is defined, an expected credit loss rate is assigned, which is calculated on the basis of the historical payment performance adjusted to current economic conditions and forecasts of future economic conditions. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Derecognition and offsetting </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Financial assets are derecognized when the rights to receive cash flows from such investments and the risks and benefits related to their ownership have expired or have been transferred. </div></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelection_111997092" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111997092_1"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_49" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_50"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_50" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_51"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_51" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_52"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: .83em;margin-top : 1.67em;margin-bottom : 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation></ix:continuation><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111997092_1" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111997092_2"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_52" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_53"><ix:exclude>

<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">BASIS OF PREPARATION OF THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (cont.) </div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_55" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_56"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111997092_2"><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Financial liabilities are derecognized when they have extinguished, i.e. when the obligation has been paid or cancelled, or has expired. In addition, the Group will account for an exchange of financial instruments with substantially different terms as an extinguishment of the original financial liability, recognizing a new financial liability. Similarly, the Group will account for a substantial modification in the current terms of a financial liability as an extinguishment of the financial liability and the recognition of a new financial liability. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Financial assets and liabilities offset each other when there is a legally enforceable right to set off such assets and liabilities and there is an intention to settle them on a net basis, or to realize the asset and settle the liability simultaneously. </div></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForMeasuringInventories" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" escape="true" id="ixv-30362"><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.b.8) Inventories </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Inventories are valued at the lower of cost and net realizable value. Cost includes costs of purchase (less trade discounts, rebates and other similar items), costs of conversion and other costs, which have been incurred in bringing the inventories to their present location and condition for their sale according to the nature of the asset. The net realizable value is the estimated selling price in the ordinary course of business less costs to sell. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In the case of refined products, costs are allocated in proportion to the selling price of such products (isomargin method) due to the difficulty of recognizing the production costs for each product on an individual basis. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Group assesses the net realizable value of inventories at the end of each period, charging the corresponding value adjustment to net income in the statement of comprehensive income when it exceeds their net realizable value, and reversing such adjustment when the circumstances that caused it change. </div></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForCashAndCashEquivalentsExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" escape="true" id="ixv-30368"><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.b.9) Cash and cash equivalents </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In the statement of cash flows, cash and cash equivalents include cash in hand, demand deposits with banks and other short-term highly liquid investments with original maturities of up to 3 months. They do not include bank overdrafts, which are presented as loans. </div></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForIssuedCapitalExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" escape="true" id="ixv-30372"><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.b.10) Shareholder&#8217;s equity </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The &#8220;Capital&#8221; and &#8220;Treasury shares&#8221; accounts are made up of shares of common stock held at nominal value. The difference between the subscribed amount of capital increases and the nominal value of issued shares is presented in the &#8220;Issuance premiums&#8221; account. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">When the Company buys its own shares to comply with share-based benefit plans to be settled with equity instruments, the cost incurred is presented in the &#8220;Acquisition cost of treasury shares&#8221; account. The difference between such cost incurred and the amount accrued from share-based benefit plans presented in the &#8220;Share-based benefit plans&#8221; account, is presented in the &#8220;Share trading premium&#8221; account (see Notes 30 and 37). </div></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_56" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_57"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_57" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_58"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_58" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_59"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: .83em;margin-top : 1.67em;margin-bottom : 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation></div></div></div> <div><div><div style="line-height:normal;background-color:white;display: inline;"><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_59" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_60"><ix:exclude>

<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">BASIS OF PREPARATION OF THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (cont.) </div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_62" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_63"><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForSharebasedPaymentTransactionsExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" escape="true" id="ixv-30435"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.b.11) Share-based benefit plans </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Group maintains share-based benefit plans with the characteristics mentioned in Note 37. Such plans are recorded in accordance with the guidelines set out in IFRS 2 &#8220;Share-based Payments&#8221;. </div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:2%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">-</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">Equity-settled share-based payment transactions are recognized as a straight-line expense over the period of service, based on the Group&#8217;s estimate of the number of equity instruments that will finally be granted considering their fair value at the grant date, with an offsetting credit entry in the &#8220;Share-based benefit plans&#8221; account in the statement of changes in shareholders&#8217; equity. At the end of each period, the Group reviews its estimate according to the number of equity instruments it expects will be granted based on the grant conditions specified under the respective benefit plan. </div></td></tr></table><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:2%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">-</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">Cash-settled share-based payment transactions are recognized as a straight-line expense over the period of service based on the Group&#8217;s estimate of the number of equity instruments assigned with an offsetting entry in the &#8220;Bonuses and incentives provision&#8221; account in the &#8220;Salaries and social security&#8221; line item in the statement of financial position, measured at fair value. Changes in the fair value of the liability are recognized in net income in the statement of comprehensive income. </div></td></tr></table></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForRecognitionOfRevenue" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" escape="true" id="ixv-30453"><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.b.12) Revenues </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Revenues from contracts with customers </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Under IFRS 15 &#8220;Revenues from Contracts with Customers&#8221;, the Group identifies the main contracts with customers (see Note 24) and assesses the goods and services involved in them to determine the performance obligations and their classification into obligations that are satisfied at a point in time and over time. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In contracts related to the sale of goods, revenue is recognized when control of the goods is transferred to the end customer, which occurs when the physical possession of the goods is transferred at the point of delivery based on the contractual terms of the agreements. When the performance obligation is satisfied at a given point in time, the Group recognizes as revenue the transaction price, which is the amount of consideration to which it expects to be entitled in exchange for those goods based on the selling price of each good. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Service contracts and construction contracts establish performance obligations that are satisfied over time. In the case of service contracts, revenue is recognized upon the effective provision of such services and in accordance with the respective contractual clauses. In the case of construction contracts, revenue is recognized by measuring the degree of progress towards complete satisfaction, where such satisfaction may be reliably measured using the input method as the most appropriate method based on the contractual terms of the agreements and considering the final estimated margin of each work and its degree of progress by the end of the period. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Additionally, and in accordance with the requirements of IFRS 15, revenues are broken down into the following categories: (i)&#160;type of good or service; (ii)&#160;sales channels, and (iii)&#160;target market, according to the reported business segments (see Notes 5 and 24). </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Income from Government incentive programs </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Under IAS 20 &#8220;Accounting for Government Grants and Disclosure of Government Assistance&#8221;, grants awarded by the National Government are recognized at fair value when there is reasonable assurance that the grants will be received and that the conditions attached to the grant will be complied with. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Income from National Government grants are disclosed in the &#8220;National Government incentives&#8221; line under the &#8220;Revenues&#8221; line item in the statement of comprehensive income. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In accordance with the requirements set out in IAS 20, the nature and characteristics of National Government grants are described in Notes 35 and 36. </div></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_63" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_64"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; <td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">BASIS OF PREPARATION OF THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (cont.) </div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_69" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_70"><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:DescriptionOfAccountingPolicyForAssetsOrDisposalGroupsAndRelatedLiabilitiesClassifiedAsHeldForSaleAndDiscontinuedOperationsExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" escape="true" id="ixv-30522"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.b.13) Non-current assets held for sale </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Non-current assets (or disposal group) classified as held for sale are measured at the lower of carrying amount and fair value less costs to sell. Immediately prior to the classification of a non-current asset (or disposal group) as held for sale, the carrying amount of the non-current asset (or disposal group) is measured in accordance with applicable IFRS, including IAS 36 &#8220;Impairment of assets&#8221;. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Non-current assets (or disposal group) are classified as held for sale if their carrying amount will be recovered through a sale or disposition transaction rather than through continuing use. In order to reach that conclusion, the Company analyze the substance of the transaction considering whether there has been a transfer of all risks and rewards (including the provision for hydrocarbon wells abandonment obligations). This condition is regarded as met only when the sale or disposition transaction is highly probable and the non-current asset (or disposal group) is available for immediate sale in its current condition. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As provided for in the IFRS 5 &#8220;Non-current assets held for sale and discontinued operations&#8221;, for the sale transaction to be highly probable the appropriate level of the Company&#180;s Management must be committed to a plan to dispose the asset (or disposal group) and an active program to locate a buyer and complete the plan must have been initiated. Further, the asset (or disposal group) must be actively marketed for sale at a price that is reasonable in relation to its current fair value. In addition, the sale transaction should be expected to qualify for recognition as a completed disposal within 1 year from the date of classification, except as permitted by IFRS 5, and actions required to complete the plan should indicate that is unlikely that significant changes to the plan will be made or that the plan will be withdrawn. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Group considers there is an impairment loss indicator under IAS 36 when a non-current asset (or disposal group) meets all the requirements to be classified as held for sale of the IFRS 5 before the approval of issuance of the financial statements (but not at the end of the period corresponding to such financial statements), and the carrying amount of such non-current asset (or disposal group) exceeds its fair value less costs of disposal. In this case, the Group is required to perform an impairment review of such non-current asset (or disposal group) separately from its CGU and, if necessary, an impairment loss is recognized in accordance with IAS 36. </div></ix:nonNumeric><ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DisclosureOfChangesInAccountingPoliciesExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" escape="true" continuedAt="TextSelection_111992395" id="ixv-30529"><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.b.14) New standards issued </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As required by IAS 8 &#8220;Accounting policies, changes in accounting estimates and errors&#8221;, below is a summary of the standards and interpretations issued by the IASB: </div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<td colspan="5" style="vertical-align:top"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">NOTES TO THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</div></div><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 1pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">AS OF DECEMBER 31, 2023, 2022 AND 2021</div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_74" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_75"><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_75" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_76"><ix:exclude>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">

<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">BASIS OF PREPARATION OF THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (cont.) </div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_76" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_77"><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Amendments to IAS 8 - Definition of accounting estimates </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In February 2021, the IASB issued amendments to IAS 8, related to the definition of accounting estimates, effective for fiscal years beginning on or after January&#160;1, 2023. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The amendments include the definition of the concept of accounting estimates in order to help entities to distinguish between accounting policies and accounting estimates - as the previous definition was interrelated to the definition of accounting policy and could lead to an error - defining accounting estimates as &#8220;monetary amounts in financial statements that are subject to measurement uncertainty&#8221;. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The IASB clarifies that changes in accounting estimates are accounted for prospectively, and if such changes are based both on new information that was not available when the previous measurements were made, as well as changes affecting the variables used in such estimate, they should not be treated as the correction of an error. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The implementation of the modifications mentioned above has not had any material effects on the Group&#8217;s consolidated financial statements. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Amendments to IAS 12 - Deferred tax related to assets and liabilities arising from a single transaction </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On May 2021, the IASB issued amendments to IAS 12 &#8220;Income Tax&#8221; related to the initial recognition of the deferred tax in transactions in which an asset and a liability are simultaneously recognized, which are applicable to fiscal years beginning on or after January&#160;1, 2023. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The amendments introduce an exception to the initial recognition exemption, with specifications on how entities should account for the income tax and the deferred tax in transactions in which the initial recognition of assets and liabilities give rise, at the same time, to equal amounts of taxable and deductible temporary differences. Therefore, in transactions where an asset and a liability are recognized, for example in relation to leases and abandonment or decommissioning obligations, the deferred tax generated by such transactions should be recognized. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Group has made the break-down of deferred tax assets and liabilities arising from Right-of-use assets and Lease liabilities, following the implementation of the aforementioned amendments. Also, the comparative information for fiscal year ended December&#160;31, 2022 and 2021 has been restated in compliance with IAS 12 amendments (see Note 17). However, this had no effect on initial retained earnings. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Amendments to IAS 12 - International Tax Reform - Pillar Two Model Rules </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In May 2023, the IASB issued amendments to IAS 12 related to the Pillar Two Model Rules of the International Tax Reform (&#8220;Reform&#8221;) developed by the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (&#8220;OECD&#8221;), which are applicable to fiscal years beginning on or after January&#160;1, 2023. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">These amendments introduce a temporary exception to the requirements of IAS 12, allowing an entity not to recognize or disclose information about deferred taxes arising from the income tax effects of applying the Reform. Additionally, it requires certain additional disclosures in the annual financial statements. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As of the date of these consolidated financial statements, the implementation of the aforementioned modifications has had no effects as there is no tax regulatory framework relating to such Reform in the jurisdictions where the Group operates. However, the Group is monitoring possible future changes that might be observed in tax regulations. </div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

In this sense, the Group did not apply these IFRS and/or its modifications in advance. </div></ix:continuation></ix:continuation></div></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111992395_2" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111992395_3"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_77" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_78"><div></div></ix:continuation></ix:continuation></div><div><div style="line-height:normal;background-color:white;display: inline;"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111992395_3" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111992395_4"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_78" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_79"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_79" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_80"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_80" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_81"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: .83em;margin-top : 1.67em;margin-bottom : 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation></ix:continuation><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111992395_4" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111992395_5"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_81" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_82"><ix:exclude>

<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">BASIS OF PREPARATION OF THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (cont.) </div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_84" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_85"><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Amendments to IFRS 10 and IAS 28 - Sale or contribution of assets between an investor and its associate or joint venture </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In September 2014, the IASB amended IFRS 10 and IAS 28 &#8220;Investments in associates and joint ventures&#8221; to clarify that in transactions involving a controlled entity, the extent of the profit or loss to be recognized in the financial statement depends on whether the sold or contributed controlled company is considered a business in accordance with IFRS 3 &#8220;Business combinations&#8221;. In December 2015, the IASB indefinitely postponed the application of such modifications. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Amendments to IAS 1 - Classification of liabilities </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In January 2020, the IASB issued amendments to IAS 1 in relation to the classification of liabilities into current and non-current, which are applicable to fiscal years beginning on or after January&#160;1, 2024. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The amendments clarify that liabilities classification in current and non-current: </div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:2%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">-</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">Must be based on existing rights at the end of the reporting period to defer settlement by at least twelve months and make explicit that only rights in place &#8220;at the end of the reporting period&#8221; should affect the classification of a liability. </div></td></tr></table>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">Is unaffected by expectations about whether an entity will exercise its right to defer settlement of a liability. </div></td></tr></table>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">

<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">-</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">That settlement refers to the transfer to the counterparty of cash, equity instruments, other assets or services. </div></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As of the date of issuance of these consolidated financial statements, the Group anticipates that the implementation of these amendments will have no significant impact on its financial statements. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Amendments to IFRS 16 - Leases </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In September 2022, the IASB issued amendments to IFRS 16 related to the measurement of leases in sale and leaseback transactions, as it failed to specify how to measure those leases after initial recognition, which are applicable to fiscal years beginning on or after January&#160;1, 2024. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Pursuant to this amendment to IFRS 16, a seller-lessee is required to measure lease liabilities arising from a sale and leaseback transaction without recognizing a gain or loss for the right-of-use it retains, and is not prevented from recognizing a gain or loss for the total or partial termination of the lease. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As of the date of issuance of these consolidated financial statements, the Group anticipates that the application of the amendments mentioned above will not significantly affect its financial statements. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Amendments to IAS 1 - Non-current liabilities with covenants </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On October 2022 the IASB issued amendments to IAS 1 in relation to the classification of non-current liabilities with covenants, which are applicable retroactively to fiscal years beginning on or after January&#160;1, 2024. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The amendments clarify that the classification of loans agreements with covenants as non-current liabilities may be affected when an entity is required to comply with such covenants on or before the date of the reporting period, even if the covenant is evaluated later. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In addition, certain additional requirements are incorporated related to the disclosure of information in notes, as this will allow financial statement users to understand the risk that non-current liabilities might fall due in the 12 months following the reporting period. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As of the date of issuance of these consolidated financial statements, the Group anticipates that the implementation of the aforementioned amendments will not have a significant impact on its financial statements, except for additional disclosures supplementing the information that is being reported. </div></ix:continuation></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111992395_5" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111992395_6"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_85" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_86"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; <td colspan="5" style="vertical-align:top"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">NOTES TO THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</div></div><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 1pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">AS OF DECEMBER 31, 2023, 2022 AND 2021</div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_89" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_90"><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_90" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_91"><ix:exclude>

<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">BASIS OF PREPARATION OF THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (cont.) </div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_91" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_92"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111992395_7"><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Amendments to IAS 7 and IFRS 7 - Supplier finance arrangements </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In May 2023, the IASB issued amendments to IAS 7 &#8220;Statement of cash flows&#8221; and IFRS 7 &#8220;Financial instruments: Disclosures&#8221; related to supplier finance arrangements, which are applicable to fiscal years beginning on or after January&#160;1, 2024. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">These amendments introduce new disclosure requirements of qualitative and quantitative information in the annual financial statements related to the mentioned supplier finance arrangements, such as contractual terms, carrying amounts of financial liabilities, settlements made and/or maturity dates, among others. The amendments do not require comparative information disclosure. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As of the date of issuance of these consolidated financial statements, the Group anticipates that the implementation of the amendments will not have a significant impact on its financial statements, except for certain additional disclosures in notes that complement the information currently presented. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Amendments to IAS 21 - Lack of exchangeability </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In August 2023, the IASB issued amendments to IAS 21 related to the methodology to be applied where there is a lack of exchangeability between two currencies, which are applicable for reporting periods beginning on or after January&#160;1, 2025. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">These amendments eliminate the applicable methodology described in IAS 21 where there was a temporary lack of exchangeability between two currencies, and introduce the definition of exchangeability between currencies and an analysis approach that requires each entity to identify whether a currency is exchangeable into another currency for each specific purpose for which such currency would be obtained following a series of parameters, such as an assessment of whether the currency is obtained within an ordinary administrative period, the ability to obtain said currency, among others. Once the absence of exchangeability between two currencies has been identified, the exchange rate should be estimated to represent that which would be obtained in an orderly transaction between market participants and which reflects economic conditions. These amendments do not specify a methodology for estimating the exchange rate to be used, which must be developed by each entity. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Additionally, these amendments incorporate disclosure requirements such as a description of the restrictions giving rise to the absence of exchangeability, a qualitative and quantitative description of the transactions involved, the types of exchange rates used and their estimation method, a description of the risks to which the entity is exposed due to the absence of exchangeability, among others. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As of the date of issuance of these consolidated financial statements, the Group is evaluating the effects of implementing these amendments. </div></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DisclosureOfAccountingJudgementsAndEstimatesExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" escape="true" continuedAt="TextSelection_111997192" id="ixv-30837"><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.c) Significant estimates and key sources of estimation uncertainty </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In preparing the financial statements at a certain date, the Group is required to make estimates and assessments affecting the amount of assets and liabilities recorded and the contingent assets and liabilities disclosed at such date, as well as income and expenses recognized in the fiscal year or period. Actual future profit (loss) may differ from the estimates and assessments made at the date of preparation of these consolidated financial statements. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The assumptions relating to the future and other sources of uncertainty about the estimates made for the preparation of these consolidated financial statements are described below: </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Oil and natural gas reserves </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Estimating oil and natural gas reserves is an integral part of the Group&#8217;s decision-making process. Oil and natural gas reserves are estimated using geological and engineering data, which implies a degree of uncertainty and depends on certain factors, assumptions and variables used in such estimation, some of which are beyond the Group&#8217;s control. The volume of oil and natural gas reserves, which is directly associated with projects, investments and business plans, is used to calculate depreciations, as well as to assess the recoverability of Upstream assets. </div><div style="margin-top:4pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Group makes estimates and assumptions related to oil and natural gas reserves in accordance with the rules and regulations set out in Rule 4-10 (a) of Regulation S-X of the SEC for the oil and natural gas industry. </div></ix:nonNumeric></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelection_111997192" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111997192_1"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_92" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_93"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_93" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_94"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_94" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_95"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: .83em;margin-top : 1.67em;margin-bottom : 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation></ix:continuation><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111997192_1" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111997192_2"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_95" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_96"><ix:exclude>

<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">BASIS OF PREPARATION OF THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (cont.) </div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_98" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_99"><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Provisions </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Group&#8217;s legal or assumed obligations are recognized, measured and disclosed in compliance with IAS 37 &#8220;Provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets&#8221;. Provisions include both obligations whose occurrence does not depend on future events (as the provision for environmental liabilities and the provision for hydrocarbon wells abandonment obligations), as well as obligations whose fulfillment depends on the occurrence of a future event that is beyond the Group&#8217;s control (as the provision for lawsuits and contingencies). </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Except for the provision for hydrocarbon wells abandonment obligations and the provision for environmental liabilties whose disbursement dates are estimated on the basis of work plans, the non-current provision for lawsuits and contingencies, given the nature of the items included, it is not possible to reasonably estimate a specific schedule for the respective disbursement dates. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In relation to the provision for lawsuits and contingencies, the final outcome of complaints, claims and litigation, as well as the category assigned by the Group to a given matter may differ, since estimates are based on the interpretation of rules, contracts, opinions and assessments of the amount of damages. Therefore, any change in the circumstances related to this type of contingencies and the strategy defined in each case might have a significant effect on the provision recognized for lawsuits and contingencies or the category assigned by the Group. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In relation to the provision for environmental liabilties, the Group is subject to several environmental protection laws and regulations imposing penalties for pollution cleanup costs and environmental damages resulting from its operations. The Company believes that the Group&#8217;s operations substantially comply with the laws and regulations currently in force relating to environmental protection, as they have been historically interpreted and applied. However, the Company regularly conducts studies in order to gain deeper knowledge of the environmental damage of certain geographic areas where the Group operates, in order to establish their status and any necessary remediation. Until such studies are completed and assessed, the Group cannot estimate the additional costs that will need to be incurred, if any. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In relation to the provision for hydrocarbon wells abandonment obligations, considering the number of wells not yet abandoned, as well as the complexity with respect to several geographic areas where the wells are located, current costs incurred for hydrocarbon wells abandonment are used for estimating future costs, which constitute the best estimate for the provision for hydrocarbon wells abandonment obligations. Changes in laws or regulations related to the abandonment of hydrocarbon wells, in costs, in the useful lives of hydrocarbon wells, in discount rates and/or in the applied technologies have an effect on the reassessment of these estimates. The accounting policies applied to the provision for hydrocarbon wells abandonment obligations are outlined in Note 2.b.3). </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Group cannot anticipate the legislation or regulations that will be enacted in the future or how future regulations will be administered, which, like the studies in progress, could materially affect the results of operations in the long term. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In relation to certain provisions, contingent liabilities and contingent assets, the Group, in accordance with the exemption contemplated under IAS 37, has decided not to disclose certain critical information that could seriously adversely affect the Group in third-party claims. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Income tax and deferred taxes </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The income tax expense for the fiscal year includes both current and deferred income tax expenses, which are determined and disclosed in compliance with IAS 12. The Group regularly assesses the positions taken in tax returns regarding situations in which tax regulations are subject to interpretations and makes provisions where appropriate based on the amounts expected to be paid to tax authorities. </div></ix:continuation></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111997192_2" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111997192_3"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_99" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_100"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_100" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_101"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_101" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_102"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: .83em;margin-top : 1.67em;margin-bottom : 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation></ix:continuation></div></div></div> <div><div><div style="line-height:normal;background-color:white;display: inline;"><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111997192_3" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111997192_4"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_102" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_103"><ix:exclude>

<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">2.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">BASIS OF PREPARATION OF THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS (cont.) </div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_105" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_106"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111997192_4"><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Income tax expense is calculated based on the tax laws enacted, or substantially enacted by the end of each period in the countries where the Group operates and generates taxable income. In addition, other factors are taken into account, such as the evaluation of the options established by such laws and their regulations, the interpretations associated with tax treatments for transactions and/or events not expressly provided for under current tax laws, analyzing if the tax authority might accept an uncertain tax treatment, and estimates related to the timing and realization of deferred taxes, such as the expected effective tax rate at such date. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Deferred tax assets recognize tax loss carryforwards to the extent their offsetting through future taxable income is probable. In assessing the recognition of deferred tax assets, the Group considers the anticipated reversal of deferred tax liabilities, projections of future taxable income and tax planning strategies. Assumptions regarding the generation of future taxable income depend on the Group&#8217;s estimates of future cash flows. To the extent future cash flows and taxable income differ significantly from the estimates, the Group&#8217;s capacity to realize the recorded net deferred tax assets might be affected. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Also, changes in tax regulations and/or their interpretations may affect such estimates. See Note 17. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Provision for Impairment of property, plant and equipment, intangible assets and right-of-use assets </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The main guidelines used in estimating the recoverable amount of property, plant and equipment, intangible assets and right-of-use assets are described in Note 2.b.5). </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Measuring the recoverable amount of an asset involves the Group&#8217;s estimates on uncertain issues, such as inflation and deflation effects on costs, the discount rate, the volume of reserves , the distribution over time of production levels associated with such reserves and future prices of products, including the outlooks on supply and demand conditions in the local and international markets for oil, natural gas and refined products, which affect selling prices considered in cash flow projections. The Group&#8217;s estimates are subject to changes as new information becomes available. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As regards measurement of CGUs that group assets of fields with oil and natural gas reserves, cash flow projections are used covering the economically productive life of the fields, limited by the termination of exploitation concessions, agreements or investment contracts. Cash flow projections are determined using the Group&#8217;s best estimate of oil and natural gas future selling prices, volumes of reserves, the distribution over time of production levels associated with such reserves, future investments, production costs, field depletion rates, the supply and demand in local and international markets, the current legislation and contractual conditions, among other factors. Likewise, cash flow forecasts of unproved reserves are weighted by risk factors. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Cash flow projections of CGUs that group assets other than those mentioned in the previous paragraph are estimated based, among other things, on the expected evolution of sales, unit contribution margins, fixed costs, variable costs and investment levels, in line with the outlooks contemplated in business plans and taking into account the current status of each group of assets. Likewise, cash flow projections until the end of an asset&#8217;s useful life are estimated by extrapolating cash flow projections based on budgets or forecasts, using the appropriate discount rates. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The prices considered in cash flow projections are based on a combination of projections available in the markets where the Group operates and taking into account the specific circumstances that could affect the different products commercialized by the Group. In general, the Group does not consider temporarily low (or high) prices or margins as an impairment indication (or reversal of an impairment loss). Impairment assessment mainly reflects long-term prices that are consistent with intermediate points between the maximum and minimum ranges observed in the market and that are within the range of price forecasts published by third-party experts of the oil and gas industry and government agencies. Natural gas prices correspond to the average weighted price per basin and sales channel, determined according to current contracts and regulations and the market supply and demand forecast. </div></ix:continuation></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_106" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_107"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_107" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_108"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_108" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_109"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: .83em;margin-top : 1.67em;margin-bottom : 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_109" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993502_110"><ix:exclude>

<td id="fintoc804823_9" style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">3.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">ACQUISITIONS AND DISPOSALS </div></div></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Dissolution of the companies YPF Holdings, Inc., YCLH Holdings, Inc. and YPF Services USA Corp. </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On January&#160;5, 2024, the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware approved, effective from December&#160;28, 2023, the dissolution of YPF Holdings, Inc., YCLH Holdings, Inc. (subsidiary <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PercentageOfOwnershipOfYPFHoldingsIncInThesubsidiary" contextRef="PAsOn01_05_2024_ApprovalByTheSecretaryOfStateOfTheStateOfDelawareForTheDissolutionOfSubsidiaryCompaniesMemberifrsfullNonadjustingEventsAfterReportingPeriodAxis_YCLHHoldingsIncMemberifrsfullSignificantInvestmentsInSubsidiariesAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-117263">100</ix:nonFraction>% controlled by YPF Holdings, Inc.) and YPF Services USA Corp. </div></ix:nonNumeric><div style="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div><ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:DisclosureFinancialRiskManagementExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" escape="true" continuedAt="TextSelection_111994427" id="ixv-31059">

<td id="fintoc804823_10" style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">4.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">FINANCIAL RISK MANAGEMENT </div></div></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Group&#8217;s activities expose it to a variety of financial risks: Market risk (including exchange rate risk, interest rate risk, and price risk), liquidity risk and credit risk. Within the Group, risk management functions are conducted in relation to financial risks associated to financial instruments to which the Group is exposed during a certain period or as of a specific date. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The following provides a description of the principal risks that could have a material adverse effect on the Group&#8217;s strategy in each operations center, performance, results of operations and financial condition. The risks facing the businesses, set out below, do not appear in any particular order of potential materiality or probability of occurrence. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The sensitivity analysis of market risks included below are based on a change in one factor while holding all other factors constant. In practice this is unlikely to occur, and changes in some of the factors may be correlated, for example, changes in interest rate and changes in foreign currency rates. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">This sensitivity analysis provides only a limited, point-in-time view. The actual impact on the Group&#8217;s financial instruments may differ significantly from the impact shown in the sensitivity analysis. </div><div style="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">&#8226;</div></div></td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: ARIAL; font-size: 9pt; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"></div><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">Market risk management </div></div></div></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The market risk to which the Group is exposed is the possibility that the valuation of the Group&#8217;s financial assets and financial liabilities as well as certain expected cash flows may be affected by changes in exchange rates, interest rates or certain other price variables. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The following is a description of these risks as well as a detail of the extent to which the Group is exposed and a sensitivity analysis of possible changes in each of the relevant market variables. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Exchange rate risk </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The value of financial assets and liabilities denominated in a currency different from the Company&#8217;s functional currency is subject to variations resulting from fluctuations in exchange rates. Since YPF&#8217;s functional currency is the U.S. dollar, the currency that generates the greatest exposure is the Peso (the Argentine legal currency). </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Likewise, based on the restrictions ordered by the BCRA for access to the Foreign Exchange Markets, the Group maintains an active strategy in the management of liquidity (see Note 35.g)). </div></ix:nonNumeric></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelection_111994427" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111994427_1"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111994427_1" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111994427_2"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111994427_2" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111994427_3"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: .83em;margin-top : 1.67em;margin-bottom : 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation></div></div></div> <div><div><div style="line-height:normal;background-color:white;display: inline;"><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111994427_3" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111994427_4"><ix:exclude>

In 2023, oil deliveries were negotiated between producers and refiners or sellers. </div><div style="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: ARIAL; font-size: 9pt; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">Liquidity risk management </div></div></div></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Liquidity risk is associated with the possibility of a mismatch between the need of funds to meet short, medium or long-term obligations. The Group intends to align the maturity profile of its financial debt to be related to its ability to generate enough cash to finance the projected expenditures for each year. As of December&#160;31, 2023, the availability of liquidity reached <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:AmountAvailableForLiquidity" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2023_LiquidityRiskMemberifrsfullTypesOfRisksAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-117298">1,123</ix:nonFraction>, considering cash of <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:Cash" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2023_LiquidityRiskMemberifrsfullTypesOfRisksAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-117299">230</ix:nonFraction> and other liquid financial assets of <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:OtherCashAndCashEquivalents" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2023_LiquidityRiskMemberifrsfullTypesOfRisksAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-117300">893</ix:nonFraction>. Additionally, the Group has other investments freely available for <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:OtherInvestmentsFreelyAvailable" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2023_LiquidityRiskMemberifrsfullTypesOfRisksAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-117301">217</ix:nonFraction> included in &#8220;Investments in financial assets&#8221; line item in the statement of financial position (see Note 14). Uncommitted bank credit lines together with the capital market constitute an important source of funding. Likewise, YPF has the ability to issue debt under the Frequent Issuer Regime. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Based on the restrictions established by the BCRA for access to the Exchange Market to maturities of principal amounts of offshore debts and the issuance of debt securities denominated in foreign currency scheduled until December 31, 2023, all the provisions issued were fulfilled by the Group. See Notes 21 and 35.g). </div></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111994427_14" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111994427_15"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111994427_15" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111994427_16"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111994427_16" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111994427_17"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: .83em;margin-top : 1.67em;margin-bottom : 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation></div></div></div> <div><div><div style="line-height:normal;background-color:white;display: inline;"><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111994427_17" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111994427_18"><ix:exclude>
