<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">(1)</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 6pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: left; line-height: normal;">Includes the contractual, undiscounted cash flows associated to the financial liabilities given that they do not differ significantly from their face values. </div></td></tr></table></ix:nonNumeric><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Most of the Group&#8217;s loans contain market-standard covenants for contracts of this nature, which include financial covenants in respect of the Group&#8217;s leverage ratio and debt service coverage ratio, and events of defaults triggered by materially adverse judicial judgements, among others. See Notes 16, 32 and 33. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Under the terms of the loan agreements and NO, if the Group breached a covenant or if it could not remedy it within the stipulated period, it would default, a situation that would limit its liquidity and, given that the majority of its loans contain cross default provisions, it could result in an early enforceability of its obligations. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Group monitors compliance with covenants on a quarterly basis. As of December&#160;31, 2023, the Group is in compliance with its covenants. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">It should be noted that, under the terms and conditions of the loans that our subsidiary Metrogas has taken, the interest coverage ratio would not have been complied with, which could have accelerated the maturities of these financial liabilities. However, the financial creditors formally accepted to waive Metrogas from complying with the contractual obligation related to such financial ratio, as of December&#160;31, 2023. </div><div style="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">&#8226;</div></div></td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: ARIAL; font-size: 9pt; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">Credit risk management </div></div></div></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Credit risk is defined as the possibility of a third party not complying with its contractual obligations, thus negatively affecting results of operations of the Group. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Credit risk in the Group is measured and controlled on an individual customer basis. The Group has its own systems to conduct a permanent evaluation of credit performance and the determination of risk limits of all of its customers and to third parties, in line with best practices using for such end internal customer records and external data sources. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Financial instruments that potentially expose the Group to a credit concentration risk consist primarily of cash and cash equivalents, investments in financial assets, trade receivables and other receivables. The Group invests excess cash primarily in high liquid investments with financial institutions with a strong credit rating both in Argentina and abroad. In the normal course of business and based on ongoing credit evaluations to its customers, the Group provides credit to its customers and certain related parties. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Likewise, the charge for doubtful trade losses is charged to net income in the statement of comprehensive income, based on specific information regarding its clients. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Provisions for doubtful accounts are measured by the criteria mentioned in Note 2.b.7). </div><ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DisclosureOfCreditRiskExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" escape="true" id="ixv-31888"><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The maximum exposure to credit risk of the Group of December&#160;31, 2023 based on the type of its financial instruments and without excluding the amounts covered by several types of guarantees is set forth below: </div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<td colspan="5" style="vertical-align:top"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">NOTES TO THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</div></div><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 1pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">AS OF DECEMBER 31, 2023, 2022 AND 2021</div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993511_3" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993511_4"><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993511_4" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993511_5"><ix:exclude>

<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">5.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">BUSINESS SEGMENT INFORMATION (cont.) </div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993511_5" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993511_6"><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">&#8226;</div></div></td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: ARIAL; font-size: 9pt; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">Downstream </div></div></div></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Downstream segment performs activities relating to: (i)&#160;crude oil refining and petrochemical production; (ii)&#160;logistics related to the transportation of crude oil to refineries and the transportation and distribution of refined and petrochemical products to be marketed at the different sales channels; (iii)&#160;commercialization of crude oil and refined and petrochemical products obtained from such processes; and (iv)&#160;commercialization of specialties for the agribusiness industry and of grains and their by-products. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Its revenues are derived primarily from the sale of crude oil, refined and petrochemical products, specialties for the agribusiness industry and grains and their by-products. These operations are performed through the businesses of B2C (Retail), B2B (Industries, Transportation, Aviation, Agro, Lubricants and Specialties), LPG, Chemicals, International Trade and Transportation and Sales to Companies. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">This segment incurs all costs related to the activities mentioned above, including the purchase of crude oil from the Upstream segment and third parties and the purchase of gasoline, propane and butane and natural gas to be consumed in the refinery and petrochemical industrial complexes from the Gas and Power segment. </div><div style="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">&#8226;</div></div></td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: ARIAL; font-size: 9pt; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">Gas and Power </div></div></div></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Gas and Power segment performs activities related to: (i)&#160;natural gas transportation to third parties and the Downstream segment, and its commercialization; (ii)&#160;commercial and technical operation of the LNG regasification terminals in Escobar and Bah&#237;a Blanca, by hiring regasification vessels; (iii)&#160;transportation, conditioning and processing of natural gas retained in plant for the separation and fractionation of gasoline, propane and butane; (iv)&#160;distribution of natural gas through our subsidiary Metrogas; and (v)&#160;the storage of the natural gas produced. Also, through our investments in associates and joint ventures, it undertakes activities related to: (i)&#160;separation of natural gas liquids and their fractionation, storage and transportation for the production of ethane, propane, butane and gasoline; (ii)&#160;generation of conventional thermal electric power and renewable energy; and (iii)&#160;production, storage, distribution and sale of fertilizers. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Its revenues are largely derived from the commercialization of natural gas as producers to third parties and the Downstream segment, the distribution of natural gas through our subsidiary Metrogas, the sale of gasoline, propane and butane to the Downstream segment and the provision of LNG regasification services. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">This segment incurs all costs related to the activities mentioned above, including the purchase of natural gas and natural gas retained in plant from the Upstream segment. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; margin-left:2%; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On January&#160;1, 2023, certain assets related to the production, storage, distribution and sale of fertilizers through the Profertil joint venture, which were formerly included in Downstream segment, were assigned to the Gas and Power segment. In addition, the comparative information for fiscal years ended December&#160;31, 2022 and 2021 has been restated. </div><div style="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 6pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: left; line-height: normal;">See Note 28. </div> </td> </tr> </table>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:6pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">(3)</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 6pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: left; line-height: normal;">See Note 21. </div> </td> </tr> </table> </ix:continuation> <div style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Fair value measurements </div></div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">IFRS 13 &#8220;Fair value measurement&#8221; defines the fair value of a financial instrument as the amount for which an asset could be exchanged, or a financial liability settled, between knowledgeable, independent parties in an arm&#8217;s length transaction. All financial instruments measured at fair value are assigned to one of the valuation hierarchy levels specified under IFRS 13 (as well as loans measured at amortized cost whose fair value is disclosed in &#8220;Fair value of financial assets and financial liabilities measured at amortized cost&#8221; section). This valuation hierarchy comprises 3 levels. </div> <div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:2%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">(i)</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">Level 1: The valuation is based on unadjusted quoted prices in active markets for identical financial assets or liabilities that the Group can refer to at the end of the period. A market is deemed active if transactions take place with sufficient frequency and in sufficient quantity for price information to be available on an ongoing basis. Since a quoted price in an active market is the most reliable indicator of fair value, this should always be used if available. Financial instruments assigned by the Group to this level comprise investments in listed mutual funds and public securities. </div> </td> </tr> </table> <div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:2%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">(ii)</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">Level 2: The fair value is determined by using valuation methods based on inputs directly or indirectly observable in the market. If the financial instrument concerned has a fixed contract period, the inputs used for valuation must be observable for the whole of this period. The Group has not valued financial instruments under this level. </div> </td> </tr> </table> <div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:2%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">(iii)</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">Level 3: The Group uses valuation techniques not based on inputs observable in the market. This is only permissible insofar as no market data is available. The inputs reflect the Group&#8217;s assumptions regarding the factors, which market players would consider in their pricing. The Group uses the best available information for this, including internal company data. The Group has not valued financial instruments under this level. </div> </td> </tr> </table></ix:continuation> </div> </div> </div> <ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993594_13" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993594_14"><div></div></ix:continuation> </div> <ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993594_14" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993594_15"><div> <div style="line-height:normal;background-color:white;display: inline;"> <ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude> <ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%"/></ix:exclude><ix:exclude> <div style="font-size: .83em;margin-top : 1.67em;margin-bottom : 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div> </ix:exclude></div> </div></ix:continuation> </div> <div><div><div style="line-height:normal;background-color:white;display: inline;"><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993594_15" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993594_16"><ix:exclude>

In general, it analyzes macroeconomic variables such as price indexes and currency devaluation, among others, and in particular, for the natural gas market, the demand volume to be covered and natural gas sales prices. </div> <div style="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In relation to the natural gas market, incentive schemes were established in recent years in order to increase the domestic production of natural gas. As of 2018 and 2019, an excess in the supply from the increased production on unconventional fields with respect to the domestic demand was observed at specific times of the year, an unusual situation in the past, which affected natural gas production due to the temporary shutdown of wells. This situation generated a reduction in natural gas sales price in the local market, which generated a drop in natural gas production due to the lack of incentives to develop projects. Consequently, on November&#160;16, 2020, the National Government approved the Plan GasAr 2020-2024 with the aim of making viable investments to increase the production of natural gas in all the country&#8217;s basins and satisfy the hydrocarbon needs of the local market. Subsequently and with the same objective, on November&#160;4, 2022, the National Government approved the Plan GasAr 2023-2028. The Group will continue analyzing the prospects for the variables mentioned above to further estimate their impact on expected cash flows. </div><div style="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On February&#160;29, 2024 (see Note 38) YPF&#8217;s Board of Directors resolved the disposal of certain groups of assets related to the Upstream business segment, mainly mature fields related to the CGU Oil, CGU Gas - Austral Basin and CGU Gas - Neuquina Basin and expects fair value less cost of disposal to be less than their carrying amount. The Company considers this to be an impairment loss indicator under IAS 36. Accordingly, the Company performed an impairment review separately from its CGU and recognized an impairment charge of property, plant and equipment of <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:ImpairmentLossRecognisedInProfitOrLossPropertyPlantAndEquipment" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023_CguOilCguGasAustralBasinAndCguGasNeuquinaBasinMemberifrsfullIndividualAssetsOrCashgeneratingUnitsAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-118421">1,782</ix:nonFraction> (<ix:nonFraction name="ypf:ImpairmentLossRecognisedInProfitOrLossPropertyPlantAndEquipmentNetOfTax" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023_CguOilCguGasAustralBasinAndCguGasNeuquinaBasinMemberifrsfullIndividualAssetsOrCashgeneratingUnitsAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-118422">1,158</ix:nonFraction> net of the income tax effect) as of December&#160;31, 2023, considering the net assets and recoverable value of each disposal group. </div><div style="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Considering, most of the transactions of oil and gas assets in Argentina during recent years are related to fields where the main targeted reservoirs are unconventional formations (specifically, the Vaca Muerta formation), and for the transactions that could be considered comparable to the assets evaluated in each disposal group, the publicly available information was insufficient to derive conclusions for a fair value in active markets for identical assets to those of each disposal group (Level 1), or inputs other than quoted prices included within Level 1 that are observable for the assets, either directly or indirectly (Level 2). </div><div style="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Accordingly, the recoverable value for each disposal group was determined applying an asset valuation technique commonly used in the oil and gas industry which is the Discounted Cash Flow Analysis technique. This valuation is considered to be Level 3 in the fair value hierarchy due to unobservable inputs used in the valuation, representing the fair value less costs of disposal measurement. </div><div style="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In estimating the discounted cash flows of the disposal groups, the Company worked closely with a third-party qualified independent valuer not related to the Group, with appropriate qualifications, to establish the appropriate valuation techniques and inputs to the model. </div></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111996213_25" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111996213_26"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111996213_26" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111996213_27"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111996213_27" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111996213_28"><ix:exclude> <div style="font-size: .83em;margin-top : 1.67em;margin-bottom : 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation> <div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111996213_28" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111996213_29"><ix:exclude>

<td colspan="5" style="vertical-align:top"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">NOTES TO THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</div></div><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 1pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">AS OF DECEMBER 31, 2023, 2022 AND 2021</div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation> <ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111996213_29" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111996213_30"><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111996213_30" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111996213_31"><ix:exclude>

<td style="width:2%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">8.</div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">PROPERTY, PLANT AND EQUIPMENT (cont.) </div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation> <ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111996213_31"><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">This valuation technique required projections of production, operating expenses, capital expenditures, hydrocarbon wells abandonment costs, royalties and taxes and the date of the termination of the concessions. The key assumptions to which the disposal groups recoverable amounts are most sensitive are production, crude oil and natural gas prices, discount rate and macroeconomic variables. Values for reserves were expressed in terms of future gross revenue, future net revenue, present value and considering a ten-year extension of the termination of certain concessions expiring in the near term. Future net revenue was calculated by deducting royalties paid in cash, operating expenses, capital expenditures and hydrocarbon wells abandonment costs, production taxes, and Argentine income taxes from future gross revenue. Operating expenses include field operating expenses, transportation and processing expenses, and an allocation of overhead that directly relates to production activities. Capital costs include drilling and completion costs, facilities costs, and field maintenance costs. Hydrocarbon wells abandonment costs are those costs associated with the removal of facilities, plugging of wells and reclamation and restoration associated with the abandonment. Present value was defined as future net revenue discounted at a discount rate post tax, which as of December&#160;31, 2023 was <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:DescriptionOfDiscountRatesUsedInCurrentEstimateOfValueInUse" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2023" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-118423">15</ix:nonFraction>%. </div><ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:DisclosureOfPropertyPlantAndEquipmentCostEvolutionExploratory" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" escape="true" id="ixv-46961"> <div style="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Set forth below is the cost evolution for the exploratory wells in evaluation stage as of the years ended on December&#160;31, 2023, 2022 and 2021: </div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

The termination of the contract with that company is based on: (a)&#160;the impossibility of YPF to receive the transportation service and of TGN to render such service, due to (i)&#160;the termination of the natural gas contract with SULGAS and AESU and (ii)&#160;the legal impossibility of assigning said contract to other shippers because of the regulations in effect, (b)&#160;the legal impossibility of TGN to render the transportation service on a firm basis because of certain changes in the legislation in force since 2004, and (c)&#160;the &#8220;<div style="font-style: normal; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-style:italic;display:inline;">teor&#237;a de la imprevisi&#243;n</div></div>&#8221; (doctrine of unforeseeability) available under Argentine law, when extraordinary events render a party&#8217;s obligations excessively burdensome. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">TGN notified YPF the termination of the transportation contract for YPF&#8217;s fault. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">TGN filed a complaint claiming compliance with the contract and payment of unpaid invoices from February&#160;20, 2007 to March&#160;20, 2009 totaling <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:NaturalGasTransportationContractAndPaymentOfUnpaidInvoices" contextRef="P02_20_2007To03_20_2009_TransportadoraDeGasDelNorteSaMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-119200">30</ix:nonFraction>. TGN then amended the complaint and claimed the payment of unpaid invoices (i)&#160;from April&#160;20, 2009 to June&#160;20, 2010 in the amount of <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:NaturalGasTransportationContractAndPaymentOfUnpaidInvoices" contextRef="P04_20_2009To06_20_2010_TransportadoraDeGasDelNorteSaMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-119201">31</ix:nonFraction>, (ii)&#160;from July&#160;20, 2010 to November&#160;20, 2010 in the amount of <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:NaturalGasTransportationContractAndPaymentOfUnpaidInvoices" contextRef="P07_20_2010To11_20_2010_TransportadoraDeGasDelNorteSaMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-119202">10</ix:nonFraction>, and (iii)&#160;from December&#160;6, 2010 to January&#160;4, 2011 in the amount of <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:NaturalGasTransportationContractAndPaymentOfUnpaidInvoices" contextRef="P12_06_2010To01_04_2011_TransportadoraDeGasDelNorteSaMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-119203">3</ix:nonFraction>. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">TGN also lodged a complaint for damages against YPF claiming the amount of <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:ClaimsAndBenefitsPaidNetOfReinsuranceRecovery" contextRef="P04_03_2013To04_03_2013_TransportadoraDeGasDelNorteSaMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-119204">142</ix:nonFraction>, plus interest and legal fees for the termination of the transportation contract. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Upon completion of the proceedings for discovery of evidence, on October&#160;16, 2020, the Lower Court rendered judgment, whereby it resolved: (i)&#160;to declare abstract the claim to comply the firm natural gas transportation contract (the &#8220;Contract&#8221;), filed by TGN; (ii)&#160;to partially grant the claim filed in the case for Contract performance, and order YPF to pay for unpaid invoices in an amount to be determined by the designated accounting expert at the stage of enforcement of judgment, plus interest and court fees; and (iii)&#160;to admit the claim for damages and order YPF to pay the amount of <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:ClaimsAndBenefitsPaidNetOfReinsuranceRecovery" contextRef="P02_16_2022To02_16_2022_TransportadoraDeGasDelNorteSaMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-119205">231</ix:nonFraction> plus interest and court fees. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On October&#160;22, 2020, YPF filed appeals against the lower court&#8217;s decision regarding the claim filed for contract performance and the claim for damages. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On February&#160;16, 2022, the Court of Appeals rendered judgment (i)&#160;confirming the lower court&#8217;s decision which ordered YPF to pay for unpaid invoices in the amount to be determined by the accounting expert designated at the stage of judgment enforcement; (ii)&#160;confirming that YPF was liable for damages in the amount of <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:ClaimsAndBenefitsPaidNetOfReinsuranceRecovery" contextRef="P02_16_2022To02_16_2022_TransportadoraDeGasDelNorteSaMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-119206">231</ix:nonFraction> plus interest, or its equivalent in Pesos at the selling exchange rate published by the BNA on the settlement date; (iii)&#160;reducing the applicable annual interest rate from <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:AnnualInterestRate" contextRef="P02_16_2022To02_16_2022_TopOfRangeMemberifrsfullRangeAxis_TransportadoraDeGasDelNorteSaMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-119207">6</ix:nonFraction>% to <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:AnnualInterestRate" contextRef="P02_16_2022To02_16_2022_BottomOfRangeMemberifrsfullRangeAxis_TransportadoraDeGasDelNorteSaMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-119208">4</ix:nonFraction>%; and (iv)&#160;imposing payment of appeal costs on defendant in the case for damages and shared payment in the case for contract performance. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On February&#160;21, 2022, YPF lodged an appeal requesting the correction and/or clarification of certain aspects in the judgment rendered by the Court of Appeal. On March&#160;7, 2022, the appeal filed by YPF for the correction and/or clarification of certain aspects in the judgment rendered by the Court of Appeal was favorably resolved. Additionally, on that date an extraordinary appeal was filed against the judgment rendered by the Court of Appeal, which was granted on April&#160;5, 2022 in relation to the federal issue raised and was denied in relation to the arbitrariness of the judgment rendered by the Court of Appeal, and a complaint appeal was filed in relation to this last aspect on April&#160;12, 2022. As of that date, the cases were under review at the CSJN in connection with the extraordinary and the complaint appeals that were filed. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On February&#160;3, 2023, YPF and TGN entered into a settlement agreement for the sole and total amount of <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:EstimatedFinancialEffectOfContingentLiabilities" contextRef="PAsOn02_03_2023_EnteringIntoSignificantCommitmentsOrContingentLiabilitiesMemberifrsfullNonadjustingEventsAfterReportingPeriodAxis_SettlementAgreementForTheAmountPayableInFourInstalmentsMemberYPFAgreementAxis_TransportadoraDeGasDelNorteSaMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-119209">190.6</ix:nonFraction> payable by YPF in 4 consecutive annual installments, starting in 2024 by which, without acknowledging facts or rights, TGN and YPF waived all claims they had or could have had against each other until that date, making abstract the extraordinary appeals and complaints filed with the CSJN. On February&#160;23, 2023, the settlement agreement was submitted to the CSJN requesting its homologation. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In April 2023, in compliance with the decision of the CSJN, the settlement agreement between YPF and TGN was filed with the Lower Court requesting its approval. On May&#160;5, 2023, the Lower Court approved said agreement. </div></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111992409_9" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111992409_10"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111992409_10" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111992409_11"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111992409_11" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111992409_12"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: .83em;margin-top : 1.67em;margin-bottom : 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation></div></div></div> <div><div><div style="line-height:normal;background-color:white;display: inline;"><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111992409_12" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111992409_13"><ix:exclude>

PROVISIONS (cont.)</ix:exclude> </div></div><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">16.a.3) Users and Consumers Association </div></div><div style="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Users and Consumers Association claims (originally against Repsol YPF S.A. before extending its claim to YPF) the reimbursement of the overprice allegedly charged to bottled LPG consumers from periods between years 1993 to 1997 and from 1997 to 2001. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On December&#160;28, 2015, the lower court rendered judgment admitting the claim for compensation from period between years 1993-1997 term filed by the Users and Consumers Association against YPF and ordered the Company to transfer the amount of <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:ProceedsFromTransferActivity" contextRef="P12_28_2015To12_28_2015_ComisionNacionalDeLaDefensaLaCompetenciaMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-119211">98</ix:nonFraction> plus interest (to be estimated by the expert witness in the settlement period) to the SE, to be allocated to the trust fund created under Law No.&#160;26,020. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The ruling rejects the claim for the items corresponding to the period 1997-2001, considering that YPF&#8217;s position in the domestic bulk LPG market had not been sufficiently proved. Furthermore, the ruling dismissed the complaint against Repsol S.A., as Repsol YPF S.A. had no equity interest in YPF, nor any other kind of relation with YPF from 1993 to 1997, period in which the plaintiffs claim YPF abused its dominant position. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Both parties filed an appeal against that decision, which was admitted with suspensive effect. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On December&#160;7, 2017, the Company was notified about the Court of Second Appeal&#8217;s judgment, which: (i)&#160;confirmed the claims for compensation for the 1993-1997 period; (ii)&#160;extends the Users and Consumers Association claim from period between years 1997 to 1999 period under the item &#8220;equity transfer of consumers to producers for the higher cost of LPG&#8221;, deferring the settlement related to the item to the execution stage of the judgment; and (iii)&#160;partially grants the appeal filed by the defendant with respect to the item &#8220;damage caused by lower or different energy consumption due to the higher cost of LPG&#8221;. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">It should be noted that the ruling confirmed by the Court of Second Appeals does not order YPF to pay the claimant the ultimately settled amount, but rather to transfer such funds to the SE for the funds to be allocated to a trust fund created by Law No.&#160;26,020, in order to expand the natural gas network in areas with lower resources according to the criteria established by the enforcement authority. The enforcement authority, within 6 months from the firm settlement of the judgment amount, must present the corresponding feasibility studies (Decree No.&#160;470/2015) together with a work plan beginning within 6 months from the presentation of the feasibility studies. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Finally, the Company filed an extraordinary appeal against the judgment of the Court of Appeals, which was sustained and the court file was submitted to the CSJN, the enforcement of the Court of Appeals&#8217; judgment still being suspended. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On June&#160;2, 2021, the CSJN forwarded the file to the National Attorney General&#8217;s Office for its opinion on the legal merits of the extraordinary appeal. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On April&#160;13, 2023, the National Attorney General&#8217;s Office issued an opinion recommending the CSJN to grant the extraordinary appeal lodged by YPF and to reverse the Court of Second Appeal&#8217;s judgment. As of the date of issuance of these consolidated financial statements, the extraordinary appeal has not been decided. </div><div style="margin-top: 10pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">16.a.4) Environmental claims </div></div><div style="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">

<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">&#8226;</div></div></td>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: ARIAL; font-size: 9pt; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">La Plata </div></div></div></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In relation to the operation of the refinery owned by YPF in La Plata, there are certain judicial claims, mostly filed by neighbors of the area seeking (i)&#160;compensation for damages arising from the alleged environmental contamination caused by the operation of the La Plata Refinery and (ii)&#160;the environmental remediation of the waterways adjacent to the mentioned Refinery. Should these claims be sustained, they could demand additional investments related to the operation of La Plata Refinery. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2006 YPF submitted a presentation before the Environmental Policy Secretariat of the province of Buenos Aires, whereby it suggested the performance of a study for the characterization of risks associated with the aforementioned contamination. </div></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111992409_14" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111992409_15"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111992409_15" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111992409_16"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111992409_16" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111992409_17"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: .83em;margin-top : 1.67em;margin-bottom : 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111992409_17" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111992409_18"><ix:exclude>

PROVISIONS (cont.)</ix:exclude> </div></div><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:DescriptionOfRiskInEnvironmentalClaims" contextRef="P01_25_2011To01_25_2011_OrganismoProvincialParaElDesarrolloSostenibleMemberifrsfullCounterpartiesAxis_ParentMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" id="ixv-119213">On January&#160;25, 2011, YPF executed an agreement with the Provincial Agency for Sustainable Development (&#8220;OPDS&#8221; by its acronym in Spanish) of the province of Buenos Aires, under the Remediation, Liability and Environmental Risk Control Program, created under Resolution No.&#160;88/2010 of the OPDS.</ix:nonNumeric> Under this agreement, the parties agreed to jointly perform a work program in the channels adjacent to La Plata Refinery over a term of <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:RefineryTermPeriod" contextRef="P01_25_2011To01_25_2011_OrganismoProvincialParaElDesarrolloSostenibleMemberifrsfullCounterpartiesAxis_ParentMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" format="ixt-sec:duryear" id="ixv-119214">8</ix:nonNumeric> years, and which involved the characterization and risk assessment studies of channel sediments. The agreement provides that should corrective actions be detected as a result of the risk assessment studies, the different alternatives and available techniques will be considered, as well as the steps needed for their implementation. Dating studies of deposited material will also be performed under the agreement, in order to determine the responsibilities of the Argentine Government in view of its obligation to hold YPF harmless in accordance with the article 9 of YPF&#8217;s Privatization Law. This study proved between <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PercentageOfHydrocarbons" contextRef="P01_25_2011To01_25_2011_BottomOfRangeMemberifrsfullRangeAxis_OrganismoProvincialParaElDesarrolloSostenibleMemberifrsfullCounterpartiesAxis_ParentMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-119215">88</ix:nonFraction>% to <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PercentageOfHydrocarbons" contextRef="P01_25_2011To01_25_2011_OrganismoProvincialParaElDesarrolloSostenibleMemberifrsfullCounterpartiesAxis_ParentMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis_TopOfRangeMemberifrsfullRangeAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-119216">91</ix:nonFraction>% of the hydrocarbons present in the channels were deposited prior to 1991. In this context, YPF, with the agreement of the OPDS, carried out several studies and characterizations through specialized consultants whose progress was notified to the provincial agency. The agreement was replaced by Resolution No.&#160;380/2019 issued by said entity, which approves the remediation modality suggested by YPF (monitored natural recovery) over a term of <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:ExtendedPeriodCoveredByFinancialStatements" contextRef="P01_25_2011To01_25_2011_OrganismoProvincialParaElDesarrolloSostenibleMemberifrsfullCounterpartiesAxis_ParentMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" id="ixv-119217">24 months</ix:nonNumeric>. YPF has answered all points required by the OPDS and requested the extension of the Resolution. On June&#160;26, 2023, through Resolution No.&#160;2,775/2023 issued by the Ministry of Environment of the Province of Buenos Aires, YPF obtained a two-year extension to continue with the remediation and monitoring works through the suggested remediation modality (monitored natural recovery). </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Regarding the judicial claims mentioned above, on February&#160;7, 2021, the Company was notified of the first instance judgment which considered the environmental damage had been proved, and therefore ordered that activities should cease and the environmental damage affecting the waterways adjacent to La Plata Refinery be remedied. <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:LossContingencyDamagesSought" contextRef="P02_07_2021To02_07_2021_OrganismoProvincialParaElDesarrolloSostenibleMemberifrsfullCounterpartiesAxis_ParentMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" id="ixv-119218">This decision determined the co-defendants&#8217; joint liability for the damages in the following proportions: YPF 90% (the Argentine Government 80% and YPF 20%) and the 2 co-defendant companies 10%. The decision was appealed by the Company.</ix:nonNumeric> As of the date of issuance of these consolidated financial statements, said appeal is pending resolution by the Federal Court of La Plata. </div><div style="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">&#8226;</div></div></td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: ARIAL; font-size: 9pt; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">Quilmes </div></div></div></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As regards with a fuel leak in the pipeline running from La Plata to Dock Sud (Progressive 37), currently operated by YPF, which occurred in 1988 when YPF was an Argentine state-owned company, as a result of an unlawful act that caused the rupture of the polyduct, there are several claims, mostly brought by neighbors of the area where they claim (i)&#160;compensation for personal damages allegedly caused by such event and (ii)&#160;environmental remediation. These processes are at the discovery stage. Fuel would have emerged and become perceptible in November 2002, which resulted in remediation works in progress conducted by the Company in the affected area, supervised by the environmental authority of the Province of Buenos Aires. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Argentine Government denied any responsibility to indemnify YPF in this case, wherefore the Company sued the Argentine Government to obtain a judicial decision declaring the invalidity of such decision. This lawsuit has not yet been resolved. </div><div style="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">&#8226;</div></div></td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: ARIAL; font-size: 9pt; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">Other environmental claims </div></div></div></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In addition to the claims discussed above, the Group has other environmental lawsuits in progress where it is claimed (i)&#160;individual damages and/or (ii)&#160;environmental remediation and/or (iii)&#160;collective damages. These proceedings are related to the activities performed by the Group in different jurisdictions of the country. In all these cases, considering the information available to date, the estimated time remaining until the end of the proceedings, and the results of the additional evidence to be presented during the continuation of the litigation, the Group has set up a provision in an amount it considers sufficient to face these claims. </div><div style="margin-top: 10pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">16.a.5) Tax claims </div></div><div style="font-size:10pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">

<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">&#8226;</div></div></td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: ARIAL; font-size: 9pt; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">Dispute over the cost deduction for hydrocarbon well abandonment </div></div></div></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Company has recorded the hydrocarbon wells abandonment costs in accordance with the criteria detailed in Note 2.b.3) and, in the absence of a specific treatment of this matter in the Income Tax Law and its Regulatory Decree, has deducted the charge for hydrocarbon wells abandonment costs in the calculation of this tax, based on the general criteria of the tax standard for deduction of expenses (accrual criteria). Nevertheless, this interpretation has been objected to by the AFIP, which would allow for deductions once the expense has been incurred. </div></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111992409_19" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111992409_20"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111992409_20" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111992409_21"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111992409_21" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111992409_22"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: .83em;margin-top : 1.67em;margin-bottom : 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation></div></div></div> <div> <div> <div style="line-height:normal;background-color:white;display: inline;"> <div style="text-align:center"> <div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111992409_22" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111992409_23"><ix:exclude>

<td colspan="5" style="vertical-align:top"> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">NOTES TO THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</div></div> <div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 1pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">AS OF DECEMBER 31, 2023, 2022 AND 2021</div></div> </td> </tr> </table> </ix:exclude></ix:continuation> <ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111992409_23"><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><ix:exclude>16. PROVISIONS (cont.)</ix:exclude> </div></div> <div style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; font-size: 8pt;">&#160;</div> <div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The AFIP understands that the deduction of expenses for hydrocarbon well abandonment should be deferred until the taxpayer has the opportunity to actually proceed to well abandonment, once the wells have been exhausted, as it considers the abandonment of the well is the event triggering the accrual of hydrocarbon well abandonment expenses. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On the other hand, the Company, as well as other companies in the oil industry, understand that the substantial event generating costs in connection with well abandonment is, in fact, the act of drilling, as drilling causes environmental impact and, consequently, the obligation to repair such impact (abandonment). This obligation is not subject to any condition since there is no uncertainty as to whether well depletion will inevitably occur. The Company has learned that similar disputes have been raised by the AFIP with other companies in the oil industry. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In this respect, in June 2016, the SRH of MINEM, the body in charge of clarifying the origin of the legal obligation in this respect, and in response to a consultation of the Chamber of Oil Exploration and Production, ruled in favor of the position of the oil companies and concluded that drilling is the substantial event generating the charge for well abandonment. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">This response of the Chamber has been informed to the AFIP by both the SRH and by YPF but, with different arguments the AFIP rejected this position. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On November&#160;7, 2018, the Company was notified by AFIP of the commencement of a determination procedure with respect to the projected adjustment for fiscal years 2011 to 2016. The Company filed its defense with the AFIP on December&#160;21, 2018. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On February&#160;3, 2020, the Company was notified by AFIP of the commencement of a determination procedure with respect to the projected adjustment for fiscal years 2017. The Company filed before the AFIP its defense on March&#160;17, 2020. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On August&#160;26, 2020, Law No.&#160;27,562 was published in the BO, expanding the regime for the regularization of taxes, social security contributions and customs duties originally established under Law No.&#160;27,541, which was regulated by AFIP General Resolution No.&#160;4,816/2020. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On June&#160;9, 2021 YPF waived the statute of limitations for fiscal year 2014 to allow the AFIP to analyze the legal grounds for the defense filed by the Company on December&#160;21, 2018, in the context of the administrative proceeding. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Company, based on the opinion of its external advisors, and notwithstanding the technical merits for defending its position, evaluated the regularization plan provided for under Laws No.&#160;27,562 and No.&#160;27,653 for the income tax and the compensations made in due course with the credit balances generated by such tax, and on November&#160;30, 2020 and March&#160;30, 2022, adhered to the aforementioned plans, thus putting an end to the dispute over the cost deduction for hydrocarbon well abandonment corresponding to fiscal periods 2011 to 2013 and fiscal periods 2014 to 2017, respectively. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Regarding fiscal years following and including 2018, it should be noted that since the enactment of Law No.&#160;27,430 (&#8220;Tax Reform&#8221;) in December 2017, the deduction of the well abandonment costs at the time of the drilling phase was admitted, considering them as part of the investment cost, regardless of the period in which the effective abandonment disbursement is made. </div> <div style="margin-top: 10pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">16.a.6) Other pending litigation </div></div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During the normal course of business, the Group has been sued in numerous legal proceedings at labor, civil and commercial courts. The Company, in consultation with its external counsel, has established a provision considering to such end the best estimate based on information available as of the date of issuance of these consolidated financial statements, including legal fees and court costs. </div> <div style="margin-top: 10pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">16.b) Provision for environmental liabilities and Provision for hydrocarbon wells abandonment obligations </div></div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Based on the Group&#8217;s current remediation and hydrocarbon well abandonment plans, the Group has set up a provision for environmental liabilities, where assessments and/or remedial actions are probable and can reasonably be estimated, and for hydrocarbon well abandonment, considering the number of wells not yet abandoned, the costs and schedule for the disbursement dates. </div> </ix:continuation></div> </div> <div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div> <hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%"/> <div style="font-size: .83em;margin-top : 1.67em;margin-bottom : 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div> <div style="text-align:center"> <div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">

SHAREHOLDERS&#8217; EQUITY </div></div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As of December&#160;31, 2023 the Company&#8217;s capital amounts to <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:SubscribedCapital" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2023" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120538">3,919</ix:nonFraction> and treasury shares amount to <div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">14</div> represented by <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:NumberOfSharesSubscribed" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2023_OrdinarySharesMemberifrsfullClassesOfShareCapitalAxis" unitRef="Unit_shares" decimals="0" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120539">393,312,793</ix:nonFraction> book-entry shares of common stock and divided into <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:DescriptionOfClassesOfShares" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" id="ixv-120540">four classes of shares (A, B, C and D)</ix:nonNumeric>, with a par value of <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:ParValuePerShare" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2023" unitRef="Unit_ARS_per_Share" decimals="INF" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120541">10</ix:nonFraction> pesos and <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:DescriptionOfVotingRights" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" id="ixv-120542">1 vote per share</ix:nonNumeric>. These shares are fully subscribed, paid-in and authorized for stock exchange listing. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As of December&#160;31, 2023, there are <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:NumberOfSharesOutstanding" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2023_ClassASharesMemberifrsfullClassesOfShareCapitalAxis" unitRef="Unit_shares" decimals="0" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120543">3,764</ix:nonFraction> Class&#160;A outstanding shares. As long as any Class&#160;A share remains outstanding, <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:DescriptionOfGrantBasedOnSharesOutstanding" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" id="ixv-76079">the affirmative vote of the Argentine Government is required for: (i)&#160;mergers; (ii)&#160;acquisitions of more than <div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:PercentageOfVotingEquityInterestsAcquired" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2023_ClassASharesMemberifrsfullClassesOfShareCapitalAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="INF" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120544">50</ix:nonFraction></div>% of YPF shares in an agreed or hostile bid; (iii)&#160;transfers of all the YPF&#8217;s production and exploration rights; (iv)&#160;the voluntary dissolution of YPF; or (v)&#160;change of corporate and/or tax address outside Argentina. Items (iii)&#160;and (iv)&#160;also require prior approval by the Argentine Congress.</ix:nonNumeric> </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Until the enactment of Law No.&#160;26,741 detailed in the next paragraphs, Repsol S.A. (&#8220;Repsol&#8221;) had a participation in the Company, directly and indirectly, of <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:ProportionOfOwnershipInterestInEquity" contextRef="P05_04_2012To05_04_2012_RepsolSAMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="4" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120545">57.43</ix:nonFraction>% shareholding while Petersen Energ&#237;a S.A.U. and its affiliates exercised significant influence through a <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:ProportionOfOwnershipInterestInSharesByRelatedParty" contextRef="P05_04_2012To05_04_2012_PetersenEnergiaSauAndAffiliatesMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="4" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120546">25.46</ix:nonFraction>% shareholding of YPF&#8217;s capital stock. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Law No.&#160;26,741 enacted on May&#160;4, 2012, changed YPF&#8217;s shareholding structure declared the class D Shares of YPF owned by Repsol as national public interest and subject to expropriation representing 51% of YPF&#8217;s equity. In addition, Law 26,741 declared that achieving self-sufficiency in the supply of hydrocarbons as well as in the exploitation, industrialization, transportation and sale of hydrocarbons, shall be considered of national public interest and a priority for Argentina, with the goal of guaranteeing socially equitable economic development, job creation, the increase of the competitiveness of various economic sectors and the equitable and sustainable growth of the provinces and regions. The shares subject to expropriation were distributed as follows: <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PercentageOfSharesSubjectToExpropriation" contextRef="P05_04_2012To05_04_2012_FederalGovernmentMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120547">51</ix:nonFraction>% for the Argentine federal government and <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PercentageOfSharesSubjectToExpropriation" contextRef="P05_04_2012To05_04_2012_StateOrProvinceMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120548">49</ix:nonFraction>% for certain Provinces. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">During the fiscal years ended December&#160;31, 2023 and 2021, the Company has not repurchased its own shares. During the fiscal year ended December&#160;31, 2022, the Company has repurchased <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:TreasuryStockSharesAcquired1" contextRef="P01_01_2022To12_31_2022" unitRef="Unit_shares" decimals="INF" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120549">1,888,798</ix:nonFraction> of its own shares issued for an amount of <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:PurchaseOfTreasuryShares" contextRef="P01_01_2022To12_31_2022" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120550">28</ix:nonFraction>, for purposes of compliance with the share-based benefit plans (see Note 37). </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In accordance with the provisions of the LGS and the CNV Rules, the Company must set aside a legal reserve of not less than <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:LegalReservesAsAPercentageOfNetProfitPriorYearAdjustmentsAndTransferFromOtherComprehensiveIncomeMinimum" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120551">5</ix:nonFraction>% of the positive result resulting from the algebraic sum of net profit or loss for the year, prior-year adjustments, transfers from other comprehensive income to unappropriated retained earnings and losses from previous years, until such reserve reaches <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:MaximumPercentageOfLegalReserve" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2023" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120552">20</ix:nonFraction>% of the sum of the &#8220;Capital&#8221; and &#8220;Adjustment of capital&#8221; accounts and the translation differences related to such accounts according to the regulation of the CNV. As of December&#160;31, 2023, the legal reserve has been fully integrated, amounting to <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:StatutoryReserve" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2023" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120553">787</ix:nonFraction>. Likewise, the Company&#8217;s Shareholders&#8217; Meeting has allocated voluntary reserves for future dividends, for investments and for purchase of treasury shares. In relation to the reserve for future dividends and in compliance with the LGS, we declare dividends in the currency of legal tender in Argentina, which is the peso. The dividends are declared and distributed based on the last annual audited financial statements in pesos submitted to the CNV. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Considering Article 3, item 11, sections c) and e), Chapter III, Title IV of CNV Rules, the balances of the accounts &#8220;Acquisition cost of treasury shares&#8221; and &#8220;Share trading premiums&#8221; in the currency of legal tender in Argentina, which is the peso, restricts the distribution of retained earnings. As of December&#160;31, 2023 the restricted balance amounts to <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:RestrictedDistributionOfRetainedEarnings" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2023" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120554">70</ix:nonFraction> of which <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:DistributableRetainedEarningsSubjectToRestrictionAcquisitionCostOfTreasuryShares" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2023" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120555">30</ix:nonFraction> corresponds to the balance of &#8220;Acquisition cost of treasury shares&#8221; account and <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:DistributableRetainedEarningsSubjectToRestrictionBalanceOfSharePremiumAccount" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2023" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120556">40</ix:nonFraction> to the balance of &#8220;Share trading premiums&#8221; account. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">When the net balance of retained earnings at the end of a fiscal year is positive, it can be distributed upon the decision of the Shareholders&#8217; meeting, while not subject to legal restrictions. Additionally, pursuant to the CNV Rules, when the net balance of &#8220;Other comprehensive income&#8221; account in the currency of legal tender in Argentina, which is the peso, is positive, it will not be distributed nor capitalized nor used to compensate accumulated losses, but will be computed as part of retained earnings in order to make comparisons to determine the situation of the Company in relation to articles 31, 32 and 206 of the LGS, or other legal or regulatory rules making reference to limits or ratios with capital and reserves, not specifically and expressly provided for under the CNV Rules. When the net balance of this account at the end of a fiscal year is negative, a restriction on the distribution of retained earnings for the same amount will be imposed. </div> </ix:nonNumeric></div> </div> <div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div> <hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%"/> <div style="font-size: .83em;margin-top : 1.67em;margin-bottom : 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div> </div> </div> <div><div><div style="line-height:normal;background-color:white;display: inline;"><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">

ISSUES RELATED TO MAXUS ENTITIES </div></div><div style="margin-top: 8pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">32.a) Legal proceedings </div></div><div style="margin-top: 8pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">32.a.1) Introduction </div></div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">At the time of its acquisition by YPF in 1995, Maxus Energy Corporation (&#8220;Maxus&#8221;) and certain of its subsidiaries (including Tierra Solutions, Inc. (&#8220;TS&#8221;), Maxus International Energy Company (&#8220;MIEC&#8221;), Maxus (US) Exploration Company (&#8220;MUSE&#8221;) and Gateway Coal Company (&#8220;Gateway&#8221;) and together with Maxus, TS, MIEC and MUSE, the &#8220;Maxus Entities&#8221;), would have certain liabilities related to former operations of a previous Maxus subsidiary: Diamond Shamrock Chemicals Company (&#8220;Chemicals&#8221;). In 1986, Maxus sold Chemicals to Occidental Chemical Corporation (&#8220;Occidental&#8221;), and in connection with that sale agreed to indemnify Chemicals and Occidental from and against certain liabilities relating to the business or activities of Chemicals prior to September&#160;4, 1986, including environmental liabilities relating to chemical plants and waste disposal sites used by Chemicals prior to that date. Mainly as a result of such indemnity obligation, the Maxus Entities have been involved in various administrative and judicial proceedings of an environmental and contractual nature in the United States, as described in Note 32.a.2). </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In June 2016, each of the Maxus Entities filed a voluntary petition under Chapter 11 of the Bankruptcy Code of the United States (&#8220;United States Bankruptcy Code&#8221;) with the United States Bankruptcy Court of the District of Delaware (&#8220;Bankruptcy Court&#8221;), which had the effect of staying the cross-claims described in Note 32.a.2.ii). In December 2016, as part of their reorganization process, the Maxus Entities, in their capacity as debtors, filed their proposed plan of liquidation (&#8220;Liquidation Plan&#8221;) in accordance with the United&#160;States Bankruptcy Code. In March 2017 the Maxus Entities and the creditors committee of the Maxus Entities (&#8220;Creditors Committee&#8221;) filed their alternative proposed plan of liquidation (&#8220;Alternative Plan&#8221;) under the United States Bankruptcy Code, which contemplated, among other matters, the creation of a liquidating trust (&#8220;Liquidating Trust&#8221;) and the cancellation of the equity participations of YPF Holdings and YCLH Holdings, Inc (&#8220;YCLH Holdings&#8221;, formerly CLH Holdings, Inc.) in the Maxus Entities. The Bankruptcy Court approved the Alternative Plan in May 2017, which was confirmed and became effective in July 2017. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In June 2018, the Liquidating Trust filed a lawsuit with the Bankruptcy Court against YPF, YPF Holdings, YCLH Holdings and YPF International (collectively, the &#8220;YPF Defendants&#8221;), as well as other entities not related to the YPF Defendants, claiming alleged damages in an amount up to <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:LossContingencyEstimateOfClaimingAllegedDamagesAmount" contextRef="PAsOn06_30_2018" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120569">14,000</ix:nonFraction>, on the basis of allegations of fraudulent transfers and alter ego liability of the YPF Defendants in connection with corporate restructuring transactions of the Maxus Entities. Throughout the 1990s and 2000s decades, certain restructuring transactions were carried out in respect of the international operations of the Group, including certain operations by the companies that made up the Maxus Entities&#8217; group, which were carried out in the ordinary course of business with the legitimate objective of achieving greater efficiencies in the management of such international operations. For its part, the Liquidating Trust alleged that (i)&#160;these restructuring transactions constitute fraudulent transfers for which the YPF Defendants are liable, and (ii)&#160;the YPF Defendants are an alter ego of the Maxus Entities and are responsible for all of their liabilities, including the environmental liabilities described in Note 32.a.2.i). The YPF Defendants rejected these allegations made by the Liquidating Trust for considering them without merit and obtained a partial summary judgment decision from the Bankruptcy Court in their favor, rejecting the &#8220;all liabilities&#8221; theory (liability for all liabilities and contingencies of the Maxus Entities) proposed by the Liquidating Trust related to the alleged alter ego damages, as described in Note 32.a.4). </div></ix:nonNumeric></div></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelection_111993565" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_1"><div></div></ix:continuation></div><div><div style="line-height:normal;background-color:white;display: inline;"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_1" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_2"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_2" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_3"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_3" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_4"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: .83em;margin-top : 1.67em;margin-bottom : 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_4" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_5"><ix:exclude>
