ISSUES RELATED TO MAXUS ENTITIES (cont.)</ix:exclude> </div></div><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On April&#160;6, 2023, the YPF Defendants, the Liquidating Trust and other companies not related to the YPF Defendants (Repsol, S.A., Repsol Exploraci&#243;n, S.A., Repsol USA Holdings LLC, Repsol E&amp;P USA LLC, Repsol Offshore E&amp;P USA, Inc., Perenco Trinidad&#160;&amp; Tobago (Holdings) ETVE SLU (f/k/a Repsol E&amp;P T&amp;T Limited), and Repsol Services Co. (collectively, the &#8220;Repsol Defendants&#8221;) signed, among other documents, a settlement and release agreement (the &#8220;Trust Settlement Agreement&#8221;) providing for a full release and discharge of all claims in exchange for payment of a settlement amount, subject to the satisfaction or waiver of certain conditions, including court approvals and other procedural events, as described in Note 32.a.4). </div><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">32.a.2) Background to the Reorganization Process of the Maxus Entities under the United States Bankruptcy Code </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Following the petition filed by the Maxus Entities with the Bankruptcy Court under the United States Bankruptcy Code in June 2016, the Company only has access to information regarding administrative and judicial proceedings against the Maxus Entities that is published by the competent authorities and/or that is publicly filed by the parties involved in such proceedings, including information published by the United States Environmental Protection Agency (&#8220;EPA&#8221;). </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The development of these administrative and judicial proceedings was relevant to the Company in light of the Liquidating Trust&#8217;s request to the Bankruptcy Court that the YPF Defendants be found liable for all liabilities and contingencies of the Maxus Entities, including those that might eventually arise in the future as a result of such proceedings (&#8220;all liabilities&#8221; theory). However, as described in Note 32.a.4), on June&#160;22, 2022, the Bankruptcy Court granted partial summary judgment in favor of the YPF Defendants, rejecting the &#8220;all liabilities&#8221; theory (liability for all liabilities and contingencies of the Maxus Entities) proposed by the Liquidating Trust relating to the alleged alter ego damages. In rejecting the &#8220;all liabilities&#8221; theory, the Bankruptcy Court agreed with the YPF Defendants that the alleged alter ego damages required evidence of causation and, therefore, the Liquidating Trust would have to prove that the claimed damages were caused by the alleged alter ego conduct. Moreover, as described in Note 32.a.4), the case brought by the Liquidating Trust has been dismissed. </div><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">32.a.2.i) Environmental administrative matters </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 1986 at the time of the sale of Chemicals to Occidental, TS (formerly Chemical Land Holdings, Inc.) owned a chemical plant located on Lister Avenue in Newark, New Jersey, on the banks of the Passaic River. The plant allegedly discharged chemicals that contaminated the area surrounding the plant (&#8220;Lister Site&#8221;), the Passaic River and Newark Bay. After the sale and up to the date the Maxus Entities filed the petition for reorganization with the Bankruptcy Court in June 2016, the plant in the Lister Site continued to be owned by TS. Occidental alleged that under the sale agreement, Maxus made itself liable to indemnify Occidental for all environmental liabilities related to the Lister Site, the Passaic River and the Newark Bay that may be Chemicals&#180; or Occidental&#180;s responsibility. Throughout the 1990s and subsequently, the EPA, the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (&#8220;Department of Environmental Protection&#8221; or &#8220;DEP&#8221;), and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (&#8220;NOAA&#8221;) initiated several administrative proceedings against Occidental, the Maxus Entities, and various other entities in connection with the study and remediation of environmental liabilities located at the Lister Site, the Passaic River, and Newark Bay, which gave rise to, among others, those mentioned below: </div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

ISSUES RELATED TO MAXUS ENTITIES (cont.)</ix:exclude> </div></div><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">32.a.2.ii) Legal proceedings in the courts of New Jersey for the Passaic River </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In relation to the alleged contamination in the Passaic River, Newark Bay, other nearby waterways and surrounding areas, in 2005 the DEP sued Maxus, TS, YPF, YPF Holdings, YCLH Holdings, Repsol and other companies, including Occidental (later adding YPF International), before the New Jersey Court seeking remediation of natural resources damages and punitive damages, among other claims. The defendants made responsive pleadings and filings. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2008 Occidental filed cross-claims before the New Jersey Court alleging that under Chemicals&#8217; sale agreement, Maxus would be liable to indemnify Occidental for the damages that the DEP claimed from Occidental, and that YPF, YPF Holdings, YCLH Holdings and Repsol (later adding YPF International) were also liable for such damages as they had received fraudulent transfers from Maxus and/or were Maxus&#8217; alter ego. The defendants rejected these allegations and asserted appropriate defenses. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2013 the DEP entered into a proposed settlement agreement with YPF, YPF Holdings, YPF International, YCLH Holdings, Maxus and TS (&#8220;Settlement Agreement&#8221;). The Settlement Agreement, which did not imply endorsement of facts or rights and presented only for conciliatory purposes, was subject to an approval process, publication, comment period and approval by the New Jersey Court. According to the terms of the Settlement Agreement, the DEP would agree to release certain claims related to environmental liabilities within a geographic area of the Passaic River initiated against YPF, YPF International, YPF Holdings, YCLH Holdings, Maxus and TS, recognizing a limited liability of up to <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:MaximumLitigationALimitedLiability" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2013_SettllementAgreementMemberYPFAgreementAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120572">400</ix:nonFraction> collectively, for these and other participants in the litigation if they were found responsible. In return, Maxus would make cash payment of <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PaymentOfLitigationSettlement" contextRef="P02_10_2014To02_10_2014_ComplianceWithTheSettlementAgreementMemberYPFAgreementAxis_MaxusEntitiesMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120573">65</ix:nonFraction> at the time of approval of the Settlement Agreement. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Simultaneously, Repsol reached a settlement agreement with the DEP, agreeing to pay <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PaymentOfLitigationSettlement" contextRef="P02_10_2014To02_10_2014_BottomOfRangeMemberifrsfullRangeAxis_NewJerseyCourtApprovedTheSettlementAgreementMemberYPFAgreementAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120574">65</ix:nonFraction> (subject to the same <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PaymentOfLitigationSettlement" contextRef="P12_31_2013To12_31_2013_NewJerseyCourtApprovedTheSettlementAgreementMemberYPFAgreementAxis_TopOfRangeMemberifrsfullRangeAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120575">400</ix:nonFraction> limitation described above). </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2013, the New Jersey Court approved the Settlement Agreement and, on February&#160;10, 2014, in compliance with the Settlement Agreement, Maxus made a deposit of <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PaymentOfLitigationSettlement" contextRef="P02_10_2014To02_10_2014_ComplianceWithTheSettlementAgreementMemberYPFAgreementAxis_MaxusEntitiesMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120576">65</ix:nonFraction>. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Additionally, on December&#160;16, 2014, the New Jersey Court approved a settlement agreement whereby the DEP agreed to settle all claims against Occidental related to the environmental liabilities within a specific geographical area of the Passaic River, in consideration for the payment of <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:LitigationSettlementClaimAmount" contextRef="P12_16_2014To12_16_2014_MaxusEntitiesMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis_SettllementAgreementMemberYPFAgreementAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120577">190</ix:nonFraction> and a sum amounting up to <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PaymentAndSettlementOfEnvironmentalLiabilities" contextRef="P12_16_2014To12_16_2014_SettllementAgreementMemberYPFAgreementAxis_TopOfRangeMemberifrsfullRangeAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120578">400</ix:nonFraction> to reimburse the State of New Jersey in the event it is required to pay a percentage of the costs for future remedial actions in accordance with the United States Federal Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation and Liability Act. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Following the signing of the aforementioned settlement agreements, the cross-claims between the defendants (Occidental, Maxus, TS, YPF, YPF International, YPF Holdings, YCLH Holdings and Repsol) remained pending resolution by the New Jersey Court. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">However, such cross-claims were stayed as of June&#160;17, 2016, when Maxus, TS, and other affiliated companies each filed a voluntary petition under Chapter 11 with the Bankruptcy Court, as described in Note 32.a.3). On June&#160;28, 2016, at Occidental&#8217;s request, the New Jersey Court transferred all remaining claims in the Passaic River litigation from the New Jersey Court to the Bankruptcy Court. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On August&#160;2, 2023, a stipulation of dismissal of all claims was filed in the New Jersey Court, effectuating the immediate dismissal with prejudice of the action as of that same date. </div></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_11" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_12"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_12" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_13"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_13" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_14"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: .83em;margin-top : 1.67em;margin-bottom : 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_14" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_15"><ix:exclude>

ISSUES RELATED TO MAXUS ENTITIES (cont.)</ix:exclude> </div></div><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">32.a.3) Reorganization Process under Chapter 11 of the United States Bankruptcy Code </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On June&#160;17, 2016, each of the Maxus Entities filed a voluntary petition under the United States Bankruptcy Code with the United States Bankruptcy Court. In this context, the Maxus Entities entered into an agreement (the &#8220;2016 Agreement&#8221;) with YPF, YPF Holdings, YCLH Holdings, YPF International and YPF Services USA Corp (&#8220;YPF Services&#8221;) (together, the &#8220;YPF Entities&#8221;), to settle all of the Maxus Entities&#8217; claims against the YPF Entities, including any alter ego claims, all of which, in the YPF Entities&#8217; opinion, had no merit. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The 2016 Agreement provided for: (i)&#160;the granting of a year-long loan by YPF Holdings for an amount of up to <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:LoanPayableToRelatedPartiesFaceValue" contextRef="PAsOn06_17_2016_MaxusEntitiesMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis_YPFHoldingsMemberifrsfullSignificantInvestmentsInSubsidiariesAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120580">63.1</ix:nonFraction> (&#8220;DIP Loan&#8221;) to finance the Maxus Entities&#8217; activities during a bankruptcy case, and (ii)&#160;a payment of <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:SettlementPayment" contextRef="P06_17_2016To06_17_2016_MaxusEntitiesMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120581">130</ix:nonFraction> to the Maxus Entities (&#8220;Settlement Payment&#8221;) for a release of all claims that the Maxus Entities might have against the YPF Entities. </div><ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:DescriptionOfSettlementPaymentSubjectToDebtorsAgreement" contextRef="P12_29_2016To12_29_2016_ChapterElevenPlanOfLiquidationMemberifrsfullClassesOfFinancialInstrumentsAxis" id="ixv-76447"><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On December&#160;29, 2016, the Maxus Entities filed with the Bankruptcy Court their proposed Liquidation Plan under the United States Bankruptcy Code. The Plan foresaw a <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:SettlementPayment" contextRef="P12_29_2016To12_29_2016_ChapterElevenPlanOfLiquidationMemberifrsfullClassesOfFinancialInstrumentsAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120582">130</ix:nonFraction> Settlement Payment under the 2016 Agreement and provided that, if the 2016 Agreement was approved, portions of the <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:SettlementPayment" contextRef="P12_29_2016To12_29_2016_ChapterElevenPlanOfLiquidationMemberifrsfullClassesOfFinancialInstrumentsAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120583">130</ix:nonFraction> Settlement Payment would be deposited into (i)&#160;a liquidating trust for distribution to creditors and (ii)&#160;an environmental response trust for use in remediation. Moreover, if the Liquidation Plan were approved, the 2016 Agreement with the Maxus Entities would likely be confirmed and the claims against the YPF Entities, including the alter-ego claims, would be settled and released in exchange for the <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:SettlementPayment" contextRef="P12_29_2016To12_29_2016_ChapterElevenPlanOfLiquidationMemberifrsfullClassesOfFinancialInstrumentsAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120584">130</ix:nonFraction> Settlement Payment. </div></ix:nonNumeric><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Liquidation Plan, however, provided for certain contingencies should the Bankruptcy Court not approve the 2016 Agreement. In that scenario, the Maxus Entities&#8217; claims against YPF Entities, including the alter-ego claims, would be transferred into a liquidating trust. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On March&#160;28, 2017, the Maxus Entities and the Creditors Committee submitted the Alternative Plan, which did not include the 2016 Agreement with the YPF Entities. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Under the Alternative Plan, the Liquidating Trust could pursue alter ego claims and any other claim belonging to the insolvent&#8217;s estate against the YPF Entities. The Liquidating Trust would be financed by Occidental in its capacity as creditor of the Maxus Entities. As such, the Alternative Plan did not contemplate the implementation of the originally submitted 2016 Agreement, and on April&#160;10, 2017, YPF Holdings gave notice that this situation constituted an event of default under the DIP Loan. By the approval of the financing offered by Occidental under the Alternative Plan, the Bankruptcy Court ordered the return of the outstanding amounts (<ix:nonFraction name="ypf:ReturnOfOutstandingAmounts" contextRef="P06_17_2016To06_17_2016_DebtorInPossessionLoanMemberifrsfullClassesOfFinancialInstrumentsAxis_MaxusEntitiesMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis_YPFHoldingsMemberifrsfullSignificantInvestmentsInSubsidiariesAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120585">12</ix:nonFraction>)&#160;under the terms of the DIP Loan, which were subsequently returned to YPF Holdings. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On May&#160;22, 2017, the Bankruptcy Court issued an order confirming the Alternative Plan submitted by the Creditors Committee and the Maxus Entities, which became effective as of July&#160;14, 2017. Through the Alternative Plan the Liquidating Trust was created, which brought in 2018 the complaint referred to in Note 32.a.4) hereafter. </div><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">32.a.4) Claim of the Liquidating Trust </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On June&#160;14, 2018, the Liquidating Trust filed a lawsuit against the YPF Defendants and the Repsol Defendants before the Bankruptcy Court, claiming alleged damages of up to <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:ClaimAllegedDamages" contextRef="PAsOn06_14_2018_MaxusEnergyCorporationLiquidatingTrustMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120586">14,000</ix:nonFraction>, on the basis of allegations of fraudulent transfers and liability as the Maxus Entities&#8217; alter ego (&#8220;Liquidating Trust&#8217;s Claim&#8221;). As described above, throughout the 1990s and 2000s decades, several restructuring operations were carried out in respect of the international operations of the Group, including operations of companies that made up the Maxus Entities&#8217; group, which were carried out in the ordinary course of business with the legitimate objective of achieving greater efficiencies in the management of the Group&#8217;s international operations. For its part, as against the YPF Defendants, the Liquidating Trust alleged that (i)&#160;these restructuring transactions constituted fraudulent transfers for which the YPF Defendants were liable and (ii)&#160;the YPF Defendants were an alter ego of the Maxus Entities and were responsible for all of the Maxus Entities&#8217; liabilities, including the environmental liabilities described in Note 32.a.2.i). The YPF Defendants rejected such allegations and filed a motion to dismiss the Liquidating Trust&#8217;s Claim (&#8220;Motion to Dismiss&#8221;). </div></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_16" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_17"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_17" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_18"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_18" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_19"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: .83em;margin-top : 1.67em;margin-bottom : 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation></div></div></div> <div><div><div style="line-height:normal;background-color:white;display: inline;"><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_19" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_20"><ix:exclude>

ISSUES RELATED TO MAXUS ENTITIES (cont.)</ix:exclude> </div></div><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Between October&#160;19, 2018 and January&#160;22, 2019, several procedural actions were completed in connection with the Motion to Dismiss. Similarly, during that period, the Repsol Defendants also filed a motion requesting that the Bankruptcy Court dismiss the Liquidating Trust&#8217;s Claim. On February&#160;15, 2019, the Bankruptcy Court denied both motions. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On March&#160;1, 2019, the YPF Defendants sought leave to appeal the order dated February&#160;15, 2019, rejecting the Motion to Dismiss. The appeal was denied by the Delaware District Court on September&#160;12, 2019, and the parties proceeded to the discovery process. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">While the aforementioned appeal was still being considered, on April&#160;1, 2019, the YPF Defendants on one hand, and the Repsol Defendants, on the other hand, answered the complaint initiated by the Liquidating Trust. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Within the framework of the Liquidating Trust&#8217;s Claim, during 2019 and 2020 court activity focused on (i)&#160;the filing of motions to withdraw the reference, the purpose of which was to have a matter transferred to district court of the respective district rather than a bankruptcy court, (ii)&#160;the discovery process, (iii)&#160;the filing of a motion to disqualify against the attorneys of the Liquidating Trust, and (iv)&#160;the definition of procedural stages. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On March&#160;23, 2020, the District Court for the District of Delaware rejected the motions to withdraw the reference raised by the YPF Defendants and the Repsol Defendants as premature. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">With regard to the discovery process, the judicial activity mainly included proceedings related to the definition of the documentary and testimonial evidence to be produced in the process. The fact discovery process substantially concluded on October&#160;21, 2021, and the expert discovery process concluded on April&#160;8, 2022. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">With regard to the motion to disqualify the attorneys of the Liquidating Trust, on December&#160;19, 2020, the YPF Defendants filed a Motion to Disqualify White&#160;&amp; Case LLP as legal representatives of the Liquidating Trust based on the Company&#8217;s understanding that such law firm might be prevented from acting in such capacity by virtue of conflicts of interest arising from the incorporation to the firm of attorney-at-law Jessica Boelter, former partner of the firm Sidley Austin LLP and member of the team of attorneys that advised the YPF Defendants in this process. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On April&#160;6, 2021, the Bankruptcy Court denied such motion for disqualification, a decision that was appealed by the YPF Defendants before the Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On September&#160;9, 2022, the Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit issued a decision affirming the Bankruptcy Court&#8217;s decision dismissing the motion for disqualification. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On March&#160;16, 2022, the Liquidating Trust filed a motion for partial summary judgment on certain of its claims against the YPF Defendants and the Repsol Defendants. That motion did not request the entry of a monetary judgment at that time, acknowledging that certain issues should be resolved at trial. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On April&#160;27, 2022, the YPF Defendants and the Repsol Defendants filed their motions for summary judgment as well as their respective oppositions to the motion for summary judgment filed by the Liquidating Trust. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On June 13, 2022, a hearing was held before the Bankruptcy Court for the presentation of the oral arguments related to motions for summary judgment. On June 22, 2022, the Bankruptcy Court rejected the motion for summary judgment filed by the Liquidating Trust stating, among other considerations, that there were relevant matters of fact in dispute that had to be settled at the trial stage. The Bankruptcy Court also partially granted summary judgment in favor of the YPF Defendants rejecting the &#8220;all liabilities&#8221; theory (responsibility for all Maxus Entities&#8217; liabilities and contingencies) proposed by the Liquidating Trust in relation to the claimed alter ego damages. In rejecting the &#8220;all liabilities&#8221; theory proposed by the Liquidating Trust, the Bankruptcy Court concurred with the YPF Defendants that the damages claimed by alter ego require evidence of causality, and, therefore, the Liquidating Trust would have to prove that the damages claimed were caused by the purported alter ego behavior. The Bankruptcy Court also stated that the liability for the alleged alter ego behavior of the YPF Defendants and the Repsol Defendants is an issue that would have to be first settled at the trial stage before the amount of damages, if any, can be analyzed. </div></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_21" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_22"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_22" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_23"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_23" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_24"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: .83em;margin-top : 1.67em;margin-bottom : 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_24" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_25"><ix:exclude>

ISSUES RELATED TO MAXUS ENTITIES (cont.)</ix:exclude> </div></div><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On September&#160;30, 2022, the Bankruptcy Court confirmed the dates proposed by the parties for trial during the months of March and April 2023. On January&#160;3, 2023, the parties jointly requested a stay of all deadlines and suspension of trial dates, with new trial dates to be held for the period between June&#160;19, 2023, and July&#160;31, 2023. The Bankruptcy Court granted the request that same day. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As mentioned in Note 32.a.1), on April&#160;6, 2023, the YPF Defendants, the Repsol Defendants and the Liquidating Trust signed the Trust Settlement Agreement. Pursuant to the Trust Settlement Agreement, the Liquidating Trust agreed to dismiss with prejudice all of the actions brought against the YPF Defendants and the Repsol Defendants and to provide a full release and discharge of all claims, in exchange for the payment of <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:AggregateClaims" contextRef="PAsOn04_06_2023_TrustSettlementAgreementMemberYPFAgreementAxis_YPFAndRepsolDefendandsMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120589">575</ix:nonFraction>, of which the YPF Defendants agreed to pay <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:ShorttermLegalProceedingsProvision" contextRef="PAsOn05_01_2023_TrustSettlementAgreementMemberYPFAgreementAxis_YPFAndRepsolDefendandsMemberifrsfullCategoriesOfRelatedPartiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-5" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120590">287.5</ix:nonFraction> (less certain deductions), plus interest accruing from May&#160;1, 2023 until the date of payment. The civil action pending before the New Jersey state court against the YPF Defendants (see Note 32.a.2.ii)) was also included in the dismissals and releases described above. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In addition to the Trust Settlement Agreement, the YPF Defendants and the Repsol Defendants signed a settlement and release agreement (&#8220;Oxy Settlement Agreement&#8221;) with Occidental and various other Occidental entities, including Occidental Petroleum Corporation and Occidental Chemical Holding Corporation (together, the &#8220;Oxy Parties&#8221;). Pursuant to the Oxy Settlement Agreement, which did not require any payment in addition to the amounts covered by the Trust Settlement Agreement given the benefits to the Oxy Parties under that agreement, the Oxy Parties agreed to release all claims they may possess against the YPF Defendants and the Repsol Defendants relating to the Maxus Entities, the Passaic River and other areas subject to environmental remediation. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The YPF Defendants and the Repsol Defendants also entered into a settlement and covenant not to sue agreement (&#8220;Government Agreement&#8221;) with various U.S. governmental entities, including the U.S. Department of Justice (on behalf of the EPA, the Department of Interior, and the NOAA) and the States of Ohio and Wisconsin (&#8220;Governmental Parties&#8221;). The Governmental Parties have covenanted not to sue the YPF Defendants or the Repsol Defendants with respect to claims similar to those the Liquidating Trust has asserted, as well as certain claims under the U.S. Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA). Given the benefits to the Governmental Parties under the Trust Settlement Agreement, the Government Agreement also did not require any payment in addition to the amounts covered by the Trust Settlement Agreement. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As noted above, the YPF Defendants&#8217; payment to the Liquidating Trust, and the dismissal and release of actions and claims against the YPF Defendants under the aforementioned agreements, were subject to a number of conditions and procedural steps, including obtaining a final court order approving the Trust Settlement Agreement and a final court order approving the Government Agreement. On August&#160;2, 2023, following satisfaction of all conditions and procedural steps, the YPF Defendants made payment under the Trust Settlement Agreement and the dismissals and releases described above became effective as to the YPF Defendants, including dismissal of all relevant state and federal actions against the YPF Defendants. </div><div style="margin-top: 10pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">32.b) Accounting matters </div></div><div style="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In connection with the petition filed with the Bankruptcy Court under the United States Bankruptcy Code by the Maxus Entities on June 17, 2016, as described in Note 32.a.2), the Company considered this an event that required reconsideration of whether the consolidation of the Maxus Entities remained appropriate. In order to carry out this analysis, the Company followed the guidelines established in IFRS 10 to reassess whether it maintained control over the activities of the Maxus Entities. This analysis, in accordance with IAS 8, was complemented by the criteria set forth in the United States Standard ASC 810 published by the FASB, the principles of which are consistent with IFRS 10, but addresses in more detail the issues related to the consolidation of entities that file a reorganization proceeding under the United States Bankruptcy Code. </div></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_26" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_27"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_27" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_28"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_28" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_29"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: .83em;margin-top : 1.67em;margin-bottom : 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation></div></div></div> <div><div><div style="line-height:normal;background-color:white;display: inline;"><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_29" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993565_30"><ix:exclude>

ISSUES RELATED TO MAXUS ENTITIES (cont.)</ix:exclude> </div></div><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Generally, when an entity files a reorganization petition under the United States Bankruptcy Code, shareholders do not maintain the ability to exercise the power to make decisions that have a significant impact on the economic performance of the business of entities because that power is usually subject to Bankruptcy Court approval. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The petition filed by the Maxus Entities under the United States Bankruptcy Code had relevant effects on the rights of YPF Holdings as a shareholder of these entities, because creditors of the bankruptcy process (the &#8220;Creditors&#8221;) replaced the shareholders in their legal capacity to file derivative suits against the directors on behalf of the Maxus Entities for breach of the Debtors&#8217; fiduciary obligations, since the Creditors would be the main beneficiaries in any increase in value of these entities. However, at the time of the voluntary filing of the reorganization petition under the United States Bankruptcy Code, it should be noted that YPF Holdings retained its right to designate directors of the Maxus Entities through shareholders&#8217; meetings, unless the Bankruptcy Court ordered otherwise. In addition, the bankruptcy cases filed with the Bankruptcy Court also affected the responsibilities and functions of the board of directors and management of each of the respective Maxus Entities. Each of the Maxus Entities had become a &#8220;debtor in possession&#8221; and, in accordance with the United States Bankruptcy Code, remained in possession of its property and, subject to certain limitations, was authorized to carry out its normal operations, unless the Bankruptcy Court ordered otherwise. Even so, during the United States Bankruptcy Code&#8217;s cases, the directors of the Maxus Entities do not have absolute discretion, since any decision outside the ordinary course of business of the Maxus Entities will be subject to the approval of the Bankruptcy Court. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Likewise, on November&#160;8, 2016, the Maxus Entities amended their by-laws in order to give greater discretion to the independent directors. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Additionally, the Alternative Plan approved by the Bankruptcy Court was confirmed and became effective in July 2017, pursuant to which the equity participations of YPF Holdings and YCLH Holdings in the Maxus Entities were cancelled, and, accordingly, these companies ceased having any participation in the Maxus Entities. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In view of the foregoing, the Company understands that it is no longer able to influence the Maxus Entities&#8217; operations and results, a necessary condition established by IFRS 10 to establish the existence of an effective financial control and therefore, on June&#160;17, 2016, it proceeded to deconsolidate the investments of the Maxus Entities. </div></ix:continuation><ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:DisclosureOfContingentAssetsAndLiabilitiesExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" escape="true" continuedAt="TextSelection_111996562" id="ixv-76622"><div id="fintoc804823_39" style="margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">33. CONTINGENT ASSETS AND LIABILITIES </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Group has the following contingencies and claims, individually significant, which in the opinion of the Company and its external counsels, have a possible outcome. In this sense, and based on the information available to the Group, including the amount of time remaining before conclusion of pending lawsuits, the results of evidence discovery and the assessment of internal and external advisors, the Group is unable to estimate the reasonably possible loss or range of loss in relation to certain matters described in section 33.b). </div><div style="margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">33.a) Contingent assets </div></div><div style="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Group has no significant contingent assets. </div><div style="margin-top: 10pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">33.b) Contingent liabilities </div></div><div style="margin-top: 10pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">33.b.1) Environmental claims </div></div><div style="font-size:12pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

CONTINGENT ASSETS AND LIABILITIES (cont.)</ix:exclude></div></div> </div><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Concessionary companies in the Neuquina basin areas </div></div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The claim was answered by YPF and the rest of the sued parties. Following several proceedings, on December&#160;30, 2014, the CSJN issued <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:NumberOfInterlocutoryJudgments" contextRef="P12_30_2014To12_30_2014_AsociacionSuperficiariosDeLaPatagoniaMemberYPFLegalEntitiesAxis_CsjnMemberifrsfullClassesOfProvisionsAxis" unitRef="Unit_Judgment" decimals="INF" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120593">2</ix:nonFraction> interlocutory judgments. The first judgment declared that all environmental damages related to local and provincial situations were outside the scope of its original competence, and that only &#8220;inter-jurisdictional situations&#8221; (such as the Colorado River basin) would fall under its venue. In the second judgment, the Court rejected the petition filed by ASSUPA to incorporate Repsol SA and the directors who carried their activities in YPF until April 2012 as a necessary third party. The Court also rejected precautionary measures and other proceedings related to such request. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As a result of such decision, a preventive action has been filed by an individual to prevent future damages and reduce presumed damages, an action for repair of damages consisting of the comprehensive remediation of collective damages allegedly caused by the hydrocarbon activity undertaken by YPF in the Province of Neuqu&#233;n. In such action, YPF answered the claim and requested that the National Government, the Provincial Government and other oil companies in the area be summoned to appear. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Concessionary companies in the Northwest Basin areas </div></div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On December&#160;1, 2014, YPF was notified of the complaint and moved for the suspension of procedural deadlines due to notification defects, which motion was granted by the Court. On April&#160;19, 2017, YPF was notified of the Court order resuming procedural deadlines and timely filed a challenge for legal defect, together with other the co-defendants. The court ordered those terms to answer the complaint be stayed until a final order is rendered on the defense based on a legal defect. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Concessionary companies in the Golfo San Jorge Basin areas </div></div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">YPF filed a legal defect exception. Based on such filing the court ordered the suspension of the terms to answer the complaint. The terms will continue to be suspended until a final decision is made and submitted by the Company, which will be resolved when notice of process has been served on, and the complaint has been answered by, all the defendant companies. On February&#160;8, 2021, the judge declared the incompetence of the federal justice in the case, understanding that the existence of an interjurisdictional damage to justify it had not been demonstrated. On March&#160;29, 2021, the Court of Appeals confirmed the first instance judgment. This decision has not been appealed by the plaintiff, and therefore is a final and conclusive judgment. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On May&#160;3, 2021, ASSUPA requested the Public Prosecutor&#8217;s Office to investigate the possible commission of criminal offences, and demanded that the Prosecution Unit for Investigations of Environmental Crimes (&#8220;UFIMA&#8221;, by its acronym in Spanish) be involved in the investigation to provide assistance in the matter of its jurisdiction, elaborating investigation strategies and/or defining courses of action for the investigation of the offenses claimed. Besides, it requested the referral of the case to the provincial courts for the continuation of the case, which generated the creation of a new case file. On September&#160;9, 2021, the judge declared his lack of jurisdiction given the absence of interjurisdictional damages. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On May&#160;14, 2021, the judge rejected ASSUPA&#8217;s request to refer the case to the provincial courts considering it inadmissible but informed that the proceedings would remain at the disposal of the judicial or administrative authorities at their request, as instrumental evidence. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Concessionary companies in the Austral Basin areas </div></div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On November&#160;2, 2015, YPF was notified of the claim and requested the suspension of procedural deadlines due to notification defects. This suspension was granted by the Court and following several incidents with different codefendants and parties summoned to appear, on June&#160;23, 2020, the judge ordered a new notification with the transfer of the case. The decision was appealed by the plaintiff. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On May 12, 2021, the case was submitted to the Federal Contentious Administrative Court of Appeals to decide on the plaintiff&#8217;s appeal on the interlocutory judgment dated June 23, 2020, in which the judge decided to sustain the claim filed by YPF, among other co-defendants, ordering the transfer of the case. On November 8, 2022, the Federal Contentious Administrative Court ratified the decision of the Lower Court the complaint to be served again. </div></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111996562_5" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111996562_6"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111996562_6" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111996562_7"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111996562_7" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111996562_8"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: .83em;margin-top : 1.67em;margin-bottom : 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation></div></div></div> <div><div><div style="line-height:normal;background-color:white;display: inline;"><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111996562_8" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111996562_9"><ix:exclude>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: ARIAL; font-size: 9pt; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">Dock Sud, R&#237;o Matanza, Riachuelo, Quilmes and Refiner&#237;a Luj&#225;n de Cuyo </div></div></div></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2006, a group of neighbors of Dock Sud, Province of Buenos Aires, sued 44 companies, including YPF, the Argentine Government, the Province of Buenos Aires, the City of Buenos Aires and 14 municipalities, before the CSJN, seeking remediation and indemnification for environmental collective damages to the Matanza and Riachuelo rivers. Additionally, another group of neighbors of the Dock Sud area, filed 2 additional environmental claims, one of which was desisted in relation to YPF, while the other claim seeks remediation and indemnification for collective environmental damages to the Dock Sud area and individual property damages allegedly suffered by several companies located in that area, including YPF, the Province of Buenos Aires and several municipalities. Currently, it is not possible to reasonably estimate the outcome of these complaints, nor is it possible to estimate the resulting associated legal fees and expenses. YPF has the right to be indemnified and held harmless by the Argentine Government for events and claims prior to January&#160;1, 1991, in accordance with YPF Privatization Law. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Through its judgment dated July&#160;8, 2008, the CSJN: </div><div style="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:2%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">-</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">Determined that the Authority of the Matanza Riachuelo Basin (&#8220;ACUMAR&#8221;) (Law No.&#160;26,168) should be in charge of executing the program for environmental remediation of the basin, being the Argentine Government, the Province of Buenos Aires and the City of Buenos Aires responsible for its performance; delegated to the Federal Lower Court of Quilmes the knowledge of all the matters concerning the execution of the remediation and sanitation; declared that all the litigations related to the execution of the remediation plan will be accumulated and be processed by this court and that this process produces lis pendens relating to the other collective actions seeking the environmental remediation of the basin, which should be archived. YPF was notified of certain resolutions issued by ACUMAR, whereby the Company was required to present an industrial reconversion plan in connection with certain YPF installations. Despite the appeal by the Company of the aforementioned resolutions, the plan was still presented. </div></td></tr></table>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">Decided that the proceedings to determine liabilities arising from past behaviors to repair the environmental damage will continue being heard by that Court. </div></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In addition to the comments included in Note 16.a.4) related to environmental claims in Quilmes, the Company has other judicial and non-judicial claims against it, based on similar arguments. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On the other hand, the monitoring works carried out routinely by YPF have allowed YPF to detect a certain degree of environmental impact on the subsoil within the vicinity of the Luj&#225;n de Cuyo refinery, which led to the implementation of a program for the survey, assessment and remediation of environmental damages, agreed by the Company with the enforcement agencies of the Province of Mendoza, which costs have been recognized in the &#8220;Provision for environmental liabilities&#8221; account of the &#8220;Provisions&#8221; line item in the statement of financial position. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Regarding the environmental damage to the aquifer surrounding the Luj&#225;n de Cuyo Refinery, a detailed research plan was conducted in order to define, analyze risks and implement mitigating actions. Thereafter, a remediation engineering plan was developed which is currently being implemented. Remediation follow-up is carried out under the supervision and with the assistance of Instituto Nacional del Agua (&#8220;INA&#8221;) and local authorities. </div><div style="margin-top: 8pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">33.b.2) Contentious claims </div></div><div style="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

Petersen filed its complaint on April&#160;8, 2015 and Eton Park filed its complaint on November&#160;3, 2016. Both complaints were filed before the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York (the &#8220;District Court&#8221;), and against the Republic of Argentina (the &#8220;Republic&#8221;) and YPF. The complaints make allegations related to the Republic&#8217;s intervention in YPF in 2012 and the Republic&#8217;s subsequent expropriation of a controlling interest in YPF held by Repsol (see Note 30). Petersen and Eton Park allege that the Republic and YPF breached purported obligations contained in the Company&#8217;s bylaws. The Petersen case and the Eton Park case were deemed to be related cases, are being conducted jointly and were assigned to the same District Court. </div></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111996562_10" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111996562_11"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111996562_11" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111996562_12"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111996562_12" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111996562_13"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: .83em;margin-top : 1.67em;margin-bottom : 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111996562_13" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111996562_14"><ix:exclude>

CONTINGENT ASSETS AND LIABILITIES (cont.)</ix:exclude> </div></div><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On September&#160;8, 2015, before Eton Park had filed its complaint, the Republic and YPF filed motions to dismiss Petersen&#8217;s claims. On October&#160;19, 2015 and October&#160;23, 2015, Petersen filed oppositions to the Republic&#8217;s and YPF&#8217;s motions to dismiss, respectively. On September&#160;9, 2016, the District Court issued a decision partially denying the motions to dismiss. The Company and the Republic appealed this decision, requesting a complete dismissal of the complaint. The Company and the Republic argued that the case should proceed in Argentina, if at all (forum non conveniens). The United States Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit (the &#8220;Court of Appeals&#8221;) held that the District Court had jurisdiction over this matter. On October&#160;31, 2018, the Company and the Republic appealed this decision to the United States Supreme Court (the &#8220;Supreme Court&#8221;). On June&#160;24, 2019, the Supreme Court declined to hear the appeal. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On August&#160;30, 2019, the Republic and YPF filed motions to dismiss both the Petersen and the Eton Park cases, once again arguing that the cases should proceed in Argentina (forum non conveniens). On June&#160;5, 2020, the District Court denied these motions to dismiss. The Republic and YPF filed their answers to the Petersen complaint on July&#160;8, 2019 and to the Eton Park complaint on July&#160;10, 2020. On July&#160;13, 2020, the District Court issued an order requiring the parties to proceed with fact and expert discovery. Given the overlap between the Petersen and Eton Park cases, they moved forward jointly and the parties proceeded with consolidated discovery in both cases. Fact discovery concluded on August&#160;27, 2021. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Expert discovery concluded on April&#160;6, 2022. On April&#160;14, 2022, Petersen and Eton Park (&#8220;Plaintiffs&#8221;) and YPF and the Republic (&#8220;Defendants&#8221;) filed opening briefs in support of cross-motions for summary judgment in the Petersen and Eton Park actions. Plaintiffs argued that the District Court should grant summary judgment in their favor on liability and damages as to both YPF and the Republic. In their opening briefs, YPF and the Republic each argued that it has no liability and owes no damages to Plaintiffs, and that the District Court should, therefore, grant summary judgment in its favor and dismiss all remaining claims against it. The parties filed opposition and reply briefs on May&#160;26, 2022 and June&#160;23, 2022, respectively. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On March&#160;30, 2023, the District Court granted YPF&#8217;s motion for summary judgment and denied Plaintiffs&#8217; motion for summary judgment as to YPF in its entirety. claims against YPF. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In line with the decision issued on March&#160;30, 2023, in the final judgment issued on September&#160;15, 2023 the District Court ordered, adjudged and decreed that all of Plaintiffs&#8217; <td style="vertical-align:bottom;text-align:center;">F - 85 </td>

<td style="vertical-align:top"><div style="font-size: 10pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">YPF SOCIEDAD ANONIMA</div></div></div></td>
<td style="vertical-align:bottom">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top"/></tr>
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid ; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:8pt">
<td colspan="5" style="vertical-align:top"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">NOTES TO THE CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</div></div><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 1pt; font-size: 8pt; font-family: ARIAL; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">AS OF DECEMBER 31, 2023, 2022 AND 2021</div></div></td></tr></table></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993494_3" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993494_4"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">35. MAIN REGULATIONS (cont.)</div></div> </div><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993494_4" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993494_5"><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The Hydrocarbons Law lays down the principles governing the exploration, exploitation, industrialization, transportation and commercialization of hydrocarbon resources in Argentina. The most relevant aspects of this Law are as follows: </div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:2%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">-</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">Liquid and gaseous hydrocarbon reservoirs located in Argentine territory and its continental shelf belong to the Argentine Government or the Provinces, depending on their territorial location. Activities related to hydrocarbon exploration, exploitation, industrialization, transportation and commercialization shall be undertaken by state-owned, private or mixed ownership companies, under the provisions of the Hydrocarbons Law and the regulations issued by the PEN. Besides, these companies shall be registered with the Registry of Oil Companies created under SE Resolution No.&#160;407/2007, under which a technical and financial analysis of those companies is conducted on an annual basis. Companies not so registered are not authorized to undertake activities in oilfields located in argentine territory. </div></td></tr></table><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:2%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">-</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">The terms for exploration permits are set at each call for bids by the enforcement authority, according to the exploration objective: (i)&#160;permit for conventional exploration concessions, the term is divided into 2 periods of up to <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:PermitOfConventionalExplorationTerm" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023_HydrocarbonDistributionMemberifrsfullTypesOfRateregulatedActivitiesAxis" format="ixt-sec:duryear" id="ixv-120646">3</ix:nonNumeric> years each, plus an optional extension of up to <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:PermitOfExtensionOfConventionalExplorationTerm" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023_HydrocarbonDistributionMemberifrsfullTypesOfRateregulatedActivitiesAxis" format="ixt-sec:duryear" id="ixv-120647">5</ix:nonNumeric> years; (ii)&#160;permit for unconventional exploration, the term is divided into 2 periods of up to <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:PermitOfUnconventionalExplorationTerm" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023_HydrocarbonDistributionMemberifrsfullTypesOfRateregulatedActivitiesAxis" format="ixt-sec:duryear" id="ixv-120648">4</ix:nonNumeric> years each, plus an optional extension of up to <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:PermitOfExtensionOfUnconventionalExplorationTerm" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023_HydrocarbonDistributionMemberifrsfullTypesOfRateregulatedActivitiesAxis" format="ixt-sec:duryear" id="ixv-120649">5</ix:nonNumeric> years; and (iii)&#160;permit for exploration in continental shelf and territorial waters, the term is divided into 2 periods of <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:PermitOfContinentalShelfAndTerritorialWatersExplorationTerm" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023_HydrocarbonDistributionMemberifrsfullTypesOfRateregulatedActivitiesAxis" format="ixt-sec:duryear" id="ixv-120650">3</ix:nonNumeric> years each, which may be extended for <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:PermitOfExtensionOfContinentalShelfAndTerritorialWatersExplorationTerm" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023_HydrocarbonDistributionMemberifrsfullTypesOfRateregulatedActivitiesAxis" format="ixt-sec:duryear" id="ixv-120651">1</ix:nonNumeric>&#160;year each. </div></td></tr></table><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:2%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">&#8201;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">The terms for exploitation concessions, which shall run from the date the concession is awarded under the respective regulation, shall be as follows: (i)&#160;conventional exploitation concession: <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:ConventionalExploitationConcessionTerm" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023_HydrocarbonDistributionMemberifrsfullTypesOfRateregulatedActivitiesAxis" format="ixt-sec:duryear" id="ixv-120652">25</ix:nonNumeric> years; (ii)&#160;unconventional exploitation concession: <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:UnconventionalExploitationConcessionTerm" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023_HydrocarbonDistributionMemberifrsfullTypesOfRateregulatedActivitiesAxis" format="ixt-sec:duryear" id="ixv-120653">35</ix:nonNumeric> years; and (iii)&#160;exploitation concession in continental shelf and territorial waters: <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:ContinentalShelfAndTerritorialWaterConcessionTerm" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023_HydrocarbonDistributionMemberifrsfullTypesOfRateregulatedActivitiesAxis" format="ixt-sec:duryear" id="ixv-120654">30</ix:nonNumeric> years. Besides, at least one year prior to the expiration of the concession, the holder of the exploitation concession may request an unlimited number of concession extensions, each for a term of <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:ConsentExpressionTerm" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" format="ixt-sec:duryear" id="ixv-120655">10</ix:nonNumeric> years. </div></td></tr></table><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:2%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">-</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">Holders of exploitation concessions may obtain a transportation concession to evacuate their production. Thus, the term of transportation concessions originating from a conventional exploitation concession will be <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:ConventionalExploitationConcessionTerm" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023_HydrocarbonDistributionMemberifrsfullTypesOfRateregulatedActivitiesAxis" format="ixt-sec:duryear" id="ixv-120656">25</ix:nonNumeric> years, and those originating from an unconventional exploitation concession <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:UnconventionalExploitationConcessionTerm" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023_HydrocarbonDistributionMemberifrsfullTypesOfRateregulatedActivitiesAxis" format="ixt-sec:duryear" id="ixv-120657">35</ix:nonNumeric> years, counted from the date of the concession award plus any extension of the terms which may be granted. </div></td></tr></table><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:2%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">&#8201;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">Since the issuance of Decree No.&#160;115/2019, the term of transportation concessions awarded through a bidding process will be <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:TransportationConcessionTerm" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023_HydrocarbonDistributionMemberifrsfullTypesOfRateregulatedActivitiesAxis_TopOfRangeMemberifrsfullRangeAxis" format="ixt-sec:duryear" id="ixv-120658">35</ix:nonNumeric> years from the date of award, which may be extended for an additional term of <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:TermOfExtensionOfTransportationConcession" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023_HydrocarbonDistributionMemberifrsfullTypesOfRateregulatedActivitiesAxis" format="ixt-sec:duryear" id="ixv-120659">10</ix:nonNumeric> years. Additionally, holders of transportation concessions granted from the effective date of such Decree and expansions of facility capacity in transportation concessions granted prior to such date and carried out thereafter, may ensure firm service capacity to shippers through capacity reservation contracts. These contracts may be freely negotiated regarding their allocation modality, prices and volumes. The uncontracted capacity and the unused contracted capacity shall be subject to the tariff to be approved by the enforcement authority. </div></td></tr></table><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:2%">&#160;</td>
<td style="width:3%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;">-</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">Holders of an exploration permit and exploitation concession shall pay: (i)&#160;annually in advance, a fee per each square kilometer or fraction, according to the scale specified by the PEN; and (ii)&#160;a percentage between <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PercentageOfAdvanceFee" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023_BottomOfRangeMemberifrsfullRangeAxis_HydrocarbonDistributionMemberifrsfullTypesOfRateregulatedActivitiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120660">12</ix:nonFraction>% and <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PercentageOfAdvanceFee" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023_HydrocarbonDistributionMemberifrsfullTypesOfRateregulatedActivitiesAxis_TopOfRangeMemberifrsfullRangeAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120661">18</ix:nonFraction>% of wellhead production of the liquid hydrocarbons extracted by way of royalty, allowing the national or provincial Executive Branch, as appropriate, and as grantors of such concessions, to reduce this rate to five percent (<ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PercentageReductionInTheConcessionFee" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023_HydrocarbonDistributionMemberifrsfullTypesOfRateregulatedActivitiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" sign="-" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120662">5</ix:nonFraction>%)&#160;considering the productivity, conditions and location of the wells. In addition, they are subject to federal, provincial and municipal taxes, customs duties on imports and exports, and, during the effective term of the exploration permit, to the tax regime established under the Hydrocarbons Law. </div></td></tr></table><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;">Default on the obligations arising under permits and concessions may cause the expiration of the terms, or the imposition of fines by the enforcement authority, as specified in the Hydrocarbons Law. </div></td></tr></table></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993494_5" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993494_6"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993494_6" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993494_7"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993494_7" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993494_8"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: .83em;margin-top : 1.67em;margin-bottom : 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993494_8" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993494_9"><ix:exclude>
