Under this Resolution the Company was awarded an annual volume of natural gas supply corresponding to the Neuquina basin of up to 965,000 m&#179;/d (Base Gas January) and a natural gas volume in the winter season of up to 3,250,000 m&#179;/d (Peak Gas 2024) under the Plan GasAr 2023-2028. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On September&#160;27, 2023, SE Resolution No.&#160;799/2023 was published, awarding the Company monthly volumes of natural gas supply to the Austral and Noroeste basins for the October 2023-December 2028 period under the Plan GasAr 2023-2028. </div><div style="margin-top: 8pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">35.d.2) Incentive programs for the domestic supply of LPG </div></div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">With the purpose of ensuring the supply of LPG to the domestic market at affordable prices ensuring LPG availability to lowest income users who have no access to the supply of natural gas through networks, the Argentine Government has implemented the following programs of relevance to the Company: </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Bottle-to Bottle Program </div></div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Concerning the bottled LPG segment, the LPG Law (see Note 35.c.4)) established the creation of a trust fund to finance the consumption of LPG in 10, 12, y 15-kg bottles for low income users having no access to natural gas distribution through networks, thereby granting the SE the power to establish benchmark prices. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In 2015, in the context mentioned above, the Bottle-to Bottle Program was created by Decree No.&#160;470/2015, subsequenty regulated through SE Resolution No.&#160;49/2015. The purpose fo this Program is to maintain price stability in the commercialization chain of butane and propane to be used in 10, 12 and 15 kg bottles and in certain supply areas. As provided for under Bottle-to Bottle Program regulations, at present the SE establishes, on an annual basis, the quotas of butane for the supply of the domestic market by producers, and the benchmark prices applicable on each ocassion to bottled LPG for residental use. Under the Bottle-to Bottle Program, producers would be paid a compensation, which was finally set at 0 from February&#160;1, 2019 by SGE Resolution No.&#160;15/2019. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Propane Network Agreement </div></div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In order to guarantee the stability of the conditions for the supply of undiluted propane through networks, on December&#160;27, 2002, the MINEM entered into an agreement with LPG producers for the supply of propane gas for distribution networks of undiluted propane gas effective until April&#160;30, 2003 and renewable for a maximum term of 1 year. Later, under Law No.&#160;26,019 of 2005, Law No.&#160;26,546 of 2009 and Decree No.&#160;496/2023, the agreement was authorized to be extended until December&#160;31, 2023. The 20th extension agreement of the Propane Network Agreement is still in force. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The agreement guarantees the supply of a given volume of gas to distributors and sub-distributors of propane gas through networks at a given price, against payment of an economic compensation to LPG producers for their lower revenues. </div><div style="margin-top: 8pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">35.d.3) Investment Promotion Regime for the Exploitation of Hydrocarbons - Decree No.&#160;929/2013 </div></div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Decree No.&#160;929/2013 provides for the creation of an Investment Promotion Regime for the Exploitation of Hydrocarbons (&#8220;Promotional Regime&#8221;), both for conventional and unconventional hydrocarbon exploitation projects. Inclusion in this Regime may be applied for by holders of hydrocarbon exploration permits and/or exploitation concessions and/or any third parties associated to such holders jointly with them, which have filed an investment project in foreign currency of at least <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:DirectInvestmentInForeignCurrency" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2023_InvestmentPromotionRegimeForTheExploitationOfHydrocarbonsDecreeNo9292013MemberYPFDecreeTypeAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120675">1,000</ix:nonFraction>, computed as of the date the project was filed, to be invested during the first 5 years of the project (this amount was modified by Law No.&#160;27,007 and reduced to <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:DirectInvestmentInForeignCurrencyAfterAmendment" contextRef="PAsOn12_31_2023_InvestmentPromotionRegimeForTheExploitationOfHydrocarbonsDecreeNo9292013MemberYPFDecreeTypeAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120676">250</ix:nonFraction>). </div></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993494_71" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993494_72"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The following are the main benefits established for subjects reached by this Regime: (i)&#160;they will be entitled, under the terms of Law No.&#160;17,319, and from the fifth successive year counted since the start-up of their respective projects, to freely sell to foreign markets <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PercentageOfSaleOnProductionOfLiquidAndGaseousHydrocarbons" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023_InvestmentPromotionRegimeForTheExploitationOfHydrocarbonsDecreeNo9292013MemberYPFDecreeTypeAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120677">20</ix:nonFraction>% of their production of liquid and gaseous hydrocarbons produced under the said projects, with a <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:ExportDutyForLiquidAndGaseousHydrocarbonsPercent" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023_InvestmentPromotionRegimeForTheExploitationOfHydrocarbonsDecreeNo9292013MemberYPFDecreeTypeAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120678">0</ix:nonFraction>% export duty, should these be applicable; (ii)&#160;they will be entitled to free availability of 100% of any foreign currency obtained from the export of the hydrocarbons mentioned in the preceding item; and (iii)&#160;for periods where national production fails to meet domestic supply needs under the terms of article 6 of Law No.&#160;17,319, subjects included in the Regime will be entitled to obtain, from fifth year following the approval and start-up of their respective projects - with respect to the percentage of liquid and gaseous hydrocarbons produced under such projects available for export as mentioned herein above - a price not lower that the reference export price, which will be determined without computing the incidence of export duties otherwise applicable. </div><div style="margin-top: 8pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">35.d.4) Incentive Programs for the Production of Conventional Hydrocarbons </div></div><div style="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">&#8226;</div></div></td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: ARIAL; font-size: 9pt; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">Provincial Stimulus Program - Province of Mendoza </div></div></div></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On December&#160;4, 2020, by Law No.&#160;9,279, the Province of Mendoza created the program known as &#8220;Mendoza Activates Hydrocarbons&#8221; (&#8220;Program I&#8221;), which seeks to promote the development, reactivation and increase of hydrocarbon activity. Program I will reimburse its beneficiaries, by means of tax credit certificates, any expenditures which, up to the authorizations limit specified in the regulation, are made in projects for the deployment of new wells, and/or the reactivation of existing ones, which as of the date of the Law was published, were inactive. These tax credit certificates may be used to pay the turnover tax and royalties. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On July&#160;7, 2021, by Law No.&#160;9,330, the Province of Mendoza created the program known as &#8220;Mendoza Activates Hydrocarbons II&#8221; (&#8220;Program II&#8221;) with the same purpose and modality as Program I, enlarging tax credit up to limit authorized under the regulations and extending the term for its use to December&#160;31, 2025, which may be extended for a term of <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:ExtendableTermOfPlan" contextRef="P07_07_2021To07_07_2021_ProvincialStimulusProgramProvinceOfMendozaMemberifrsfullGeographicalAreasAxis" format="ixt-sec:duryear" id="ixv-120679">3</ix:nonNumeric> years. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On December&#160;31, 2021, by Law No.&#160;9,364, the Province of Mendoza created the program known as &#8220;Mendoza Activates Hydrocarbons III&#8221; (&#8220;Program III&#8221;) with the same purpose and modality as Programs I and II, enlarging tax credit up to limit authorized under the regulations and extending the term for its use to December&#160;31, 2026, which may be extended for a term of <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:ExtendableTermOfPlan" contextRef="P01_01_2021To12_31_2021_ProvincialStimulusProgramProvinceOfMendozaMemberifrsfullGeographicalAreasAxis" format="ixt-sec:duryear" id="ixv-120680">3</ix:nonNumeric> years. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As of the date of issuance of these consolidated financial statements, the proposals for Program I, which involve projects in Barrancas, Vizcacheras and Loma Alta Sur areas, and for Program II, which involve projects in Barrancas and Desfiladero Bayo areas, were approved. </div><div style="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>
<table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="BORDER-COLLAPSE:COLLAPSE; font-family:ARIAL; font-size:9pt;border:0;width:100%">
<tr style="page-break-inside:avoid">
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">&#8226;</div></div></td>
<td style="width:1%;vertical-align:top">&#160;</td>
<td style="vertical-align:top;text-align:left;"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-family: ARIAL; font-size: 9pt; text-align: justify; line-height: normal;"><div style="letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">Provincial Stimulus Program - Province of Neuqu&#233;n </div></div></div></td></tr></table><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">By Decree No.&#160;913/2021, the Province of Neuqu&#233;n ordered the creation of the &#8220;Provincial Hydrocarbon Reactivation Program&#8221; for the promotion of investment and the increase in conventional hydrocarbon production. The program contemplates a financial incentive for investments through the granting of tax benefits, by obtaining a non-transferrable tax credit certificate for up to 50% of the amount of the approved investment, which may be used until December&#160;31, 2026 for the payment of the turnover tax, once the investments made have been certified. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Decree No.&#160;424/2023 provided continuity to the Program created by Decree No.&#160;913/2021, enabling the submission of new investment plans with tax credit that may be used until December&#160;31, 2028. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Under the Provincial Hydrocarbon Reactivation Program, YPF has executed agreements with the Province of Neuqu&#233;n to obtain the benefits of this Program, which involve projects in the Oct&#243;gono Fiscal, Al Norte de La Dorsal, Loma La Lata - Sierra Barrosa, Se&#241;al Cerro Bayo and Volc&#225;n Auca Mahuida areas. </div></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993494_77" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993494_78"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">35.e.1) Income tax </div></div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Law No.&#160;27,468, published in the BO on December&#160;4, 2018, established that the inflation adjustment procedure for taxation purposes will be applicable for fiscal years beginning January&#160;1, 2018. In the first, second and third fiscal years since it became effective, this procedure shall be applicable if the variation in the CPI, estimated from the beginning to the end of each of those years exceeds <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PercentageRateVariationInTheCPI" contextRef="P01_01_2018To12_31_2018" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120687">55</ix:nonFraction>%, <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PercentageRateVariationInTheCPI" contextRef="P01_01_2019To12_31_2019" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120688">30</ix:nonFraction>% and <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PercentageRateVariationInTheCPI" contextRef="P01_01_2020To12_31_2020" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120689">15</ix:nonFraction>%, for the first, second and third year of application, respectively. From the fourth year, i.e., fiscal year beginning on January&#160;1, 2021, the procedure will apply to the extent the CPI variation accumulated over 36 months prior to the applicable fiscal year end exceeds 100%. Considering that the CPI as of December&#160;31, 2023, 2022 and 2021 exceeds the mentioned parameters, the Group applied the tax adjustment for inflation in its income tax estimate. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On June&#160;16, 2021 Law No.&#160;27,630 was published in the BO, introducing the following amendments to the Income Tax Law: </div><div style="font-size:8pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

MAIN REGULATIONS (cont.)</div></div> </div><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993494_87" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993494_88"><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On July&#160;21, 2023, AFIP General Resolution No.&#160;5,391/2023 was published in the BO, establishing a one-time extraordinary pre-payment on account of the income tax for taxpayers which, in their tax returns for fiscal year 2022 or 2023, as appropriate, meet the following conditions: (i)&#160;have reported a taxable income, without applying tax loss carryforwards, of at least <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:TaxableIncomeMinimumExcludingTaxLossesCarryForwards" contextRef="P07_21_2023To07_21_2023_TwoThousandAndTwentyTwoAndTwoThousandAndTwentyThreeMemberYPFPeriodAxis" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120698">600</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million pesos; and (ii)&#160;have not determined any income tax. This extraordinary pre-payment will be estimated by applying <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PercentageOfPrepaymentsOfTaxArrivedWithoutConsideringTheTaxLosses" contextRef="P07_21_2023To07_21_2023_TwoThousandAndTwentyTwoAndTwoThousandAndTwentyThreeMemberYPFPeriodAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120699">15</ix:nonFraction>% on the taxable income of the fiscal year immediately preceding that in which the pre-payment is to be recorded, without considering tax loss carryforwards. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Budget Law 2023 - Deferral of tax adjustment for inflation </div></div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On December&#160;1, 2022, Law No.&#160;27,701 was published in the BO, which introduced changes to the Income Tax Law, establishing the possibility of deferring the tax adjustment for inflation contemplated under such Law corresponding to the first and second fiscal years beginning in January 2022, allowing to record, at taxpayer&#8217;s choice, one third of the adjustment in such fiscal year and the remaining two thirds in equal parts in the over the immediately following two periods. This benefit will only be admissible for subjects whose investment in the purchase, construction, manufacturing or final import of fixed assets, except automobiles, in each of the 2 fiscal periods immediately following the calculation of the respective first third, is equal or higher than <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:MinimumInvestmentForDeferralOfTaxAdjustmentForInflation" contextRef="P12_01_2022To12_01_2022_ChangesInTaxRatesOrTaxLawsEnactedOrAnnouncedMemberifrsfullNonadjustingEventsAfterReportingPeriodAxis" unitRef="Unit_ARS" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120700">30,000</ix:nonFraction>&#160;million pesos. </div><div style="margin-top: 8pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">35.e.2) Personal assets tax - Substitute taxpayer </div></div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Individuals and foreign entities, and undivided estates, regardless of whether they are domiciled or located in Argentina or abroad, are subject to a personal assets tax of <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PersonalAssetsTaxRate" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="4" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120701"><ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PersonalAssetsTaxRate" contextRef="P01_01_2021To12_31_2021" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="4" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120702"><ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PersonalAssetsTaxRate" contextRef="P01_01_2022To12_31_2022" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="4" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120703">0.50</ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction></ix:nonFraction>% of the value of any shares or ADS issued by Argentine entities. The tax is levied on the Argentine issuers of such shares or ADS, such as YPF, which must pay this tax as substitutes for the respective shareholders, and is based on the equity value (following the equity method), or the book value of the shares derived from the last financial statements as of December&#160;31 of each year. Under the Personal Assets Tax Law, the Group is entitled to seek reimbursement of the tax paid by the shareholders subject to such tax, using the reimbursement method the Group considers appropriate. </div><div style="margin-top: 8pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">35.e.3) Fuels tax </div></div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">From the existence of market prices for petroleum products following the deregulation of the hydrocarbon sector, Law No.&#160;23,966 established a tax on liquid fuel transfers, which levied certain types of fuels, replacing the former regime based o regulated prices. Since August 2003, the calculation method originally consisting of a fixed value per liter according to the respective type of fuel was replaced by a rate on the average sales price. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Later, under the Tax Reform, the new mechanism was modified reestablishing the fixed amounts per liter, which are adjusted quarterly based on variations in the CPI. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Incentive Regime for the Internal Supply of Fuels (&#8220;RIAIC&#8221;, by its acronym in Spanish) </div></div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On June&#160;16, 2022, Decree No.&#160;329/2022 was published in the BO, creating a promotion regime that allows refining and/or integrated refining companies to receive an amount equal to the sum they have to pay as tax on Liquid Fuels and Carbon Dioxide (&#8220;Tax on fuels&#8221;) for diesel imports, which may be applied to pay such tax. The RIAIC will be applicable to diesel imports and crude oil transfers from June&#160;16 to August&#160;16, 2022, that meet certain requirements established in said Decree and its corresponding regulation. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On February&#160;22, 2023, Decree No.&#160;86/2023 was published in the BO through which the RIAIC is reestablished, recognizing an amount equivalent to the amount that refining companies and/or integrated refiners must pay as fuel tax for imports of diesel and gasoline made between January&#160;1 and February&#160;28, 2023, which may be applied to the amount to be paid for such tax up to a limit of <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:ApplicableTaxRate" contextRef="P02_22_2023To02_22_2023_ChangesInTaxRatesOrTaxLawsEnactedOrAnnouncedMemberifrsfullNonadjustingEventsAfterReportingPeriodAxis_ImportedDieselMemberifrsfullProductsAndServicesAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120704">20</ix:nonFraction>% and <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:ApplicableTaxRate" contextRef="P02_22_2023To02_22_2023_ChangesInTaxRatesOrTaxLawsEnactedOrAnnouncedMemberifrsfullNonadjustingEventsAfterReportingPeriodAxis_ImportedGasolineMemberifrsfullProductsAndServicesAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120705">17</ix:nonFraction>% of the sales in the domestic market of imported diesel and gasoline, respectively, that meet certain requirements established in said Decree and its corresponding regulation. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On July&#160;10, 2023, SE Resolution No.&#160;570/2023 was published in the BO, extending the effective term of the RIAIC established through Decree No.&#160;86/2023 for all import operations of diesel and gasoline carried out from March&#160;1, 2023 to April&#160;30, 2023, that meet certain requirements established in said Decree and its corresponding regulation. </div></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993494_88" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993494_89"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; MAIN REGULATIONS (cont.)</div></div> </div><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993494_93" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993494_94"><div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On September&#160;7, 2023, Decree No.&#160;461/2023 was published in the BO, which reestablished the RIAIC for all import operations of diesel and gasoline carried out from August&#160;1, 2023 to October&#160;31, 2023 that meet certain requirements. On November&#160;23, 2023, SE Resolution No.&#160;952/2023 was published in the BO, which extended the effective term of the provisions of Decree No.&#160;461/2023 for import operations of diesel and/or gasoline carried out until November&#160;30, 2023. </div><div style="margin-top: 8pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">35.e.4) Regime for the regularization of taxes </div></div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On August&#160;26, 2020, Law No.&#160;27,562 (the &#8220;Law on Social Solidarity and Production Reactivation within the Public Emergency Framework&#8221;) was published in the BO, which declared the extension of the regularization of tax, social security and customs obligations originally established for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) under Law No.&#160;27,541. In the case of legal entities owning financial assets abroad, they should previously comply with the requirement to repatriate at least <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PercentageRepatriationOfAssetsLegalCompliance" contextRef="P08_26_2020To08_26_2020" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120706">30</ix:nonFraction>% of those assets within 60 days from the date they adhered to the regime (including shareholders holding at least <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PercentageRepatriationOfAssetsLegalCompliance" contextRef="P08_26_2020To08_26_2020" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120707">30</ix:nonFraction>% of the capital stock). </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The regime allowed to include obligations past due as of July&#160;31, 2020 and established a cash discount or plans from <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:PaymentInPlansInstalmentsDescription" contextRef="P07_31_2020To07_31_2020" id="ixv-120708">48 to 120 installments</ix:nonNumeric>, depending on the type of debt and taxpayer, subject to a <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:BorrowingsInterestRate" contextRef="PAsOn07_31_2020_FixedInterestRateMemberifrsfullTypesOfInterestRatesAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120709">2</ix:nonFraction>% fixed monthly interest rate in the first 6 installments and BADLAR rate in pesos at private banks from the seventh installment. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Adherence to the plan, which originally expired on October&#160;31, 2020, was successively extended until December&#160;15, 2020 by Decree No.&#160;966/2020. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On November&#160;11, 2021, Law No.&#160;27,653 &#8220;Tax Relief Law to Strengthen the Recovery of Economic and Social Activities Affected by the COVID-19 Pandemic&#8221; was published in the BO, which (i)&#160;it extended the moratorium granted under Law No.&#160;27,541 as amended by Law No.&#160;27,562, extending its deadlines and further covering obligations past due as of August, 31, 2021, included; (ii)&#160;with exclusive effect for the regularization of outstanding amounts detected by AFIP&#8217;s audit activity, interest in excess of <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PercentageInterestInExcessOfPrincipalOutstandingAmount" contextRef="P11_11_2021To11_11_2021" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120710">40</ix:nonFraction>% of the principal outstanding amount were written off and payment in plans of up to <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:PaymentInPlansInstalmentsDescription" contextRef="P11_11_2021To11_11_2021" id="ixv-120711">72 installments</ix:nonNumeric> was authorized, and (iii)&#160;removed the restrictions on dividend distribution prior to August&#160;26, 2022, unless the Company shall have pre-cancelled such tax debt, established under Law No.&#160;27,541. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In addition, AFIP General Resolution No.&#160;5,157/2022, published in the BO on February&#160;25, 2022, established that term for adherence to the regularization regime mentioned above was until March&#160;31, 2022, included, term which was extended to April&#160;29, 2022 by AFIP General Resolution No.&#160;5,181/2022 published in the BO on April&#160;1, 2022. </div><div style="margin-top: 8pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">35.e.5) Tax for an Inclusive and Solidary Argentina (&#8220;PAIS Tax&#8221;, by its acronym in Spanish) </div></div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On July&#160;24, 2023, Decree No.&#160;377/2023 was published in the BO, through which the scope of the PAIS Tax established by Law No.&#160;27,541/2019 to import operations of certain goods and services when access to the Exchange Market is required for their acquisition and payment. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The rates applied to foreign currency purchases are: (i)&#160;<ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PercentageOfTaxRateOnServicesAcquiredAbroad" contextRef="P07_24_2023To07_24_2023_TaxRateForAnInclusiveAndSolidaryArgentinaMemberYPFSchemeAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120712">25</ix:nonFraction>% for the acquisition of certain services abroad or provided in the country by non-residents; (ii)&#160;<ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PercentageOfTaxRateOnContractingServicesAndFreightServices" contextRef="P07_24_2023To07_24_2023_TaxRateForAnInclusiveAndSolidaryArgentinaMemberYPFSchemeAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="3" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120713">7.5</ix:nonFraction>% for contracting, abroad or in the country by non-residents, freight services and other transport services for the import or export of goods; and (iii)&#160;<ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PercentageTaxRateForImportOfGoods" contextRef="P07_24_2023To07_24_2023_TaxRateForAnInclusiveAndSolidaryArgentinaMemberYPFSchemeAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="3" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120714">7.5</ix:nonFraction>% for the import of goods, except for those mentioned in section 2 paragraph e) of Decree No.&#160;377/2023 and its corresponding regulations. On December&#160;13, 2023, Decree No.&#160;29/2023 was published in the BO, which increased the rates mentioned in items (ii)&#160;and (iii)&#160;to <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PercentageOfTaxRateOnGoodsAndServicesAfterRevision" contextRef="P12_13_2023To12_13_2023_TaxRateForAnInclusiveAndSolidaryArgentinaMemberYPFSchemeAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="3" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120715">17.5</ix:nonFraction>%. </div><div style="margin-top: 8pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">35.e.6) Tax benefits for price agreements </div></div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On August&#160;26, 2023, Decree No.&#160;433/2023 was published in the BO, which established tax benefits effective until October&#160;31, 2023, for entities entering into price agreements for the domestic market with the Secretariat of Commerce of the Ministry of Economy, or adjusting existing ones. These tax benefits include the suspension of the payment of the PAIS Tax for certain goods, the reduction to <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PercentageOfExportDutyAfterReduction" contextRef="P08_26_2023To08_26_2023_TaxBenefitsForPriceAgreementsMemberYPFSchemeAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120716">0</ix:nonFraction>% of the rate of export duties for certain tariff headings, facility plans for the payment of export duties by certain productive sectors and the extension of the payment term of certain taxes and social security obligations. On October&#160;26, 2023, by Decree No.&#160;551/2023, these tax benefits were extended until December&#160;31, 2023. </div></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993494_94" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993494_95"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993494_95" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993494_96"><ix:exclude><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993494_96" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993494_97"><ix:exclude><div style="font-size: .83em;margin-top : 1.67em;margin-bottom : 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation></div></div></div> <div><div><div style="line-height:normal;background-color:white;display: inline;"><div style="text-align:center"><div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993494_97" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993494_98"><ix:exclude>

MAIN REGULATIONS (cont.)</div></div> </div><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993494_99" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993494_100"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">35.f) Customs regulations </div></div><div style="margin-top: 8pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">35.f.1) Export duties </div></div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Export duties, taxes and other charges related to transactions carried out under the &#8220;Export Increase Program&#8221; and associated with Decree No.&#160;492/2023, Decree No.&#160;549/2023, Decree No.&#160;597/2023 and Decree No.&#160;28/2023 shall be paid using as tax base the amount resulting from the foreign currencies received and settled in accordance with such Decrees and their supplementary regulations (see Note 35.g)). </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Hydrocarbons </div></div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Since September 2018, hydrocarbon export duties which had previously been effective since 2000 and were suspended in January 2017, were reestablished. Mechanisms varied from setting a fixed amount to establishing rates on the taxable value or FOB value. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On May&#160;19, 2020, Decree No.&#160;488/2020 was published in the BO, establishing a floating rate for hydrocarbon export duties ranging from <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:FloatingRateForHydrocarbonExportDuties" contextRef="PAsOn05_19_2020_BottomOfRangeMemberifrsfullRangeAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120717">0</ix:nonFraction>% (where the Brent crude price is equal to or below <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:BrentCrudePrice" contextRef="PAsOn05_19_2020_BottomOfRangeMemberifrsfullRangeAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD_bbl" decimals="0" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120718">45</ix:nonFraction> US$/bbl) to <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:FloatingRateForHydrocarbonExportDuties" contextRef="PAsOn05_19_2020_TopOfRangeMemberifrsfullRangeAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120719">8</ix:nonFraction>% (where the Brent crude price is equal to or above <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:BrentCrudePrice" contextRef="PAsOn05_19_2020_TopOfRangeMemberifrsfullRangeAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD_bbl" decimals="0" scale="0" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120720">60</ix:nonFraction> US$/bbl). It was effective until December 2021. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On December&#160;31, 2020, Decree No.&#160;1,060/2020 was published in the BO effective until December&#160;31, 2022, establishing a <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:ExportDutyPercentage" contextRef="P01_01_2020To12_31_2020_ExportDutyRateMemberifrsfullTypesOfRateregulatedActivitiesAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="3" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120721">4.5</ix:nonFraction>% export duty rate on goods included in Chapter 29 of the MERCOSUR Common Nomenclature (&#8220;NCM&#8221;), in which ethanol and methanol, among others, are included. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Agricultural products </div></div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On March&#160;4, 2020, Decree No.&#160;230/2020 was published in the BO, which established a <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PercentageOfIncreaseInExportDuty" contextRef="P03_04_2020To03_04_2020_AgriculturalProductsMemberifrsfullProductsAndServicesAxis_TopOfRangeMemberifrsfullRangeAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120722">33</ix:nonFraction>% tax (maximum tax rate allowed under Law No.&#160;27,541), on the export of soybean and soybean byproducts. Tax rate on export of wheat, corn and sorghum remained at <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:ExportDutyPercentage" contextRef="P03_04_2020To03_04_2020_WheatCornAndSorghumMemberifrsfullProductsAndServicesAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120723">12</ix:nonFraction>%. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On October&#160;5, 2020, Decree No.&#160;790/2020 was published in the BO, by which the export duties on soybean and soybean byproducts, such as soybean oil and soybean meal, are fixed at <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:ExportTaxRate" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023_SoybeanMemberifrsfullProductsAndServicesAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120724">33</ix:nonFraction>% and <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:ExportTaxRate" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023_SoybeanByproductsMemberifrsfullProductsAndServicesAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120725">31</ix:nonFraction>%, respectively, from January 2021. From March 2022, all export duties for the products mentioned above were set in <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:ExportTaxRate" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023_SoybeanMemberifrsfullProductsAndServicesAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120726">33</ix:nonFraction>%. As of January 2023, the export duties established by Decree No.&#160;790/2020 were restored. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Import licenses </div></div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On July&#160;5, 2017, the Ministry of Productive Development published Resolution No. E 523/2017, establishing an automatic and non-automatic import licensing regime for goods classified under all NCM tariff headings and intended for definitive entry for consumption. Besides, it determined that NCM tariff headings listed in Annexes II to XIV of the said resolution are subject to non-automatic import licensing. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On March&#160;10, 2021, by Resolution No.&#160;5/2021 issued by the Undersecretariat of Trade Policy and Management, Annex XII was amended, whereby several goods, including diesel, are now subject to the automatic import licensing system. </div><div style="margin-top: 8pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">35.f.2) Customs collections </div></div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On March&#160;29, 2023 AFIP General Resolution No.&#160;5,339/2023 was published in the BO, suspending, until December&#160;31, 2023, the application of exclusion certificates from the income tax and VAT collection regimes for final imports of goods. </div><div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In addition, in order to calculate income tax prepayments, collections as a result of the said suspension may no longer be computed, and in certain cases, computing VAT collections is temporarily restricted. </div></ix:continuation></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993494_100" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993494_101"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top:1em; In both cases, these tariff headings are determined by the SE and provided the imports are made by taxpayers indicated by the Secretariat to such end. On November&#160;1, 2023, by AFIP General Resolution No.&#160;5,441/2023, the effective term of these provisions was extended until November&#160;30, 2023. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On December&#160;29, 2023, by AFIP General Resolution No.&#160;5,476/2023, the provisions of AFIP General Resolution No.&#160;5,339/2023 were extended until June&#160;30, 2024, eliminating the temporary restrictions for computing VAT collections. </div><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">35.g) Regulations related to the Foreign Exchange Market </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">With the aim of regulating access to the Foreign Exchange Market for payments of imports of goods and services, payments of principal and interest of foreign financial debts and payment of profits and dividends, among other things, the BCRA established the following requirements: </div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

In order to obtain the benefits under these regimes, companies must: (i)&#160;be registered with the Register of Oil Companies and be holders of hydrocarbon exploitation concessions; (ii)&#160;adhere to these regimes under the terms established by the SE; (iii)&#160;obtain an incremental production under the terms defined in the Decree; and (iv)&#160;comply with the Regime for Promotion of Employment, Work and Development of Regional and National Providers of the Hydrocarbon Industry. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Beneficiaries of RADPIP and RADPIGN regimes will have, for a percentage of the incremental production in accordance with (iii)&#160;above, access to foreign exchange currencies on the Exchange Market for the payment of principal and interest on foreign trade and financial liabilities, including liabilities with non-resident related companies and/or profits and dividends. Such access to the Exchange Market will not be subject to prior approval by the BCRA. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On the other hand, through Communications &#8220;A&#8221; 7,788 and &#8220;A&#8221; 7,803 the BCRA established the possibility for entities in the energy sector and beneficiaries of Decree No.&#160;277/2022 to subscribe bills in U.S. dollars payable in pesos at zero rate (&#8220;LEDIV&#8221;, by its acronym in Spanish) simultaneously with the financing of imports, pre-financing of exports and/or foreign currency settlements. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Export Increase Program </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In relation to settlements through the Foreign Exchange Market of funds received from abroad, the BCRA established the following regulations: </div><div style="font-size:6pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&#160;</div>

MAIN REGULATIONS (cont.) </div></div><div style="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&#160;</div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993494_117"><div style="margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">35.h) Decree of Necessity and Urgency (&#8220;DNU&#8221; by its acronym in Spanish) No.&#160;70/2023 </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">On December&#160;21, 2023, Decree No.&#160;70/2023 was published in the BO, declaring the state of public emergency in economic, financial, fiscal, administrative, pension, tariff, health, and social matters until December&#160;31, 2025. This decree repeals, introduces, and/or amends certain laws. The main measures established include the following: (I)&#160;reforming the structures of existing subsidies in order to ensure that final users have access to basic and essential electricity and natural gas consumption; (ii)&#160;calculating the cost of basic consumption based on the tariffs of each supply point; (iii)&#160;defining mechanisms related to the allocation of subsidies and their collection by users; (iv)&#160;amending the LGS and Law No.&#160;23,696 (&#8220;State Reform Law&#8221;) to establish that no prerogatives or advantages of public law will be granted to companies in which the National Government is a shareholder; (v)&#160;amending Law No.&#160;20,680 (&#8220;Supply Law&#8221;) which granted the Ministry of Economy&#8217;s Secretariat of Commerce the power to impose regulations and sanctions related to the supply and distribution of goods; and (vi)&#160;repealing Decree No.&#160;1,060/2000 which set maximum deadlines to contracts for the exclusive supply of fuel signed between oil companies and gas stations and limited to <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:MaximumPercentageOfPermissibleInterestsInGasStations" contextRef="PAsOn12_21_2023_DecreeOfNecessityAndUrgencyDNUByItsAcronyminSpanishNo702023MemberYPFStatutoryActAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-120738">40</ix:nonFraction>% the interest of the former in the networks of gas stations commercializing the brands of their property. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Although the DNU No.&#160;70/2023 needs to be debated and ratified by at least one of the houses of the National Congress, its provisions are effective since December&#160;29, 2023, except for some provisions that have been subject to precautionary measures that suspended their validity. As of the date of issuance of these consolidated financial statements, it is not possible to anticipate the evolution of the modifications set out in such DNU nor the new measures that might be announced nor its impacts. </div><div style="margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; font-size: 9pt; font-family: ARIAL;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;">35.i) CNV Regulatory Framework </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Information requirements as Settlement and Clearing Agent and Trading Agent </div></div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">As of the date of issuance of these consolidated financial statements, the Company is registered in the CNV under the category &#8220;Settlement and Clearing Agent and Trading Agent - Direct Participant&#8221;, record No.&#160;549. Considering the Company&#8217;s business and the CNV Rules, the Company will not, under any circumstance, offer brokerage services to third parties for transactions in markets under the jurisdiction of the CNV, and it will also not open operating accounts to third parties to issue orders and trade in markets under the jurisdiction of the CNV. </div><div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">In accordance with the regulations to the CNV, the Company is subject to the provisions of Section 5 c), Chapter II, Title VII of the regulations to the CNV, &#8220;Settlement and Clearing Agent - Direct Participant&#8221;. In this respect, as set forth in Section 13, Title VII, Chapter II, of the CNV rules, as of December 31, 2023, the equity of the Company exceeds the minimum equity required by such Rules. </div></ix:continuation></div></div><div style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"></div><hr style="color:#999999;height:3px;width:100%"/><div style="font-size: .83em;margin-top : 1.67em;margin-bottom : 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div></div></div></div> <div> <div> <div style="line-height:normal;background-color:white;display: inline;"> <div style="text-align:center"> <div style="width:8.5in;text-align:left;margin-left: auto;margin-right: auto">

EMPLOYEE BENEFIT PLANS AND SIMILAR OBLIGATIONS </div></div> <div style="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Retirement plan </div></div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Effective March&#160;1, 1995, the Group has established a retirement plan, through which it makes contributions to a mutual fund for an amount equivalent to the amount contributed by each adhering member, between <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PercentageOfSalaryContributionToMutualFundRetirementPlan" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023_BottomOfRangeMemberifrsfullRangeAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-121028">3</ix:nonFraction>% and <ix:nonFraction name="ypf:PercentageOfSalaryContributionToMutualFundRetirementPlan" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023_TopOfRangeMemberifrsfullRangeAxis" unitRef="Unit_pure" decimals="2" scale="-2" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-121029">10</ix:nonFraction>% of their monthly compensation, and has no legal or constructive obligation to make additional contributions in the event that the mutual fund does not have sufficient assets to meet the benefits. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The plan members will receive from the Group the contributed funds before retirement only in the case of voluntary termination under certain circumstances, dismissal without cause or in case of death or incapacity. The Group has the right to discontinue this plan at any time, without incurring termination costs. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">The amount charged to expense related to the retirement plan was <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:EmployeeBenefitsExpense" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023_RetirementPlanMemberifrsfullDefinedBenefitPlansAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-121030">3</ix:nonFraction>, <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:EmployeeBenefitsExpense" contextRef="P01_01_2022To12_31_2022_RetirementPlanMemberifrsfullDefinedBenefitPlansAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-121031">4</ix:nonFraction> and <ix:nonFraction name="ifrs-full:EmployeeBenefitsExpense" contextRef="P01_01_2021To12_31_2021_RetirementPlanMemberifrsfullDefinedBenefitPlansAxis" unitRef="Unit_USD" decimals="-6" scale="6" format="ixt:num-dot-decimal" id="ixv-121032">3</ix:nonFraction> for the years ended December&#160;31, 2023, 2022 and 2021, respectively. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Objective performance bonus programs and performance evaluation programs</div> </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">These programs cover certain of the Group&#8217;s personnel and are paid in cash. These bonuses are based on compliance with corporate objectives, business unit objectives and individual performance. They are calculated considering the annual compensation of each employee, certain key factors related to the fulfillment of these objectives and the performance evaluation of each employee. </div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; EMPLOYEE BENEFIT PLANS AND SIMILAR OBLIGATIONS (cont.)</ix:exclude> </div></div> <div style="margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px; font-size: 8pt;">&#160;</div> <div style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Share-based benefit plans </div></div> <div style="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">From the fiscal year 2013 the Company has decided to implement a share-based benefit plan aimed at aligning the performance of certain executive-level employees, managers and key or critical technical knowledgeable personnel, with the objectives of the strategic plan of the Company. This plan, organized in annual programs, consists in giving participation, through shares of the Company, to each selected employee with the condition of remaining in it for the period defined in the plan (period of up to <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:RetirementPlanServicePeriod" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" format="ixt-sec:durwordsen" id="ixv-121037">3 years</ix:nonNumeric> from the grant date, hereinafter &#8220;service period&#8221;), being this the only necessary condition to access the agreed final retribution. </div> <div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Consistent with and with similar characteristics to share-based benefit plans approved in previous years, the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors: </div> <div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0px; margin-bottom: 0px;">&#160;</div>

The indicated matured fields consist of a total of 55 areas which are being segregated in 18 disposal groups. This disposal of assets is consistent with the Company&#8217;s new management plans, which considers that the rationalization of the conventional Upstream portfolio is one of the drivers on which the YPF&#8217;s strategy is based, with focus on activities and investments in unconventional fields. These groups of assets are expected to qualify for recognition as a completed disposal within 12 months since the decision of the YPF&#8217;s Board of Directors and as such, they met all the criteria to be classified as held for sale as of that date. Accordingly, the assets will be reclassified from &#8220;Property, plant and equipment&#8221; line item to &#8220;Assets held for sale&#8221; line item and the related provision for hydrocarbon wells abandonment obligations to &#8220;Provision for hydrocarbon wells abandonment obligations held for sale&#8221; line item as current items in the statement of financial position. The disposal of these groups of assets did not meet the IFRS 5 held for sale criteria as of December&#160;31, 2023, accordingly these disposal groups of assets were not classified as held for sale as of that date. </div> <div style="margin-top:8pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:9pt; font-family:ARIAL;text-align:justify">Considering the aforementioned YPF&#8217;s Board of Directors&#8217; decision, impairment indicators under IAS 36 has been evaluated for each group of assets (see Note 8). font-size: 9pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">S - 1 </div></div><div style="font-size: 8pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-size: 8pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">&#160;</div></div><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"></div></div> <ix:nonNumeric name="ifrs-full:DisclosureOfConsolidatedAndSeparateFinancialStatementsExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" escape="true" continuedAt="TextSelection_111993596" id="ixv-86461"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;text-indent: 0px;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">SUPPLEMENTAL INFORMATION ON OIL AND GAS PRODUCING ACTIVITIES (UNAUDITED) </div></div></div></div> <div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"> </div></div> <div style="text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 9pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">The following information is presented in accordance with Accounting Standards Codification (&#8220;ASC&#8221;) No.&#160;932 &#8220;Extractive Activities - Oil and Gas&#8221;, as amended by Accounting Standards Update (&#8220;ASU&#8221;) 2010 - 03 &#8220;Oil and Gas Reserves. Estimation and Disclosures&#8221;, issued by the Financial Accounting Standards Board (&#8220;FASB&#8221;) in January 2010. </div></div> <div style="text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 9pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Oil and gas reserves </div></div> <div style="text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 9pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Proved oil and gas reserves are those quantities of oil and gas which by analysis of geoscience and engineering data, can be estimated with reasonable certainty to be economically producible (from a given date forward, from known reservoirs, and under existing economic conditions, operating methods and government regulations) prior to the time at which contracts providing the right to operate expire, unless evidence indicates that renewal is reasonably certain, regardless of whether deterministic or probabilistic methods are used for the estimation. The project to extract the hydrocarbons must have commenced or the operator must be reasonably certain that it will commence the project within reasonable time. In some cases, substantial investments in new wells and related facilities may be required to recover proved reserves. </div></div> <div style="text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 9pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">Information on net proved reserves as of December&#160;31, 2023, 2022 and 2021 was calculated in accordance with the SEC rules and FASB ASC 932 rules. Accordingly, crude oil prices used to determine reserves were calculated for crude oils of different quality produced by the Company. Consequently, to calculate our net proved reserves as of December&#160;31, 2023, the Company considered, according to the SEC rules and FASB ASC 932 rules, the unweighted average realized price of crude oils for each month within the <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">12-month</div> period ended December&#160;31, 2023, which refers to the domestic crude oil prices adjusted by each different quality produced by the Company. </div> <div style="text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 9pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">Additionally, since there are no benchmark market natural gas prices available in Argentina, the Company considered the <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">12-month</div> period average ended December&#160;31, 2023 of domestic market realized prices according to the SEC rules and FASB ASC 932 rules, and the prices of contracts awarded to YPF under the Plan GasAr 2020-2024 and the Plan GasAr 2023-2028 for certain areas, which will be in effect until their corresponding termination dates. See Note 35.d.1) to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements. </div> <div style="text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 9pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Notwithstanding the foregoing, commodity prices have fluctuated significantly in recent years. </div></div> <div style="text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 9pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Net reserves are defined as that portion of the gross reserves attributable to the interest of YPF after deducting interests owned by third parties. In determining net reserves, the Group excludes from its reported reserves royalties due to others, whether payable in cash or in kind, where the royalty owner has a direct interest in the underlying production and is able to make lifting and sales arrangements independently. By contrast, to the extent that royalty payments required to be made to a third party, whether payable in cash or in kind, are a financial obligation, or are substantially equivalent to a production or severance tax, the related reserves are not excluded from the reported reserves despite the fact that such payments are referred to as royalties under local regulations. The same methodology is followed in reporting our production amounts. </div></div> <div style="text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 9pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Natural gas reserves exclude the gaseous equivalent of liquids expected to be removed from the gas on concessions and leases, at field facilities and at gas processing plants. These liquids are included in net proved reserves of NGLs. </div></div> <div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"></div> <div style="font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 9pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;text-indent: 0px;"><div style="display:inline;"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Technology used in establishing proved reserves additions in 2023 </div></div></div> <div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;"> </div> <div style="text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 9pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">YPF&#8217;s estimated proved reserves as of December&#160;31, 2023 are based on estimates generated through the integration of available and appropriate data, utilizing well-established technologies that have been demonstrated in the field to yield repeatable and consistent results. Data used in these integrated assessments include information obtained directly from the subsurface via wellbore, such as well logs, reservoir core samples, fluid samples, static and dynamic pressure information, production test data, and surveillance and performance information. The data utilized also include subsurface information obtained through indirect measurements, including high quality <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">2-D</div> and <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">3-D</div> seismic data, calibrated with available well control. Where applicable, geological outcrops information was also utilized. The tools used to interpret and integrate all this data included both proprietary and commercial software for reservoir modeling, simulation and data analysis. In some circumstances, where appropriate analog reservoir models are available, reservoir parameters from these analog models were used to increase the reliability of our reserves estimates. </div> </ix:nonNumeric></div></div><ix:continuation id="TextSelection_111993596" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993596_1"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top: 1em; <td style="width: 3%; vertical-align: top;text-align:justify;"> <div style="text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; line-height: normal;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">(1)</div></div> </td>
<td style="vertical-align: top;text-align:left;"> <div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; line-height: normal; text-align: left;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Mainly includes lawsuits, result from assignment of areas and financial accretion for the hydrocarbon wells abandonment obligations, among others. </div></div> </td> </tr> </table> </ix:nonNumeric><div style="margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 1em"><ix:continuation id="TextSelection_111992337"></ix:continuation></div> <div style="clear:both;max-height:0pt;"></div> <div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; margin-top: 12pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: left;"><div style="text-decoration: underline; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">Standardized measure of discounted future net cash flows </div></div> <div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt; text-align: justify;">The standardized measure is calculated as the excess of future cash inflows from proved reserves less future costs of producing and developing the reserves, future income taxes and a discount factor. Future cash inflows represent the revenues that would be received from production of <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">year-end</div> proved reserve quantities assuming the future production would be sold at the prices used for reserves estimates as of <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">year-end</div> (the &#8220;average price&#8221;). Accordingly, crude oil prices used to determine reserves were calculated each month, for crude oils of different quality produced by the Group. </div></ix:continuation> </div> </div> <ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993596_72" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993596_73"><ix:exclude><div style="margin-top: 1em; margin-bottom: 0em; page-break-before: always;"></div></ix:exclude></ix:continuation> <ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993596_73" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993596_74"><ix:exclude><hr style="width: 100%; height: 3px; color: rgb(153, 153, 153);"/></ix:exclude></ix:continuation><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993596_74" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993596_75"><ix:exclude> <div style="font-size: 13.28px; margin-top: 1.67em; margin-bottom: 1.67em;font-weight: bold;"><a href="#toc">Table of Contents</a></div> </ix:exclude></ix:continuation> <div style="text-align: center;"> <div style="width: 8.5in; text-align: left; margin-right: auto; margin-left: auto;"><ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993596_75" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993596_76"><ix:exclude> <div style="text-align: center; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 9pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">S - 16 </div></div> <div style="font-size: 8pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-size: 8pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">&#160;</div></div> <div style="text-align: justify; font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-weight:bold;display:inline;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">SUPPLEMENTAL INFORMATION ON OIL AND GAS PRODUCING ACTIVITIES (UNAUDITED) (cont.) </div></div></div> </ix:exclude></ix:continuation> <ix:continuation id="TextSelectionAppend_111993596_76" continuedAt="TextSelectionAppend_111993596_77"><div style="text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 9pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">The Company considered the unweighted average realized price of crude oils for each month within the <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">12-month</div> period ended December&#160;31, 2023, which refers to the domestic crude oil prices adjusted by each different quality produced by the Company. </div> <div style="text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 9pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">Additionally, since there are no benchmark market natural gas prices available in Argentina, the Company considered the <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">12-month</div> period average ended December&#160;31, 2023 of domestic market realized prices according to the SEC rules and FASB ASC 932 rules, and the prices of contracts awarded to YPF under the Plan GasAr 2020-2024 and the Plan GasAr 2023-2028 for certain areas, which will be in effect until their corresponding termination dates. See Note 35.d.1) to the Audited Consolidated Financial Statements. </div> <div style="text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 9pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;">Future production costs include the estimated expenditures related to production of the proved reserves, plus any production taxes without consideration of future inflation. Future development costs include the estimated costs of drilling development wells and installation of production facilities, plus the net costs associated with dismantling and abandonment of wells, assuming <div style="white-space: nowrap; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">year-end</div> costs continue without consideration of future inflation. Future income taxes were determined by applying statutory rates to future cash inflows less future production costs and less tax depreciation of the properties involved. The present value was determined by applying a discount rate of 10% per year to the annual future net cash flows. </div> <ix:nonNumeric name="ypf:DisclosureOfDiscountedFutureNetCashFlowFromOilAndGasExplanatory" contextRef="P01_01_2023To12_31_2023" escape="true" id="ixv-99966"> <div style="text-align: justify; font-family: Times New Roman; font-size: 9pt; margin-top: 6pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-family: &quot;Times New Roman&quot;; font-size: 9pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">The standardized measure does not purport to be an estimate of the fair market value of the Group&#8217;s proved reserves. An estimate of fair value would also take into account, among other things, the expected recovery of reserves in excess of proved reserves, anticipated changes in future prices and costs and a discount factor representative of the time value of money and the risks inherent in producing oil and gas. </div></div> <div style="font-size: 6pt; margin-top: 0pt; margin-bottom: 0pt;"><div style="font-size: 6pt; letter-spacing: 0px; top: 0px;display:inline;">&#160;</div></div>
